entries.title: The .dark [data-skin="midnight"] selector never matches on the <html> path
entries.detail: A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself. app/layout.tsx stamps data-skin on documentElement (the global skin preview path, including marketing); only the shell root is a descendant. So midnight-dark renders a MIXTURE: the generic .dark palette with midnight's light-mode overrides under it. The comment at app/layout.tsx:142-143 asserts the opposite, which is why it survived. One selector, but it repaints every midnight-dark surface, so it wants its own pass with a baseline recapture.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='lib/theme/skins.ts',C='app/globals.css';if(!fs.existsSync(S)||!fs.existsSync(C))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const ids=[...new Set([...src.matchAll(/\bid:\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/g)].map(m=>m[1]))];const def=(src.match(/DEFAULT_SKIN[^=]*=\s*\x27([a-z0-9-]+)\x27/)||[])[1];if(!def||ids.length<2)process.exit(79);const css=fs.readFileSync(C,'utf8').replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'');const bad=[];for(const id of ids){if(id===def)continue;if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no compound .dark[data-skin] selector; the <html> preview path paints the generic .dark palette');if(!new RegExp('\\\\.dark\\\\s+\\\\[data-skin=\\\\x22'+id+'\\\\x22\\\\]').test(css))bad.push(id+': no descendant .dark [data-skin] selector; the authed-shell path loses its dark block');}if(bad.length){console.error(bad.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. Non-vacuity proven by the parent, not taken on report: reverting to the descendant-only selector fails skin-dom-selectors.test.ts with 'A descendant combinator cannot match an element against itself'. The second half matters more than the row did — authoring the selector LIST would have silently dropped the block from check-contrast's resolver, which scored the raw prelude and returned null for any comma-separated selector, so the contrast gate would have kept printing green for midnight-dark while measuring nothing there (ADR-970). Fixed in the same pass; selectorWeight now scores each part of a list independently.

entries.title: The app shell statically imports the entire admin module registry
entries.detail: settings-panel.tsx imports MODULE_COMPONENTS from components/admin/modules/module-map — a 'use client' pure registry with 38 static imports and no hooks, handlers or browser APIs. It reaches crypto-browserify/stream-browserify: 406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip on EVERY authed page, verified as a blocking script tag in served HTML. Fix: next/dynamic per module, import module IDS not components, and add import 'server-only' to lib/journey-plans and lib/practices so the class fails the build. NOTE: needs a route-level first-load measurement, which the agent container cannot produce (next build fails page-data collection without service-role creds).
entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-18 (ADR-1074). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN NUMBERS, both measured. (1) THE HEADLINE WAS STALE. '406 kB raw / 121 kB gzip reaching crypto-browserify on every authed page' was already spent by dc47b89 when the 42 catalog modules moved behind dynamic(); nobody re-measured afterwards. A paired A/B on one tree with only settings-panel.tsx differing puts the registry import itself at 9.3 KB raw / 2.0 KB gzip (955.8 -> 946.5 KB raw over entryJSFiles for app/(main)/layout). Real, and 40x smaller than the row claimed. A number quoted once and never re-derived is how a row keeps promising a win that was already banked. (2) THE crypto-browserify HALF WAS REAL, and it was NOT in module-map. It came through lib/journey-plans and lib/pillars, both of which SAID 'Server-only' in their headers and neither of which was: journey-settings.tsx imported normalizeJourneyMeeting and circle-builder.tsx imported PILLAR_SLUGS - a pure coercion function and an array of four strings - and each dragged createAdminClient, @supabase/supabase-js, lib/practices, lib/zaps, lib/achievements, lib/automations and crypto-browserify into the client graph. Both are extracted to dependency-free modules (lib/journeys/meeting.ts, lib/pillars/slugs.ts), re-exported from their old homes so no server caller changed, and the originals now carry a real `import 'server-only'`. Proved against a real client compile: next build reaches 'Compiled successfully in 3.7min', which a client module still reaching either file could not do. The rail keeps ONE synchronous fact - INLINE_MODULE_IDS, 38 strings with zero imports - because an id with no inline body draws nothing, and that feeds the section count that feeds hasContent. Verified the gate myself: re-adding the static import fails check-shell-weight.test.ts by name, twice.

entries.title: Sentry no longer ships to routes with no DSN configured
entries.detail: The static `import * as Sentry` is gone; the SDK is now reached through a dynamic import gated on process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN — the one env form the browser can resolve, since Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at build time. The server-only SENTRY_DSN fallback is deliberately NOT consulted here because it is never inlined into the browser bundle and could only read undefined. The hard part was the export contract: Next reads onRouterTransitionStart off this module's namespace and calls it on every client navigation, so it MUST stay defined with Sentry off — it is now a stable wrapper delegating to an async-loaded hook, with a .catch that leaves it a no-op if the chunk fails, because monitoring must never take down the app it monitors. Stated cost: a navigation in the first few ms of a configured session may go untraced. VERIFIED BEYOND THE ONE FILE (the searchSiteIcons lesson): every importer of lib/observability/sentry was enumerated — only sentry.server.config.ts and sentry.edge.config.ts import it statically, both server/edge runtimes, and lib/maps/diagnostics.ts deliberately reads the value without importing. No client component pulls it, so the SDK cannot re-enter the baseline chunk by a side door.
entries.notes: Artifact-verified 2026-08-17, not inferred: built with no DSN and read the emitted chunks. The 236,682-byte Sentry SDK chunk appears in 0 of 4,149 client entry lists across all 404 page_client-reference-manifest.js files, and the baseline chunk in rootMainFiles contains only the gated async loader. app/error, app/global-error and components/ui/route-error.tsx still import the SDK statically; Turbopack keeps those in async groups, so they are not a baseline regression and were deliberately left alone.

entries.title: revalidate = 3600 is dead on the four /discover detail routes
entries.detail: All four detail routes now declare generateStaticParams alongside their revalidate, so they enter the prerender manifest and ISR is live. Each reuses the redaction-safe reader the index and sitemap already use, bounded (200), and each carries a .catch(() => []) so a build without Supabase credentials degrades to on-demand rendering instead of failing — which matters because this repo's agent containers cannot complete page-data collection. dynamicParams defaults true, so newer rows still render on demand and join the set on revalidate. The three /discover INDEX pages were deliberately NOT touched: they are LIVE-012, blocked on an auth-navigation decision.

entries.title: Decide how /discover index pages resolve isAuthed without killing ISR

source.ref: ADR-1080; docs/FINALIZE-PLAN.md 10.9, 10.12; proxy.ts next= carry from #2132

entries.detail: CLOSED 2026-08-18, and the row's OWN BLOCKER had already dissolved. It read 'proxy.ts builds its redirect by rewriting the pathname and NEVER setting next=, so the destination is lost' and called for an owner decision between two options. #2132 (2026-08-13) had already taken option (a): proxy.ts sets ?next=<pathname+search> on its sign-in redirect and /sign-in re-validates it into the fq_post_login cookie that /auth/callback honours. Re-read before acting, which is the only reason this did not ship the wrong fix. That made lib/community-href.ts redundant AND wrong: it rewrote every signed-out card link to /sign-in?next=<path>, which for /people is exactly what the proxy now does anyway, and for /circles/<slug> and /events/<slug> is strictly WORSE - the first has a public twin the proxy deliberately lets through (lib/nav/public-twin.ts) and the second is anon-readable outright (isPublicEventView), so both were being sent to a login wall in front of a page they could already see. So the boolean is gone, community-href.ts is deleted, and the six pages that awaited supabase.auth.getUser() for it (discover/{,circles/,events/,places/[citySlug]/,cities/[citySlug]/,events/in/[city]/[category]/}page.tsx) render statically again, honouring the export const revalidate = 3600 each already declared. Crawlers gain too: /circles and /people are robots-disallowed, so a bot now skips the link instead of fetching a /sign-in?next= it can only discover is noindex. app/page.tsx passed a hardcoded false, which is the tell that the splash had already decided the boolean was not worth an auth read.

entries.title: The sitemap's batched podcast read was silently truncating at 1000 rows
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS STALE AND THE REAL BUG WAS WORSE. The N+1 had already been collapsed — sitemap.ts called a batched reader. But that batch used `.limit(min(n*200, 5000))` with no `.range()`, and `.limit()` does not raise PostgREST's server-side `max_rows` (supabase/config.toml:18 = 1000, and service_role does not escape it). So it declared a 5000-row appetite, received 1000, and reported no error. Because the batch orders `created_at DESC` ACROSS ALL SPACES, the dropped rows were whole trailing Spaces: their /podcasts index and every Show URL vanished from the sitemap with nothing to notice. Collapsing 200 correct small queries into one truncated one traded latency for missing URLs — the third instance today of a fix whose instrument could not tell 'nothing there' from 'I could not see'. Now paged explicitly with `.range()` over a TOTAL order (created_at DESC, id ASC — the tiebreaker is required so a created_at tie cannot straddle a page boundary and be skipped or repeated), stopping on a short page. Still O(rows), never O(Spaces).

verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE — that the batched read pages — rather than the row's words. Backed by app/sitemap.test.ts, which rebuilds the URL list the old per-Space loop would have emitted and requires an exact match, and which was confirmed to FAIL against an unpaged read (expected 1000 to be 1500) before being accepted.

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-17. The probe that flagged this row as stale was `grep-present /'app'|"app"/` in check-canon.mjs, which passes on the mere appearance of the string 'app' - shape, not truth. Replaced with the consequence, measured in-process: import the guard, assert SEAM_ROOTS still covers app/ AND lib/, run scanCodeSeam() over the real tree and require zero member-facing violations. MEASURED: 3,398 files under app/ + lib/ + components/, 22,437 member-facing strings judged, 0 violations. The floors (MIN_SEAM_FILES 2000, MIN_SEAM_STRINGS 15000) make a guard that stops finding the corpus exit 79 rather than report a clean sweep of nothing. Proved BOTH ways: a real banned string ('Find your tribe') under a copy key fails it, narrowing SEAM_ROOTS fails it by name, and the SAME words in a comment and in an internal identifier do NOT fire it - the false-positive half is what keeps a widened guard from being routed around.

🔴 RE-SCOPED 2026-08-21, because this probe COST MAIN A RED BUILD. It called scanCodeSeam(), which parses every file in the seam — 3,413 files, 21,947 strings, 7.57s of CPU. check:backlog runs under a 20s CPU budget asserted by scripts/backlog-contract.test.ts, and this ONE row was 41% of it. On 2026-08-21 the budget came in at 20,080ms against the 20,000ms ceiling and main went red for 56 minutes (commit 6127a26), on a merge that had changed nothing but 18 PNGs.

WHAT THE PROBE DROPPED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LOSS OF COVERAGE. It asserted found.length === 0 — that the whole tree is on-canon. That is precisely what `pnpm check:canon` asserts, and check:canon runs as its own guard in the SAME CI job. Duplicating it bought nothing and cost something real: a canon violation introduced by anyone, anywhere, would fail THIS ROW, reporting a regression in the seam-widening work that shipped months ago. A probe should measure its own row's consequence, not re-grade a neighbouring guard.

WHAT IT STILL MEASURES, which is this row's actual consequence: the seam was WIDENED past content/ to app/ + lib/, and it reaches a real corpus. SEAM_ROOTS must still contain both roots (narrowing it fails by name), and seamFiles() must still return at least MIN_SEAM_FILES. seamFiles is the directory WALK without the parse — newly exported for this, 0.031s against 7.57s, a 244x reduction — so the non-triviality floor survives intact: a walk that breaks or a root that moves still trips it rather than reporting a clean sweep of nothing.

entries.detail: There is no repo-side gate for function grants at all: check-grants.mjs covers tables only, and nothing anywhere references has_function_privilege. 29 anon-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions currently rest on a human remembering to read an advisor. entries.title: R7: the eyebrow role is no longer hand-rolled where the code itself names it
entries.detail: THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO. It called this 'largely mechanical' over ~698 sites with 3 adopters. Measured 2026-08-17: 615 sites pair `uppercase` with a LITERAL tracking value (tracking-wide 436, widest 59, wider 60, 20 arbitrary), against 87 already on the `eyebrow` utility and 69 on `tracking-eyebrow`. 87 adopters, not 3. The population is NOT one role, which is why a sweep is the wrong instrument: the dominant string is 11px `text-2xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-muted`, and a large share are pill badges (rounded-pill px-2 py-0.5) and dense table headers. Sweeping them means 11px -> 12px, semibold -> bold and 0.025em -> 0.18em - a 7.2x tracking change that widens a label inside a px-2.5 pill it was sized to fit. That is an unreviewed visual change to several hundred surfaces, not a rename. WHAT SHIPPED is the half a machine can settle: of the 15 slots the CODE ITSELF names `eyebrow`, SEVEN hand-rolled the role across five different letter-spacings, all in the shared kit - EditorShell, Toast, StudioWindow, SparkShell, EntityHeader, JourneyBuilder, HostCohostSection. All seven now compose the utility. The rest is a ratchet, seeded at the POST-sweep 608 rather than the 615 found, which is what makes reverting any of the seven raise it.

entries.notes: ADR-1072. The structural finding is the one worth keeping: lib/theme/eyebrow-role.test.ts had seven assertions, all green, ALL READING globals.css AND NONE READING A CALL SITE. The definition was locked while the product rendered the role ten ways - a guard on the definition cannot see adoption. 🔴 STILL OPEN AND AN OWNER CALL, tracked as OWN-027: there is a SECOND eyebrow implementation nobody reconciled. components/page-editor/blocks/kit.tsx exports an <Eyebrow> component with about 26 adopters rendering text-body-sm (0.875rem) - DAWN's declared eyebrow size, i.e. the exact half of the DAWN split that globals.css resolved DOWN to 0.75rem on 2026-08-05. Which register wins is a design decision, not a refactor. The ratchet is ADVISORY by design (check:adoption is continue-on-error in ci.yml); the blocking half is the vitest assertion. Both are in the probe because losing either would leave the other reading as coverage.

entries.title: The rail ladder: Auto / Open / Strip, persisted, plus a desktop left-rail fold

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1071). THE ROW WAS STALE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION AND RIGHT ABOUT THE GAP. The three-position ladder and the desktop left-rail fold were already built and already gated. The PERSISTED half had nothing behind it: replacing the whole body of writeStoredRailFolds with `return` left all 38 tests in rail-fold.test.ts PASSING, and deleting railFold from the shell mount in app/(main)/layout.tsx - the entire no-flash path - left 288 tests passing with tsc green. AND IT SURFACED A REAL DEFECT. writeStoredRailFolds is built to survive blocked localStorage (the setItem throw is swallowed, the cookie still lands) but readStoredRailFolds read localStorage and nothing else. No baseline recapture needed - the rail's state at rest is unchanged, and the new behaviour only fires when localStorage is empty AND a cookie exists, which a fresh capture browser never has.

entries.title: Send the three prod-ahead tokens back to DAWN (NOT the fourth)
entries.detail:
CORRECTED 2026-08-19: this row listed FOUR tokens and one of them must not be sent. --color-focus-ring, --color-text-on-broadcast and --color-text-subtle are genuinely correct in production and wrong in DAWN's artifact, and SYNC.md requires they go back on the next round or the next handoff silently reintroduces the AA failures they fixed. --color-text-on-primary is NOT one of them and has not been since 2026-08-06. Production is #FFFFFF and DAWN is #FFFFFF; verified in both files 2026-08-19, and lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts derives the divergence set from both stylesheets on every pnpm test and agrees. What happened was a SPLIT, not a revert: while on-primary was ink every rank core inherited an ink glyph and gold, the lightest core by design, fell to 2.46:1. The glyph moved to its own token (--color-text-on-rank) and the button label went back to white. SENDING THE OLD ROW WOULD ASK DAWN TO MAKE ON-PRIMARY INK, reintroducing, from the very sheet meant to prevent regressions, the exact failure the split fixed. design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md section 4 is the authority and says so under the heading "Do not send"; that sheet is machine-checked and this row was not, which is why the row drifted and the sheet did not. PROD-AHEAD section 5 also lists twelve additions DAWN has no row for, including --color-text-on-rank itself, which the outbound handoff should carry as new rows rather than corrections. ── ⏳ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24, THE PREMISE HOLDS EXACTLY, AND THE ROW MOVES TO `blocked` BECAUSE NO CODE UNBLOCKS IT. Both stylesheets were diffed directly (app/globals.css vs design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css, parsed per top-level block, not via the test runner): --color-focus-ring light prod #B86A15 vs DAWN #E2912F · --color-text-on-broadcast prod #1A1206 vs DAWN #FFFFFF in BOTH modes · --color-text-subtle prod #6E6558 / #A2957D vs DAWN #8F8675 / #7E735F. THREE tokens, five rows, unchanged since 2026-08-19. 🔴 --color-text-on-primary AGREES in both modes (#FFFFFF on both sides) and is still the row that must NOT be sent. Dark focus-ring agrees (#F2B14E), and --color-text-on-rank (#1A1206) is prod-only — an ADDITION for §4 of the handoff, not a correction. THE SEND HAS NOT HAPPENED: design_handoff/CHANGES.md is still the 2026-08-03 round, so no inbound reply references the 2026-08-19 handoff. 🔴 IT IS OWNER-ONLY. DAWN is an external Claude Design project and design_handoff/README.md's loop is copy-the-bundle, owner-mediated in both directions; there is no repo-side action that delivers a doc to it. THE PAYLOAD IS NOW ONE STEP: HANDOFF-TO-DAWN-2026-08-19.md opens with a paste block naming the one file to give DAWN and the one sentence to say, mirroring the “▶ Paste this into Claude Code” block CHANGES.md uses in the inbound direction. Nothing else is pending on this row — the doc, the machine-checked token set and the do-not-send note are all already in the tree.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. THE SEND HAPPENED AND DAWN APPLIED ALL OF IT. The row's own closing condition was 'when a CHANGES.md reply references the 2026-08-19 handoff, or the owner confirms delivery'. Both are now true. design_handoff/CHANGES.md's H1 reads 'DAWN round of 2026-08-25 (reply to HANDOFF-TO-DAWN-2026-08-19.md)', and its §2 lists every correction as applied value-for-value: focus-ring #B86A15, text-on-broadcast #1A1206 both modes, text-subtle #6E6558 / #A2957D, primary-strong #965C12, surface-post aliased to var(--color-surface), plus all twelve additions from PROD-AHEAD §5 including --color-text-on-rank. DAWN also corrected its own .theme-light-lock scope in step, which carried private copies of five of those values — an extension the handoff did not know about and DAWN volunteered.
  🔴 AND CLOSING IT EXPOSED THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH, WHICH IS LIVE-127. The corrections were applied in DAWN, not in the vendored photocopy: design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css is still the 2026-08-03 export and still holds --color-focus-ring #E2912F. So PROD-AHEAD.md — the sheet the NEXT outbound handoff copies — was still asking DAWN to apply work DAWN finished three weeks ago, and lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts was green throughout, because green there means 'found == declared' and both sets are eight rows. Green never meant the files agree. That is the same stale-row failure this row was CORRECTED for on 2026-08-19, recurring one level up: not a stale row in the sheet, a stale FILE under the whole sheet.

entries.title: The vendored DAWN bundle is a photocopy three rounds old; the token half is now reconciled, the design half is not
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while syncing DAWN's reply, and the finding is the guard, not the files. design_handoff/dawn/ is a hand-copied snapshot of an external Claude Design project. design_handoff/CHANGES.md is DAWN's prose reply. They are copied ACROSS SEPARATELY and nothing measured whether they were the same round. On 2026-08-25 the reply arrived and the bundle did not.
  MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: every marker CHANGES.md says it wrote is absent from the file it names. tokens/effects.css has no 'hero-zone' (the four legibility rungs), ui_kits/marketing/sections.jsx has no 'data-hero-zone', tokens/colors.css has no 'on-media' family, ui_kits/app/index.html has none of the rewritten banner copy, ui_kits/app/nav-rail.jsx has none of the five corrected admin keys. guidelines/on-media.card.html was never copied at all. And colors.css still holds --color-focus-ring #E2912F, the pre-correction brand amber. The bundle is the 2026-08-03 export.
  🔴 WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts reads that colors.css on every pnpm test and was GREEN, because it asserts found-divergences == declared-divergences and both sets are eight rows. Green means 'they disagree in the ways we wrote down'. Read as freshness — which is how it was read — it says the opposite of what is true. The cost was already banked: design_handoff/PROD-AHEAD.md, the sheet the next outbound handoff copies verbatim, was asking DAWN to apply five corrections DAWN applied on 2026-08-25 (LIVE-027).
  ✅ WHAT LANDED WITH THIS ROW. scripts/check-dawn-bundle.mjs declares which round the bundle is and fails BOTH ways. The dangerous direction is the second: if the bundle is re-exported and the declaration is not moved, a refreshed colors.css silently closes five declared divergences, and a sheet that still lists them either re-sends applied work or gets 'reconciled' by pushing DAWN's old values back into app/globals.css — un-fixing three measured AA failures. The guard's failure text names the three files that must move together. PROD-AHEAD.md §0 now carries the do-not-re-send banner, and the divergence test's header says in full what a green run there does not mean.
  THE OWNER STEP IS ONE ACTION: re-export design_handoff/dawn/ from the DAWN project and drop it in. Everything else is already wired and will tell you what to update.

── ✅ THE COLOUR HALF IS CLOSED, 2026-08-26, WITHOUT AN EXPORT. The owner could not download the DAWN bundle, so the question became: how much of this round can be reconciled from what is already written down, and where is the line?
  THE LINE IS TRANSCRIPTION vs INVENTION. CHANGES.md §2 documents every colour value DAWN applied, and PROD-AHEAD §5 carries the twelve additions' hexes (CHANGES.md names them but prints no values). Copying those into design_handoff/dawn/tokens/colors.css is TRANSCRIPTION of two independent written statements - DAWN's own changelog, and the owner confirming it in-thread. Writing tokens/effects.css's four hero rungs, the nav-rail keys, the banner copy or guidelines/on-media.card.html would be INVENTION: those are design artifacts, described in prose, not specified in it. DAWN made precisely that mistake this round - it drew a hero plate from a description production had deleted on an owner ruling (PROD-AHEAD §6a). So the token half was done and the design half was deliberately left.
  ✅ RESULT, AND IT IS COMPLETE FOR ITS HALF: all EIGHT declared divergences closed at once, and prodOnly went empty in both modes. lib/theme/dawn-divergence.test.ts derives the set on every pnpm test and both ledgers are now empty - not because nobody looked, but because the two stylesheets agree on every colour token, re-proven each run. Twelve corrections across :root, .dark AND .theme-light-lock (the lock carried private copies of five, which CHANGES.md §2 flagged), plus eight new tokens.
  🔴 THE GUARD HAD TO CHANGE SHAPE, and that is the durable part. It modelled ONE round for the whole bundle. The moment one file was current and five were not, a single BUNDLE_ROUND was false in BOTH directions: '2026-08-03' rejects the file that IS current, '2026-08-25' demands five that are not. Provenance moved onto each marker - `transcribed` / `exported` / `pending` - where it can actually be true, and the guard now fails per-file in either direction. It caught this partial sync itself: after colors.css changed it went red naming the exact three files that must move together, which is what it was built to do.
  WHAT IS LEFT IS GENUINELY OWNER-ONLY and is now five markers plus one absent file, all design work: tokens/effects.css (hero rungs), ui_kits/marketing/sections.jsx (data-hero-zone), ui_kits/app/index.html (banner copy), ui_kits/marketing/beta.jsx (Funnel induction), ui_kits/app/nav-rail.jsx (five admin keys), guidelines/on-media.card.html (never arrived). ⚠️ NONE OF IT IS LOAD-BEARING: design_handoff/ is eslint-ignored and every reference to it from app code is a COMMENT citing a path. It cannot reach production. This row is housekeeping, and the sheet that could actually mislead - PROD-AHEAD.md - is now correct.

Half green is the honest reading of a mixed bundle.

The quantities the row names were already real and already wired (PLACEHOLDER_ALLOWANCES = false; the free rungs are 200 contacts, 300 sends/mo, 3 QR codes, 1 published Journey, 1 operator seat), and the enforcement seams were built to short-circuit on gatesLive rather than to be added later. What was decorative was the SWITCH, not the machinery.

MEASURED THE SAME DAY, so 'live' is not taken on trust: every non-root Space holds 0 contacts and 0 QR codes, the root Space is exempt from metering by type, and no Space crosses a meter on flip day. The grandfather rule in allowanceVerdict means a cap only ever stops the NEXT write.

entries.title: Loom D1: Studio ingest + ranked search — four extras built, the fifth struck as stale
entries.detail:
Shipped, but the ingest extras are still pending: checksum dedupe, EXIF strip, dims/colors/blurhash, the rendition set, and FTS-ranked/trigram search.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate. ── ⚙️ RE-TESTED AND RE-SHAPED 2026-08-24 (ADR-1082). The row is TRUE - no ingest module exists, no `textSearch` appears anywhere in the tree - but it is MIS-SHAPED: it reads as build-from-zero and is actually a WIRING job. 🔴 THE MOST USEFUL FINDING FOR SEQUENCING: PR 1 NEEDS NO MIGRATION. Every column and index D1 writes to is already applied - sha256, blurhash, focal_x/y, orig_width/height and the dedupe index library_assets_sha256_idx (20260920000000_library_dam.sql:15-33), plus the generated search_tsv column with GIN and a gin_trgm_ops index on title (20260919000000_library_assets.sql:61-88). So the first increment carries ZERO ADR-1111 ordering risk and can merge alongside siblings in any order. THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: eight upload sites, but six already funnel through insertSpaceLibraryImage (lib/library/store.ts:264). Only two bypass it - app/(main)/admin/library/actions.ts:53 and recraft-actions.ts:101 - so widening the chokepoint plus routing those two covers everything. FIRST PR: a pure lib/library/ingest.ts (node:crypto sha256 + a dependency-free image-header dimension parser), the widened chokepoint writing sha256/width/height, dedupe on the existing (space_id, sha256) index, the two bypass sites routed through it, and materialize.ts:772's `bytes: 0`. 🔴 THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT IN PR 1, each with a reason. (1) EXIF STRIP CARRIES A HAZARD THE ROW NEVER MENTIONS: removing APP1 removes the ORIENTATION tag, so any phone JPEG relying on it renders rotated. The safe form strips APP1/APP13/XMP then re-emits a minimal APP1 carrying only Orientation, proven by a test on a rotation-6 JPEG that keeps orientation and loses GPS. Note only photos over 3.5 MB currently lose EXIF at all, by accident, via the canvas re-encode at image-shrink.ts:127. (2) blurhash and colours need PIXEL DECODE, which server-side means sharp - and check:og-trace is at 67 of a 100 ceiling with this seam reachable from the Loom picker, page editor, importer and email studio. That is the 2026-08-11 ENOSPC fan-out one directory over; compute them in the browser where image-shrink.ts already holds an ImageBitmap. (3) FTS ranking is its own PR because it is the one piece that MAY need a migration: PostgREST can filter on search_tsv with no schema change but cannot ORDER BY ts_rank, so either rank in-process (migration-free, recommended first) or add a search_library_assets RPC mirroring the existing match_library_assets - and that path takes the full ADR-1111 ordering discipline. ⚠️ lib/library/store.ts:149 says FTS is 'a follow-up, D7', contradicting BUILD-LIST.md:1233 which puts it in D1; the code comment is the stale one and gets fixed in the same pass.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1121). FOUR OF THE FIVE WERE REAL AND WERE BUILT; THE FIFTH WAS ALREADY ANSWERED AND WAS STILL SITTING IN THIS ROW. 🔴 THE RENDITION SET IS STRUCK, NOT BUILT: HYG-017 established against the LIVE database that `library_renditions` has no table and no index — created 20260920000000_library_dam.sql:47, dropped 20260925000000:16 — and four places in the tree say transforms are ON-THE-FLY (ADR-480's migration header, lib/library/renditions.ts, PROG-D3's scope line, BUILD-LIST's Loom owner-decision line) against this row's one line saying otherwise. A rendition is a REQUEST, never a row; RENDITION_PRESETS belongs to D3's resolver. That is the fourth row in eight days to be wrong about its own scope (ADR-1082, ADR-1112): a probe checks whether the work is DONE and nothing checks whether it is still WANTED.

WHAT WAS BUILT. (1) CHECKSUM DEDUPE, on the (space_id, sha256) index that had been sitting unused since the DAM migration. The hash is taken AFTER the strip, which is what makes it useful rather than theatrical: two exports of one photo differing only in their EXIF block now dedupe to one asset. Space-scoped on purpose — a global match would hand one space another space's image — and it short-circuits BEFORE the storage write, so a duplicate costs no disk. (2) EXIF/XMP/IPTC STRIP WITH ORIENTATION PRESERVED. The row named the strip but not its hazard: the rotation tag lives in the same APP1 block as the GPS coordinates, so the obvious `drop APP1` is privacy-correct and renders every portrait phone photo SIDEWAYS. The strip re-emits a 32-byte APP1 carrying Orientation alone, proven on a rotation-6 fixture that keeps the rotation and loses the coordinates; ICC_PROFILE and the Adobe marker are kept because both change how the file DECODES. (3) DIMENSIONS from the container header (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP ×3 chunk flavours) plus BLURHASH + PALETTE. 🔴 THE PIXEL WORK RUNS IN THE BROWSER AND MUST STAY THERE: a server decode means sharp, check:og-trace has it at 67 of 100, and this seam is reachable from the picker, page editor, importer and email studio. MEASURED FAN-OUT OF THIS CHANGE: ZERO — no runtime dependency added, no next/og, no native module, and the probe asserts all four new modules stay clean of both. (4) FTS-RANKED + TRIGRAM SEARCH, WITH NO MIGRATION. Both indexes already existed (search_tsv GIN + title gin_trgm_ops, 20260919000000:61-88); PostgREST can FILTER a tsvector but cannot `order by ts_rank`, so both arms run and merge and lib/library/search-rank.ts does the ordering. FTS is stemmed and cannot match a fragment or a typo; trigram matches fragments and ranks nothing; neither is a superset of the other.

ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: store.ts:149's comment claiming FTS was 'a follow-up, D7' (BUILD-LIST put it in D1; the comment was the stale one), and the zero-size lie at materialize.ts — now NULL, because a path that files an already-stored object genuinely does not know the size and 0 renders as a real '0 B' asset. BOTH former bypass sites are gone: the Loom Studio upload now inserts through insertSpaceLibraryImage like everything else, so there is exactly ONE place a Loom row is written.

NOT CLAIMED, and split out rather than hidden: server-side GENERATORS (Recraft, Vera covers, importer seeds) get a checksum and dimensions but no blurhash, because no browser exists on those paths. That is HYG-021.

verify.cmd: node scripts/prog-d1-probe.mjs

entries.notes: Probes the CONSEQUENCE in-process (LIVE-034 forbids a probe that spawns a test runner): the dedupe read is scoped to (space_id, sha256); the strip re-emits an orientation APP1 rather than merely deleting one; the four new modules import neither sharp nor next/og; search reaches search_tsv and ranks; the Loom Studio upload no longer writes library_assets directly; and nothing references library_renditions. Verified to FAIL on a mutation that makes the strip re-emit orientation 1 instead of the real one — i.e. it catches the sideways-photo regression, not merely the presence of a function. Unit proofs live in lib/library/{ingest,blurhash,search-rank,space-images}.test.ts and lib/page-editor/loom-field-actions.test.ts under `pnpm test`.

entries.title: Loom D2: the AssetField seam + backfill
entries.detail:
One Upload / Pick from library / Paste URL control replacing ImageField everywhere; blocks store an asset REFERENCE plus a URL cache; render resolves reference → CDN url; backfill existing site-media URLs into the catalog and rewrite references.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── ⚙️ RE-TESTED, RE-SHAPED AND HALF-SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1130). The row promised three things; the census against the LIVE database found ONE of them real. (1) THE ONE CONTROL ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS ALREADY EVERYWHERE: components/loom/loom-picker.tsx has 16 consumers (page editor, entity blocks, Studio spark, branding, events, QR, email), and the row's 'Paste URL' leg was overruled by an owner directive recorded in three code headers — the Loom is the only way in, upload lives inside the picker, no paste box. (2) THE REFERENCE HALF WAS GENUINELY UNBUILT and is NOW SHIPPED for Puck documents: an image value is string | AssetRef ({ assetId, url }, lib/library/asset-ref.ts); the picker's onSelectAsset/onSelectManyAssets hand the caller the reference; imgField, loomImageField and the gallery field store it; the BlockRender walk unwraps every ref to its URL string before any renderer sees props (proven byte-identical against the same doc stored as strings); and getPublishedData refreshes stale caches via lib/library/resolve-refs.ts — fail-open to the cache, zero queries for a ref-free document, zero sharp/og-trace fan-out. Legacy strings stay legal forever, so NO stored document was rewritten. (3) 🔴 THE BACKFILL'S PREMISE IS DEAD, IN THE GOOD DIRECTION, and it was the row's own headline. Measured 2026-08-25: live pages documents hold ZERO site-media URLs (2 URL occurrences total, 1 distinct, external); all 6 page_content.hero_image site-media references already have catalog rows; 15 of 23 site-media objects are catalogued and the other 8 are importer/<intakeId>/ INTAKE STAGING files referenced only by 7 business_intake staging rows (LIVE-120), which the post-ADR-1121 importer no longer produces uncatalogued. There is nothing to backfill and nothing to rewrite; the backfill is STRUCK with these numbers, not built.

REMAINING SEQUENCE, in order: (a) HYG-029 — reference-storing adoption beyond the Puck fields: entity-block controls, Studio spark image fields, header-image-field, email studio, and the DECISION for column-backed surfaces (spaces.brand_logo_url, page_content.hero_image, page_settings.og_image_url cannot hold a ref in a text column — companion id columns or stay URL-cached). (b) Space-document cache refresh: space docs render refs correctly via the cache today (the unwrap is in the shared BlockRender), but readPageDoc does not call refreshAssetRefUrls; wire it when D3 edits can re-point a live asset's URL. (c) The usage index over refs is D4 (block_usage per ADR-975) — refs make it a cheap JSONB scan; do not build it here.

verify.evidence: Seam half shipped + proven in-tree (lib/library/asset-ref.test.ts, lib/library/resolve-refs.test.ts, the AssetRef describe in lib/page-editor/block-render.test.tsx, all under pnpm test); backfill struck on the ADR-1130 census. Remaining breadth is HYG-029 + the space-doc refresh.

entries.title: Loom D7: semantic + AI
entries.detail:
Populate embedding, hybrid FTS+vector RRF ranking, AI auto-tag and colour extraction, background removal / upscale. Later the Weave generative composer.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate. ── 🔴 ITS FIRST ITEM IS ALREADY SHIPPED, found 2026-08-24 while re-testing PROG-D1. 'Populate embedding' and vector search are LIVE and cron-driven: lib/library/embeddings.ts exports reindexLibraryEmbeddings / matchLibraryAssets / similarLibraryAssets over the match_library_assets RPC (20260921000000_library_embeddings.sql), wired into the Studio at app/(main)/admin/library/page.tsx:162,167 behind sort=relevant, with a cron at vercel.json:37. D7's real remainder is hybrid FTS+vector RRF, auto-tag, colour extraction and background removal - and RRF is BLOCKED ON D1's FTS half, a dependency neither row states.

── UNBLOCKED 2026-08-25: the RRF dependency this row named is met. PROG-D1 shipped the FTS half (lib/library/search-rank.ts merges a search_tsv arm with a trigram arm and ranks them), so hybrid FTS+vector RRF now has both inputs. Note what it must NOT copy: D1's ranking is in-process because PostgREST cannot `order by ts_rank`. A true RRF over both signals wants ONE query that ranks both, which is the `search_library_assets` RPC ADR-1121 scoped and deliberately did not build — and that path takes the full ADR-1111 migration ordering discipline. Colour extraction is also partly done: library_assets.colors is populated on browser uploads by lib/library/image-describe.ts, so D7's remainder there is generated assets (HYG-021) and AI auto-tag.

entries.title: Re-theme P4: universal browse hero
entries.detail:
The 24 plain IndexTemplate pages adopt heroOverlay so the hero is everywhere.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── SEAM SHIPPED (#2254): lib/layout/index-hero.ts — resolveIndexHero(route, opts) returns a spreadable IndexTemplate prop bag over a four-rung ladder, with INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS holding the route->cover map and the short/large product decision. PROG-P6 / ADR-1122 then made rung 2 resolve itself through the copy cascade.

🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127). THE ROW COUNTS ONE OF THE TWO BROWSE COMPOSITIONS, AND NAMES THE WRONG DEFECT.
  · COUNTED BY RENDER SITE: 41 browse render sites, not 24 pages. 32 compose IndexTemplate; 9 head an operator-rearrangeable body with MarketHero (the sanctioned editable index, PAGE-FRAMEWORK §8.5: /circles, /channels, /events via events-surface.tsx, /spaces/directory, /discover/spaces, /classifieds, /housing, /market, /store). Of the 32, 7 already drew the band, so 25 were plain — the row's 24 was one off, on half the surfaces.
  · THE DEFECT IS NOT A MISSING heroOverlay. MarketHero is a thin wrapper over the SAME PageHero the heroOverlay branch renders, so those 9 already looked right. What they lacked was the LADDER: getPageHeaderImage (rung 1, the operator's Settings > Basics header-image uploader) appeared in exactly 3 of the 41 render sites, and 4 more reached it via resolveIndexHero. 7 of 41. THE OTHER 34 READ THE OPERATOR'S UPLOAD NOWHERE, and savePageSeo gates that uploader on isSafeRoute rather than an allowlist — so an operator could upload a header image on any of them and watch nothing happen. ADR-1122's /network bug at 34x scale. Invisible in production only because page_settings holds ONE header image in the whole table (/crew, a Dashboard, which does read it).
  · THE RESOLVER'S OWN EXEMPLARS HAD NOT ADOPTED IT. /practices, /journeys and /library are the three pages whose duplicated stanza motivated index-hero.ts, and all three still carried it verbatim a week later, while the module header read "this module is the one copy". It was the fifth.

✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127), 18 files:
  · resolveMarketHero + asMarketHero in lib/layout/index-hero.ts — the editable-index twin, same four rungs, MarketHero's prop names. `cover` is REQUIRED because MarketHero types `image` non-null (the gradient band is a result on a utility index and a broken header on a hero-led commerce one). All 9 MarketHero sites adopted; each lost its hand-rolled resolveHeaderElement call and gained rungs 1 and 2. Zero visual change today.
  · /practices, /journeys, /library spread {...hero}; ~30 lines of re-typed ladder deleted. Zero visual change (the map already held their exact covers).
  · /events/calendar adopts the band — the one plain index whose SECTION carries a live operator hero (page_content['/events'].hero_image, set in June). Its new row is the first to separate the two flags: size is about the BAND (short: a month grid is a work surface), inheritHero is about the IMAGE (true: the calendar is the Events section wearing a different body).

⏳ STILL OPEN: the 24 remaining plain IndexTemplate pages — LIVE-117, and counted nowhere else. That is a real layout change on 24 surfaces (each page's h1 moves onto a band), not a dropped rung, so it carries its own PR, screenshots and visual-baseline pass; it also would not fit here under the 40-file gate.

verify.evidence: Program phase, HALF SHIPPED. The ladder half is proven by lib/layout/index-hero.test.ts (35 cases, including 7 over resolveMarketHero and the /events/calendar row) and by the tree: `grep -rl "<MarketHero"` returns 9 render sites and all 9 now reach rung 1 through resolveMarketHero, where 0 of 9 did on 2026-08-25. The open half is the 24 plain IndexTemplate pages, probed executably by LIVE-117 (it fails today and counts them). Census reproduced by grepping render sites for <IndexTemplate>/<MarketHero> and for heroOverlay|resolveIndexHero|resolveMarketHero|getPageHeaderImage.

entries.title: Re-theme P5: entity headers onto PageHero
entries.detail:
Fold the DetailTemplate band pages onto the one PageHero grammar, so entity and index become one component.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-24 (AGENTS.md / ADR-1082). THE ROW SAID 43; IT IS 30. Counted by RENDER SITE, not by import: 28 files render DetailTemplate directly and 2 more (/events/<slug> and /discover/events/<slug>) reach it through EventDetailTemplate = 30 LIVE SURFACES. The 43 swept in things that are not band pages: 2 loading.tsx skeletons, the EventDetailTemplate wrapper itself, a test file, and 3 marketplace pages (classifieds / housing / market) that render ListingDetailTemplate — a SEPARATE template that never touches DetailTemplate.
Second premise, also wrong: 'band pages' implies they have bands. Of the 30, only 9 carried any cover at all (a bespoke identity-variant PageHero passed through the `hero` escape hatch) and 1 more put cover art inside a `band` slot. THE OTHER 20 HAD NO COVER. And DetailTemplate's `coverImage` — the 'standard Detail cover' PAGE-FRAMEWORK §8.5 documents — had ZERO CALLERS: every coverImage= in the tree was on a PageHero nested inside `hero`. So P5 is not a re-theme of 43 existing bands. It is giving 20 pages a cover they never had and retiring 9 hand-rolled stanzas.

── SEAM SHIPPED 2026-08-24 (branch theme/p5-entity-hero, ADR-1117). lib/layout/detail-hero.ts — resolveDetailHero(route, opts) returns a spreadable DetailTemplate prop bag, the detail-side twin of PROG-P4's index-hero.ts. Its four-rung ladder is INVERTED from the index's (the entity's own cover outranks the operator's site-wide image, because on an entity page the entity's owner owns the surface), and each section carries a tail of 'placeholder' (the gradient band) or 'none' (no cover), because on a detail page the h1 lives BELOW the cover so the band is decoration, not the thing carrying the title. 35 unit tests cover every rung, both tails, the focus-travels-with-its-image rule, the longest-prefix map, and both fail-safe paths. An UNMAPPED route resolves to no cover, so adopting on an unmapped page is a visual no-op — which is what lets the rest land in PRs under the 40-file CI limit.

── ADOPTED 2026-08-25 (branch theme/p5-adoption, ADR-1136) — 26 of 30 surfaces now resolve through lib/layout/detail-hero.ts (21 standard + 5 identity). Re-measured first (ADR-1082): still 30 render sites on main@fcb5348c4 — the census held — but the '9 bespoke stanzas' split did not: only 5 of the 9 carry the resolveHeaderElement stanza (/channels/<id>, /circles/<slug>, /journeys/<slug>, /journeys/<slug>/learn, /people/<handle>); the other 4 hand-roll a bespoke cover NODE, not the stanza. The module gained the identity twin — asIdentityHero + resolveIdentityHero, the detail echo of PROG-P4's resolveMarketHero: same four-rung ladder, PageHero prop names, empty ladder = null (the gradient) because the identity band carries the h1. All 5 stanza pages adopted it, deleting their copies; their lockups did not move. The 17 straightforward sites adopted resolveDetailHero (the 2 client islands via their server pages; VeraProfile became async). 14 new DETAIL_HERO_DEFAULTS rows, every one image:null + tail:'none' (pinned by a unit test): no cover invented, rung 2 armed — the operator's section Settings image stops being dropped on the floor. One visible change: /discover/journeys/<slug> gains rung 1 (journey_plans.cover_image + cover_focus). /support, /connections, /admin/crm/pipeline and the Space podcast show stay deliberately unmapped (private/operator surfaces; square show artwork is identity, not a cover).

── REMAINING — 4 of 30, each a bespoke cover COMPOSITION whose folding is a behaviour change with its own PR + screenshots (ADR-1117 §'what this does not do', reaffirmed ADR-1136):
  · /circles/starter/<slug> — a generated TemplateCover (pillar-branded cover art), no element resolve to retire.
  · /spaces/<slug> profile layout — its own Header/Hero cover-size vocabulary (readCoverSize/readCoverScrim), never consults the header element.
  · /events/<slug> + /discover/events/<slug> via EventDetailTemplate — a multi-source event-media ladder (uploaded cover → scanned poster → crop) with no element resolve; folding it would newly make event cover height element-tuned.
  · The 2 loading.tsx skeletons follow their pages, which did not move.
  · SEPARATE, NOT P5: the 3 ListingDetailTemplate pages are a different template. File their own row if their hero should join the grammar.

verify.evidence: 26 of 30 render sites resolve through lib/layout/detail-hero.ts — 21 spread resolveDetailHero, 5 identity pages spread resolveIdentityHero; grep 'resolveDetailHero\|resolveIdentityHero' across app/ + components/ counts the call sites, and lib/layout/detail-hero.test.ts (45 cases) probes the ladder, the identity twin, and pins every ADR-1136 map row to image:null + tail:'none'. The 4 non-adopters are bespoke cover compositions, enumerated in the detail.

entries.title: Re-theme P6: the copy cascade
entries.detail:
Generalize page_content into a site -> section -> page inherit-cascade, widen editable fields to body copy and images, and extend check:canon to .tsx. Overlaps LIVE-018.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1122). Two of the three clauses did not survive measurement.

✅ CLAUSE 3 WAS ALREADY DONE, by LIVE-018 / ADR-1065, eight days before this row was picked up. check:canon's SEAM_ROOTS is ['app','lib','components'] and its walk takes /\.tsx?$/. Measured: 3,406 seam files, 1,882 of them .tsx, 21,674 member-facing strings judged, 0 violations. The violation count for 'turning it on' is ZERO, because it is on.

⚠️ CLAUSE 1'S PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. page_content does not hold copy. Production, read 2026-08-25: SIX rows, all six on SECTION ROOTS (/circles, /events, /journeys, /nearby, /network, /practices). ZERO set title. ZERO set description. ALL SIX set hero_image. The one row mentioning a CTA (/circles, label 'Start a Circle') has an EMPTY cta_href, so it has never rendered. The operator's real use of this table is one field, the section hero, stored at exactly the rung a cascade would inherit FROM, while the reader only ever looked at the exact route.

✅ SHIPPED (ADR-1122): lib/layout/content-cascade.ts, resolving page -> section(s) -> site ('*') -> coded fallback in one query, request-cached, fail-safe, PER FIELD. Identity fields (title/description) deliberately do not inherit, because they feed pageContentMetadata and inheriting them manufactures duplicate meta descriptions across a section; the CTA resolves as ONE unit so a page label is never spliced onto a section link. NO MIGRATION: the section rung is the row that already exists. resolvePageContent consumes it. resolveIndexHero now resolves rung 2 itself, closing a live bug: /network has carried a page_content hero since June and dropped it on the floor. INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS gains inheritHero (false on the three utility rows) so the cascade cannot silently overturn the short/large split. longestPrefixRow is shared out of the cascade module and index-hero consumes it. 26 cascade tests plus 10 new index-hero tests.

⏳ STILL OPEN, COUNTED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE:
  (a) WIDEN THE EDITABLE FIELDS to body copy and images. This is the half that needs COLUMNS, and it is deliberately not in the cascade PR: a new migration file makes every other open branch red under check:migrations --require-ledger until it merges, and four branches were open that night. Its own PR, when the tree is quieter.
  (b) AN OPERATOR SURFACE FOR THE SITE RUNG. The resolver reads '*' and the test covers it, but CONTENT_EDIT_ROUTES gates writes to real routes, so nothing can set it yet. One editor entry, not a schema change.
  (c) The cascade does NOT subsume the two hero ladders, and that is a finding rather than a gap. See ADR-1122's last-but-one section: they order DIFFERENT tables by ownership, deliberately in opposite directions (operator-owned browse surface vs host-owned entity). What was genuinely shared is now shared: the prefix loop and the page_content rung.

verify.evidence: Program phase. The shipped half is proven by lib/layout/content-cascade.test.ts (26 cases, every rung) plus lib/layout/index-hero.test.ts; the open half is (a) and (b) in the detail.

entries.title: Re-theme P7: per-Space / white-label theming depth
entries.detail:

entries.title: Re-theme P9: marketing ↔ in-app reconciliation — the brands already agree, the GATES did not
entries.detail:
Align the marketing brand system with the app tokens where they diverge.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

── ✅ RE-MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1123). THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THE ROW SHRANK. "Align the marketing brand system with the app tokens" assumes TWO systems. There is ONE, and what diverged was the GATES, not the brand.

MEASURED (marketing = app/(marketing)/** + components/marketing/**, 61 ts/tsx files, plus the marketing header/footer; in-app = app/(main)/** + components/**, 1,996 files):
  · Raw hex / text-[Npx] / inline rgb() on marketing: 🔴 ZERO, across all 61 files, with the check:tokens marketing exemption lifted. There was nothing for the exemption to protect.
  · Colour utility vocabulary: marketing uses a strict SUBSET of the one @theme inline map. Exactly 3 utility names appear on marketing and nowhere in-app (border-ink-border, text-ink-border, text-surface-elevated) and all three are app tokens. No marketing-only colour exists.
  · --color-marketing-canvas: DELIBERATE, and complete — overridden in every block that overrides --color-canvas (:root, .theme-light-lock, [data-skin=midnight], .dark, .dark [data-skin=midnight]). No skin gap.
  · Anton display face (font-display at 22x the in-app rate) and the .mk-band/.mk-beat/.mk-cont/.mk-tight rhythm: DELIBERATE. NOT flattened. check:headers and check:templates keep their marketing skips — those govern PAGE STRUCTURE, which genuinely differs.
  · Hand-rolled eyebrows: marketing 8 sites (0.13/file) vs in-app 463 (0.23/file). 🔴 IN-APP IS WORSE. Not a marketing divergence; P2/P3 debt.
  · Literal rounded-2xl over rounded-card: marketing 34 (0.53/file) vs in-app 717 (0.36/file). Marketing ~1.5x worse per file, but this is the repo-wide literal-radius ratchet (P1), not P9. Deliberately NOT folded in: a large invented row beats nothing.

THE TWO REAL GAPS, BOTH CLOSED HERE:
  1. check:tokens exempted app/(marketing)/ and components/marketing/ whole-tree, on the claim that marketing is "a separate brand design system". Measured at 0 violations — the exemption was the only artifact still asserting a second system existed. DELETED.
  2. check:contrast modelled the cream ground with ONE pair (--color-text) while the app canvas beside it carried five foregrounds. The marketing canvas is 5/255 DARKER in light mode, so every twin ratio is tighter and none had been measured. SEVEN pairs added (now 8 total): text-muted 5.21, text-subtle 4.79, primary-strong 4.75, focus-ring 3.34 all PASS in all five render states; border-strong 1.29, primary 2.19 and success 3.80 are waived at their measured floors.

🔴 THE FINDING THAT JUSTIFIES THE WHOLE ROW: components/marketing/comparison-table.tsx already pinned its ledger cards to bg-surface with the comment "a `yes` cell's `text-success` clears 4.5:1 on the surface tone and misses it on the canvas tone". That is exactly right (4.67 on a card, 4.05/3.80 on the cream) and it was true for as long as the comment existed, with the gate green the whole time, because the gate did not model that ground. The pair is now entered and frozen — the rank-gold treatment — so the fact is printed on every run instead of surviving only as a comment.

entries.title: DAWN Phase 3: the mechanical sweeps (2,004 sites, 91% raw <button>)
entries.detail:
RE-CENSUSED 2026-08-25 (the 2026-08-19 figure had itself expired). On the ratchet basis ({app,components,lib}/**/*.tsx, tests and the primitives themselves excluded, comments blanked by check-adoption's own corpus loader): 1,830 raw <button>, 168 <input>, 4 <select>, 2 <textarea> = 2,004 sites, against the row's claimed 2,072. Two of the row's four sub-figures were bare-grep drift. Select and textarea are DONE (both on their floors); input is not a sweep either. What is left is the button sweep and nothing else.

── HOW A SLICE IS CUT (ADR-1119, amended by ADR-1124). By SHAPE, not by directory: the set of raw <button> sites whose className is a NEAR-MISS for one `variant × size` of the Button primitive — every token the primitive emits for that pair is present, and every token the site carries is one the primitive's BASE already supplies. It is near-miss and NOT set-equality, because no raw <button> in the tree is set-equal to the primitive: BASE adds `tap-target`, `press` and `lift-1` on purpose. Converting GAINS those three, so EVERY SLICE MOVES RENDERED PIXELS — that is the program working, not a defect. The query is `scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs`; run it, do not re-derive it.

── SLICE 1 (dawn/phase3-slice-1, ADR-1119): the `primary × sm` class, 43 sites in 33 files.

── SLICE 2 SHIPPED 2026-08-25 (dawn/phase3-slice-2, ADR-1124): the `primary × md` class. MEASURED at 53 sites in 40 files, against slice 1's pre-sizing of 49 in 37 — the estimate did NOT hold, and 40 source files alone would have breached the 40-file CI ceiling. Cut to the 40 sites in 31 files that are NOT import-reachable from any surface test/e2e/visual.spec.ts photographs, so the slice cannot move a committed baseline. raw-button-bg 513 → 466, literal-radius 2291 → 2222. Because `primary × md` is the primitive's DEFAULT pair, every converted site is a bare <Button> with no className and no props.

── WHAT IS LEFT, WITH ITS ADDRESS. raw-button-bg = 466 (the ratcheted half) before slice 1 merges, 423 after both slices land. The two named residues are HYG-022 (2 sites the `primary × sm` slice left behind) and LIVE-114 (the 13 `primary × md` sites on watched surfaces). Beyond them the remaining population is mostly ghost/secondary fills, a different sweep: raw <button> overall is ~1,787 in 587 files, so ~74% of button sites carry no primary fill at all.

── UNPARKED 2026-08-20 (owner ruling): scheduled into the build-out; sequence in meta.slate.

entries.title: The `primary × sm` bucket is not empty: 2 sites survived slice 1 because they carry the primitive's own `lift-1`
entries.detail:
ADR-1119 asserted that slice 1 was exhaustive for `primary × sm` — "Slice 1's bucket reads 0". Re-run on origin/main at de6c218cd with the query now committed as scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs, the class reads 45 sites in 34 files, of which slice 1 takes 43 in 33. The 2 left behind are both in app/(main)/admin/marketing/deliverability/requeue-button.tsx, and the reason is instructive: they carry `lift-1`, which is part of what the primitive itself emits for the primary variant. They are CLOSER to the primitive than the 43 that were converted, and an unwritten query that treated any unrecognised token as a disqualifier read that as a reason to skip them.

The finding is not the 2 sites; it is that an exhaustiveness claim whose instrument is not in the repo cannot be re-run by a reviewer, by CI, or by the next agent — so it is a claim about an intent rather than about a set. scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs is the fix; this row is the debt it exposed. Fold these 2 into any later `primary × sm` pass; do not open a PR for them alone.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. The row said 'fold these 2 into any later primary × sm pass; do not open a PR for them alone', and the reason that instruction has now expired is that slice 1 HAS merged: `node scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs --variant primary --size sm` read 45 when this row was written and reads 2 today, both in app/(main)/admin/marketing/deliverability/requeue-button.tsx. There is no later pass to fold into — these two ARE the remainder, and the bucket now reads 0.
  BOTH BECOME `<Button size="sm">`, which is a straight token-for-token swap: BASE already carries inline-flex / items-center / gap-1.5 / font-semibold, SIZE.sm is exactly px-3 py-1.5 text-meta, and VARIANT.primary carries the bg / hover / text-on-primary / lift-1 the hand-rolled string spelled out. Three differences, all in the primitive's favour: `rounded-lg` becomes the skinnable `rounded-control` role radius, disabled opacity moves 60 → 50 to match every other button in the product, and both sites GAIN `tap-target`, `press` and the motion-reduce guard they never had.
  ONE BUTTON IN THAT FILE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT HAND-ROLLED and the file now says so: the discard control is a secondary/outline pair, and `dawn-bucket.mjs` tracks only primary × sm and primary × md, so no row measures it. Converting it here would have been a change nothing asked for and nothing would notice — the definition of widening. It comes with whatever pass claims it.
  The row's own point survives its closure and is worth keeping: the finding was never the 2 sites, it was that ADR-1119's exhaustiveness claim had no instrument in the repo, so nobody could re-run it. scripts/dawn-bucket.mjs is why this row could be measured today rather than argued about. Probe exits 0; adoption fell (raw-button-bg -2, literal-radius -3); tsc, lint, check:tokens and check:a11y-names all clean.

entries.title: Three instrument defects, and the third was blanking 121,627 characters of real markup
entries.detail: Found independently by two agents, which is what makes them findings rather than opinions. raw-input's lookahead excludes only type="hidden", so ~18 type="file" triggers behind hidden/sr-only are PERMANENTLY un-retirable debt inside a ratchet. And white-black-literals does not exclude app/print/**, though DAWN-CONVERSION §1 names it a carve-out, so its floor is permanently 2. Both mean a ratchet can never reach its true floor. Unscheduled, and it should not be.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17. The row named two defects and got both counts wrong; the third and worst was not in the row at all. (1) raw-input's lookahead: 37 concealed file triggers, not ~18, and 0 of the 37 are visible. (2) white-black-literals: the floor was permanently 27, not 2, and the sharper defect the row missed is that A TOTAL CANNOT TELL A CARVE-OUT FROM NEW DEBT — retire one annotated site, add one bare bg-white, and it reads 27 -> 27 '✅ held'. Now 0 with a per-site KEEP <utility>: <reason> escape, so the decisive case FAILS. (3) THE ONE NOBODY KNEW: stripComments treated a string literal as code, so a file input's accept glob ending slash-star opened a block comment that ran to the next close token — 121,627 characters of real markup blanked across 101 files, hiding 23 debt sites in 6 classes. A FALSE FALL: literal-radius read 2,281 against a 2,287 floor and printed '✅ shrank' while the true count was 2,292, a RISE. It also made fix (1) 40% inert, because the glob had already blanked the className that proves concealment. Five floors moved UP as a result — none is new design debt, all are sites the corpus was hiding, each recorded `rebased` and flagged on every run. Tests assert @2 is strictly un-blanking versus @1, so the corpus change can only reveal debt, never hide it.

entries.title: Nothing prevents the build cache overflowing again, because the gate that would is calibrated in the wrong units
entries.detail:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18, and the row changed shape rather than closing. THE SYMPTOM IS GONE: three consecutive production builds (18:46, 19:01, 19:09) uploaded 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling and every one logged 'Restored build cache from previous deployment'. No invalidation line anywhere. The 1.53 GB reading the row was filed on does not reproduce. WHAT IS STILL TRUE is the second half of the original row: nothing PREVENTS a recurrence. scripts/check-cache-budget.mjs was written for exactly that on 2026-08-17 and has never run on a real build. It was wired into postbuild in #2159 and TAKEN BACK OUT before merge, because the preview build of that change printed what no amount of reading could: 'TRIMMED the build cache before Vercel could reject it. What the build was about to hand back measured 2.40 GiB, over the 1.38 GiB trim point. drops the cheap half instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1520 MiB).' THE FLOOR ARM WAS RIGHT (node_modules 933 MiB, 27% clear of its 1.25 GiB budget, exactly as predicted). THE TRIM ARM IS CALIBRATED AGAINST THE WRONG QUANTITY: measure() sums RAW BYTES ON DISK and Vercel's ceiling applies to the PACKED archive. Raw 2.40 GiB versus a packed upload of 1.26-1.29 GB is about 2:1, not the ~3% the script's header assumes, because the Turbopack cache compresses hard and is the dominant term. Wired as-is it would delete a 1.5 GiB compiler cache on EVERY build to prevent an overflow that is not happening, turning a working warm cache into a guaranteed cold compile forever. TO CLOSE: fix the calibration (LIVE-048), then wire the gate in the SAME change as a preview build that prints it green. Do NOT close this row by deleting the guard or by declaring the symptom gone: the symptom being gone is why there is time to get the instrument right, not a reason to skip it.

STILL OPEN 2026-08-19, and the reason is now narrower than 'the gate is broken'. The gate is fixed (LIVE-048) and it is running on every production build, but in WARN-ONLY mode (LIVE-035): it measures and reports and cannot trim. So a cache heading for the 1.50 GB ceiling would be SEEN and named in the build log, and then nothing would stop it. Recurrence is now visible rather than prevented, which is a real improvement over nothing watching and is still not this row. It closes when the gate is promoted to blocking on the strength of a confirmed PACKED_PER_RAW.

Trend, read from production build logs on 2026-08-19: packed cache uploads of 1.26 GB across the day's deploys against the 1.50 GB ceiling, consistent with the 1.26 / 1.28 / 1.29 GB readings from 2026-08-18. Not rising.

THE PROBE ON THIS ROW WAS ITSELF WRONG, and the tree caught it the same day. It asked only whether check-cache-budget appears in postbuild. On 2026-08-19 it started appearing there in --warn-only mode, so the probe flipped to passing while the row stayed true: nothing prevents an overflow, it is merely reported now. That is the shape-not-truth failure four ADRs name, and a probe walked into it the first time the tree moved. Rewritten to measure the CONSEQUENCE -- the gate must be in postbuild AND not carry --warn-only AND still contain a delete path -- so it agrees with the row today and passes only when an overflow can actually be stopped.

HEADROOM RE-READ 2026-08-19 with the corrected constant, and it is tighter than this row assumed. Preview build 3jeNVZxuUy7thPjXpazjMC6yHwVo uploaded 1.32 GB against the 1.50 GB ceiling: 12% clear, not the 16% the 1.26 GB production reads implied. The cache is a single term, turbopack at 1459 MiB, so there is no second thing to trim if it grows. The gate now SEES this on every build and still cannot act on it.

🔴 FOUR PACKED READINGS TODAY, AND THE HEADROOM IS NARROWING:
    2026-08-18 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 production          1.26 GB   16% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2178)     1.32 GB   12% clear
    2026-08-19 preview (#2179)     1.35 GB   10% clear

⚠️ READ THAT CAREFULLY RATHER THAN AS A TREND LINE. The two production builds started COLD ('Build cache: <1 MB' on input), while the two previews compiled against a warm turbopack cache, so the 1.26 and the 1.35 are not the same measurement repeated. What IS comparable is the two previews, 8 minutes apart: turbopack went 1459 -> 1493 MiB, and those trees differed in what they compiled, so even that is one observation and not a rate.

What is NOT in doubt is the tightest true reading: 1.35 GB against a 1.50 GB ceiling is 10% clear, on a cache whose .next/cache half is a SINGLE term. If turbopack grows past roughly 1.65 GiB the whole cache is discarded, node_modules included, and the gate that would trim it first is deliberately unable to (warn-only, LIVE-035). That is this row, stated in numbers.

SIXTH READING, and it widens rather than tightens: preview xpkMNeSxJCWTTn35uvCeoacVbM7n uploaded 1.29 GB, 14% clear. The 8.7%-clear production figure from dpl_6FfMfAv7mHXQ3P2X3GmTxSCwDvEz remains the MAXIMUM observed and is still the number to plan against -- a preview that compiled less code is not evidence the ceiling moved. Recorded because the spread between same-day builds (1.26-1.37 GB) is now visibly dominated by what each build compiled, which is the reason this row still refuses to call any of it a trend line.

── CLOSED 2026-08-19 (owner: "Cache Budget: implement best practice"): the gate is calibrated in Vercel's units (PACKED_PER_RAW = 0.53, settled from a real paired reading: raw measure printed beside the same build's 'Uploading build cache' line, measured 0.5254, rounded toward firing early), the trim reaches only the named compiler-cache list (proven by mutation in scripts/check-cache-budget-trim.test.ts, including a reconstruction of the 2026-08-18 size-sorted mutant), loose top-level files are named in the composition and unreachable by the trim, and the gate runs BLOCKING in postbuild. The promotion landed in the same change as the preview build whose postbuild printed it green; the warn-only pin inverted with it.

entries.title: 20 route handlers are green by human assertion, and 11 of them claim `public`
entries.detail: check:authz now sees all 72 route handlers, but 52 are green because a gate was DETECTED and 20 because a human read them and said so. The ledger states this in its own header rather than hiding it, and pins each route's normalized-body digest so an edit forces a re-read — but a reason is not a proof. The sharp end is the three asserted `public` routes that touch the admin client: app/api/vitals, app/api/people/[handle]/vcard, app/api/llms.txt. Give each a per-route test pinning what it must never return, the way app/api/status/route.test.ts already pins its 'no secret' promise. The three asserted-public routes that touch the admin client now carry per-route tests: app/api/vitals, app/(main)/people/[handle]/vcard and app/llms.txt, 27 assertions between them. They pin what each must NEVER return rather than that it returns something - vitals writes profile_id NULL whatever the payload says, answers with an EMPTY body so the sink cannot echo a payload back, never reads headers or cookies, caps the batch and truncates the session id. VERIFIED ADVERSARIALLY, and the first attempt is worth recording: breaking the route to bank `profileId` did NOT fail the suite, which looked like a vacuous test. It was not - the attacker-shaped fixture sends `profile_id`, and re-running the break with that key failed exactly as it should ('expected 00000000-...-0001 to be null'). A break that does not fire is a claim about the TEST that has to be checked before it is believed.

entries.title: check:authz is file-level: it sees a gate is called, not that it runs on every path
entries.detail: LIVE-022 closed the VISIBILITY half — app/api/** was invisible because the classifier's first predicate required 'use server', which a Next 16 Route Handler never is. The granularity half is untouched and the guard's own header says so: it detects that a recognised gate is called SOMEWHERE in the file, not that it runs before every write on every path through every exported method. A route exporting GET and POST where only GET is gated reads as green. Stated here rather than left in an agent report, because an unrecorded limitation is how a partial gate comes to be read as full coverage (ADR-970).

verify.evidence: scripts/check-authz-guards.mjs header states the file-level limit explicitly. Confirmed 2026-08-17: the classifier tests src for gate tokens per FILE, with no per-export analysis.

entries.notes: Closed 2026-08-17 (ADR-1070). check:authz was FILE-level: it saw a gate called somewhere in the file, so an early return before the gate, a gate on one branch of an if, and a gated GET beside an ungated POST all read as green. It now requires EVERY exported HTTP method to pass three structural rules, following the body through a wrapper's local handler (27 cron routes) and into file-local helpers: R1 per-export, R2 the gate is not nested inside if/else/switch/catch, R3 no createAdminClient() query above the gate. R3 IS A DELIBERATE NARROWING AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. A literal 'any return before the gate' rule was tried against the real corpus first: it fires on 10 of the 52 gated handlers and all ten are validation (400 on a malformed body, 429 on rate limit, an empty list for a blank query). Shipping that would have been 100% false positives on day one, which is the ADR-970 shape - a guard that cannot fire honestly gets routed around and then reads as coverage. What is dangerous is not returning early, it is answering from the service-role client before you know who is asking, and that is what R3 measures. IT FOUND THREE REAL FALSE GREENS, each re-verdicted as a digest-pinned human reading: check-handle (auth.getUser inside an if, over a SECURITY DEFINER RPC) -> public; auth/callback (auth.getUser three branches deep in a swallowed analytics block; the real credential check is exchangeCodeForSession) -> token-credential; q/[slug] (service-role read of the code row before getMyProfileId, which answers WHO scanned, not MAY they) -> self-scoped. Counts moved 52 gated / 20 asserted to 49 / 23, and the standing 'the ledger must never outgrow the gated set' test still holds.

entries.title: Recapture the visual baselines the beta cutover and the skin fix deliberately changed
entries.detail: TWO deliberate changes moved pixels and both need a re-photograph; neither is a regression. (1) /pricing on ALL FOUR skins x desktop and mobile: the beta cutover removed the struck-through anchors, the beta captions and two FAQs, so the page is 258px shorter (18083 -> 17825) and pr-compare fails 8 of 80 with 72 passing. MEASURED in CI on f899596. (2) midnight-dark everywhere: LIVE-008 fixed a selector that could never match, so the skin now paints its real palette instead of the generic .dark one with midnight's LIGHT feel underneath — every midnight-dark baseline is a photograph of the wrong rendering. The @a11y run will also report white-on-#F0AD4E unwaived; the waiver was deliberately NOT pre-added, because that list records ratios axe actually reported and inventing one fabricates a measurement. Recapture by dispatching .github/workflows/e2e-manual.yml with base_url set to this branch's preview and update_baselines + capture_shell (the skin fix moves the SHELL as well as the marketing pages, which is the case that file's header says needs both flags), then update_a11y + capture_shell for the ratchet. Capturing in CI is not a workaround for a missing tool here — it is the only correct environment, because a baseline is only valid against a deployment of the same kind as the one pr-compare photographs.

verify.evidence: MEASURED in CI 2026-08-17 (pr-compare on cc3f6f5, run 32077852358): 80 visual checks PASSED, 0 failed, and 'App shell covered: 4/4 surfaces, 16/16 checks'. Recaptured by dispatching e2e-manual with update_baselines and WITHOUT capture_shell: the 8 failures were all /pricing across four skins x two viewports, and the shell was already passing 16/16, so capture_shell would have rewritten 16 good PNGs for nothing. The commit touched exactly 8 files, all /pricing, which is the failure set exactly. pr-compare is still red, but on the @a11y half only (8 midnight-dark contrast contexts, OWN-014) - the @visual half this row owns is green.

entries.notes: The row also claimed 'every midnight-dark baseline is a photograph of the wrong rendering'. THAT WAS NOT BORNE OUT: midnight-dark passed everywhere except /pricing, and /pricing failed on all four skins equally, which is the beta cutover shortening the page rather than a skin problem. The skin fix did change midnight-dark's palette, but the change was not pixel-visible on the captured surfaces - it surfaced as CONTRAST findings instead, which is OWN-014.

entries.title: 17 controls across 14 files had no accessible name, and nothing measured it
entries.detail: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-17 with a real TypeScript JSX parse and all eight naming paths the accessible-name computation actually has. The original figure was 143 'may have no accessible name'; the honest number is 17, in 14 files, out of 3,605 controls judged across 1,884 files. 126 of the 143 - 88% - were FALSE POSITIVES, because the first scan could not resolve label-WRAPPING components and could not read an element's CONTENTS; those two blind spots alone account for 2,091 correctly-named controls. All four files the row named as examples (circle-builder, practice-builder, block-edit-panel, search-overlay) contained ZERO real violations. The 17 were real: 13 icon-only buttons wrapping a bare lucide icon (announced as 'button' and nothing else), 2 sr-only file inputs, and 4 slug fields whose visible caption was a <span> rather than a <label> - exactly the class check:labels documents itself as unable to see. All 17 are fixed, so the guard ships at ZERO with no allowlist and no ratchet file: nothing to waive and nothing to quietly grow. Named by: 1,808 contents, 735 aria-label, 428 placeholder (weak), 283 wrapping label, 174 htmlFor, 105 title, 53 label prop, 13 spread (unknowable), 6 aria-labelledby.

Does not fire, same file and same icon, when named by visible text, by aria-labelledby, or by a wrapping native label. The guard already runs on every pull request from the ci.yml guards array, so re-running it here is duplicated work rather than independent evidence. The probe therefore asserts the PIN IS LIVE - the script exists, it has a test so something proves it can fire, package.json exposes it, and ci.yml's guards array names it - in milliseconds. Unwire it from CI and this row reopens.

entries.title: The beta rate is grantable per Space, privately, and no public surface moves
entries.detail: CODE HALF ONLY — OWN-024 is the owner half. spaces.beta_price_grant is a private flag ONLY the checkout reads. resolveLoadoutPriceId decides on the pure three-armed loadoutChargeArm: lock (re-bill the grandfathered locked_price_id) -> founding (the window is open OR this Space carries the grant) -> list. No expiry, because the grant is SPENT by the first successful checkout: the reconciler writes the charged price as the lock and arm 1 wins forever after, so revoking it later cannot raise anyone's rate. Read in its OWN PostgREST request rather than added to the existing space select, because an undeployed column fails the WHOLE request with 42703 — the profiles.email bug already recorded in that file. Fail-safe FALSE: unreadable means charge list, never less. The panel distinguishes not_deployed from granted:false and says 'Not available yet' instead of showing a toggle that would look enabled and quietly do nothing.
entries.notes: Proven by consequence: the test pins the EXACT set of prices a visitor is quoted across offering cards, JSON-LD, plan rows and the /pricing table, and asserts $19/$49/$190/$490 are absent. Five mutants each take it red. Mutant B — leaking the beta rate to /pricing — ESCAPED the first draft, which is why the sweep was widened to the surfaces reading effectiveCatalogAmounts rather than its display twin. Security posture measured rather than assumed: SELECT on spaces is column-level so a new column is invisible to anon/authenticated, but UPDATE is TABLE-level and the column inherits it; a column-level revoke cannot help, so the proposal states the condition to watch instead of pretending to close it.
