entries.title: All 18 Space micro-sites ship one link and it goes nowhere: the seeded "Get in touch" button is href="#"
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 in the same census as LIVE-110 (ADR-1115). All 18 Space micro-site documents in production carry exactly ONE link and it is the same dead one: the `SpaceCallout` block, labelled "Get in touch", `ctaHref: '#'`. A visitor on any Space page reaches the bottom of the page, reads a button that asks them to make contact, clicks it and stays exactly where they are.

IT IS SEEDED, NOT AUTHORED, which is why it is identical 18 times: lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143 ships `ctaHref: '#'` as the default. So there are two halves and shipping either alone leaves the bug live:
  • CODE — the template must seed a real destination, or seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set). The document already contains a `SpaceContact` block, so an in-page anchor to it is the smallest honest target.
  • DATA — the 18 documents already written keep '#' regardless; they need a document migration in the shape of 20270305000000.

Not urgent the way LIVE-110 is (a Space page has other paths to its owner) but it is the only link those pages have, and it is a button that lies.

── 🔴 PREMISE RE-TESTED 2026-08-25 AGAINST PRODUCTION BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN (ADR-1082, ADR-1125). `recaptureQuery` from scripts/stored-links.json was re-run against the live database and the result is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-24 capture on every axis: three stores, 4 / 1 / 18 documents, 8 / 5 / 18 hrefs set, 20 / 3 / 36 empty, and the same three targets at the same hit counts (/onboarding/beta 7+4, the absolute form 1+1, '#' 18). NO PREMISE HAD EXPIRED — all three rows are still true, which is the outcome ADR-1082 exists to establish either way.

⚠️ CORRECTED 1 — '18' IS EVERY SPACE THAT HAS A PAGE DOCUMENT, NOT EVERY SPACE. There are 20 spaces; 2 carry no `pageDocs` key, so they hold no stored link at all and will seed from the corrected template the first time they get one. The count is right; the scope needed a sentence.

🔴 CORRECTED 2 — THE ROW'S OWN REMEDY WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED, and this is the correction that mattered. The row says to "seed the callout with an empty ctaHref so the block draws no button at all (SpaceCallout, like MediaText, renders its CTA only when label and href are both set)". That is true of MediaText (media.tsx: `cta={ctaLabel && ctaHref ? … : undefined}`) and it was FALSE of SpaceCallout, which gated its button on `ctaLabel` ALONE and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`. An empty href fell straight back to '#'. Shipping the row exactly as written would have left all 18 buttons as dead as they started, behind a diff that looked like a fix. The renderer is the real defect.

⚠️ CORRECTED 3 — THREE SEEDING SITES, NOT ONE. The row names lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts:143. The block registry's own `defaultProps` seed '#' too, for BOTH `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA` (components/page-editor/blocks/profile.tsx), so a Callout dragged in from the palette shipped the same dead button. The old probe grepped ONE file and could not see the other two; the probe now covers all three.

── ✅ THE CODE HALF IS DONE (ADR-1125). SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now require BOTH a label and a destination before they draw a button — the MediaText rule applied to the two blocks that lacked it — and all three seeding sites emit '' instead of '#'. Proven by components/page-editor/blocks/profile.cta-href.test.tsx (9 tests) and negative-controlled: 7 of the 9 FAIL against origin/main and pass here; the 2 that pass on both are positive controls asserting a real href still renders.

⏳ THE DATA HALF IS STAGED AND DELIBERATELY UNAPPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270323000000_stored_doc_links_repair.sql. It rewrites the 18 seeded callouts to `#contact` — every one of the 18 documents contains a `SpaceContact` block and it renders inside `<section id="contact">` — but only for the 16 Spaces that have contact details to show. `SpaceContactBlock` returns null with no rows and its section carries `empty:hidden`, so for `danny-kenduck` and `templeofaset` (zero of address / hours / phone / email / website, measured 2026-08-25) `#contact` would be a second dead button in a new costume; those two get '' and, now the renderer is fixed, draw no button at all. THIS ROW STAYS OPEN UNTIL THE OWNER APPLIES THE MIGRATION AND THE CENSUS IS RE-CAPTURED, which is the correct reading rather than a shortfall: scripts/check-stored-blocks.mjs settled this exact question for its own probe — "a probe that went green on the declared state would close a row whose work has not happened". The census arm is still red, on purpose. ── 🔴 RE-MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, AND THE CENSUS THIS ROW'S PROBE READS WAS STALE. scripts/stored-links.json carried capturedAt 2026-08-25 while its BODY still held the 2026-08-24 reading, so the probe went on agreeing with `open` from a snapshot that no longer described production. That is precisely the failure HYG-023 names — the census has no checker and no freshness rule, so a date can move without the data moving with it. Re-captured from live. ✅ CLOSED, AND IT LANDED EXACTLY AS THE OWNER RULED IT SHOULD ON 2026-08-25 (anchor to the in-page contact block) — the work was already shipped when the ruling was made. Both halves hold: the CODE half seeds ctaHref empty in lib/page-editor/templates/space-default.ts and SpaceCalloutBlock now requires BOTH a label and a destination, so a new Space draws no button until its operator points it somewhere; and the DOCUMENT half is done — all 18 stored Space micro-sites now carry ctaHref '#contact', 16 set hrefs, ZERO at '#'. #contact is the right target and is stable: SpaceContact renders inside <section id="contact">, the anchor lib/spaces/section-anchors.ts names canonically for the derived profile menu.

entries.title: SiteHeader has no phone navigation at all, so /discover/* and /help offer a visitor nothing but a CTA

source.ref: the comment at the PrimaryNav call

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24 while fixing LIVE-106, and it is the LARGER surface of the two. components/layout/site-header.tsx renders PrimaryNav, which is `hidden md:block`, and unlike MarketingHeader it renders NO mobile sheet - its own comment says so: 'Desktop only; mobile relies on the prominent CTA + footer nav until a drawer ships.' So on every /discover/* page and every /help page, a phone visitor has a wordmark, a search glyph and a CTA, and no header navigation whatsoever. That is the public browse surface the sitemap advertises. ── IT IS NOW CHEAP: MarketingMobileMenu is a pure projection of a ResolvedMenu (ADR-1118), takes `headerMenu` + `light`, and SiteHeader already fetches the same `headerMenu`. The open questions are taste, not architecture: the dark variant over a hero, and whether the sheet crowds the mobile search glyph. Deliberately NOT bundled into ADR-1118 - it is a different component with its own header-fit contract and its own visual baselines.

── ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Owner ruled the shape in two steps: reuse the marketing sheet rather than build a second one, keep the mobile search glyph, and make it viewer-aware.
  WHAT LANDED: SiteHeader renders MarketingMobileMenu below md on the server-auth path and a new ViewerMobileMenu on the client-auth path, both fed the same DB-backed `headerMenu` PrimaryNav gets. ViewerMobileMenu mirrors ViewerPrimaryNav exactly — same useViewer hook, same viewerRoleFor collapse — so on a statically-rendered /discover page the sheet and the bar agree about who is looking once /api/viewer answers, and agree before it too (both render the anonymous view, which is the HTML a crawler gets).
  THE VIEWER-AWARE HALF IS TWO SEPARATE PROPS, and keeping them separate is deliberate — it mirrors PrimaryNav, which already keeps `viewerRole` apart from `isAuth`. `viewer` gates the nav rows; `isAuth` decides only the footer. A janitor previewing as a visitor carries viewerRole 'visitor' AND isAuth true, and both readings are correct at once: hide what a visitor cannot see, and do not offer to sign in someone who already is.
  A SECOND DEFECT THE ROW DID NOT NAME, found while wiring it: the sheet's footer was an unconditional "Sign in" + join-the-beta pair. On MarketingHeader that is right, because the marketing chrome is always logged-out. On SiteHeader it would have invited a signed-in member to sign in, and then to join a beta they are already in — copy that tells a member the product does not know them. The footer now branches: signed in gets one "Your feed" link.
  MarketingHeader's own call is BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged (both new props are optional and default to the visitor reading it always had), which is what its existing test pins by exact string — that test passing unmodified is the proof this is additive.
  PROVEN BY: marketing-mobile-menu.test.ts, 12 cases. The behavioural arm drives sheetGroups with a member-gated menu and asserts a visitor sees ['/pub'] where a member sees ['/pub','/mem']. The wiring arms are source-shape on purpose and for the reason stated above sheetGroups: the sheet only mounts on a tap and `pnpm test` has no browser — and both defects LIVE-106 found were wiring, a prop never passed and a projection that dropped children. check:adoption held, check:a11y-names 3576 controls named, check:labels green. ADR-1158.

── 🔴 RE-OPENED THE SAME DAY. THE CODE LANDED, THE PROBE PASSED, AND THE BUTTON DOES NOT RENDER. This row was marked done on its `cmd` probe, which greps components/layout/site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` and `headerMenu={headerMenu}`. Both strings are present, so the probe passes. The probe measures SOURCE; the consequence this row is about is a button on a phone. That gap is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs, committed here in the cleanest possible form: a probe that passes by existing.
  WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is not ambiguous:
  • A baseline capture (e2e-manual run #53, update_baselines, no capture_shell) ran against the branch preview at 18:57-19:04Z. `/api/status` on that alias returns commit `f1b832a`, the commit carrying this change, and the /discover mobile shot ran at 19:04:24 — well after the deployment was serving. So the build under test HAD the change.
  • The run captured 128 surfaces and committed NOTHING: `No baseline changes to commit.` The /discover mobile PNG is byte-identical to the one taken before this change.
  • The committed `discover--dawn-light-mobile.png` header strip shows wordmark, search glyph, "Sign in", "Start a Circle" — and no hamburger. Exactly the state this row was opened about.
  • POSITIVE CONTROL, which is what makes the reading safe: `about--dawn-light-mobile.png` — the same suite, same viewport, same run — DOES show the hamburger, because MarketingHeader has had one since ADR-1118. So the suite renders and photographs this control when it is there.
  ⚠️ A SECOND SIGNAL POINTS THE SAME WAY AND IS WORTH RECORDING: surfaces.ts documents at length that /discover's MOBILE height drifts between requests, because six live queries feed it and three are order- or clock-sensitive. A recapture 20 hours after the baseline returning byte-identical output is itself odd, and whatever explains that may also explain the missing button — the two may be one fact, not two.
  🔵 NOT YET EXPLAINED, and stated as unexplained rather than guessed: the JSX is present and correct at the end of SiteHeader, `tsc` and `lint` are clean, app/discover/layout.tsx does render `<SiteHeader variant="light" authMode="client" />`, ViewerMobileMenu mirrors ViewerPrimaryNav (which DOES render), and the wrapper is `md:hidden` against a 390px capture viewport. Hypotheses NOT yet tested: a stale prerender served from a restored build cache; the header's flex fit at 390px with search + Sign in + CTA + a new 40px control; something specific to the client-auth path. Reading the deployed HTML is the next step and the container's egress could not reach it (the preview is SSO-gated and the one-shot share token is per-path).
  🔴 THE PROBE MUST CHANGE WITH THE FIX. A source grep cannot close this row — it already did once. The honest gate is the visual suite: this row closes when a /discover MOBILE recapture MOVES, with the /about control still showing its own hamburger in the same run.

── THE PROBE ITSELF IS NOW THE RECORD OF THE MISTAKE. `check:backlog` fails BOTH ways, so re-opening this row made it fail as 'says OPEN, tree says DONE' — the guard insisting the probe is right and the status wrong. It is the other way round, and that is the whole lesson: the probe was a grep of components/layout/site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` and `headerMenu={headerMenu}`, which is satisfied by the change EXISTING rather than by it working. AGENTS.md: a row a repo cannot probe is `manual` with evidence, and this consequence — a control visible on a 390px viewport of a deployed build — genuinely is not reachable from `pnpm test`, which has no browser. So it becomes manual rather than keeping a gate that already produced one false close. The retired probe, kept here so nobody restores it as an improvement: `node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='components/layout/site-header.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(!/MobileMenu/.test(t)){console.error('SiteHeader still renders no phone navigation, so /discover/* and /help have no header nav below md');process.ex`

── ✅ RE-CLOSED 2026-08-25 ON DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE, AND THE RE-OPEN ABOVE WAS WRONG ABOUT THE FACT WHILE BEING RIGHT ABOUT THE PROBE. The button renders. Production `/discover` at commit 06bf0e5 serves, immediately after the auth cluster:
    <div class="shrink-0 md:hidden"><button type="button" aria-label="Open menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="dialog" class="rounded-lg p-2 transition-colors text-text hover:bg…
  Exactly one occurrence of `Open menu` and exactly one `md:hidden` in the whole document, on both /discover and /discover/topics. The change works and always did.
  🔴 SO WHAT DID THE BASELINE CAPTURE ACTUALLY SAY? NOTHING. `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` in playwright.config.ts, against a /discover mobile page that is 390 x 9675 = 3,773,250 pixels. Two percent of that is **75,465 pixels** of permitted drift. A 40 x 40 hamburger is 1,600 pixels — **2.1% of the allowed budget, 0.042% of the page.** `pnpm test:e2e:update` runs `playwright test --update-snapshots`, which rewrites a snapshot only when the comparison FAILS. The comparison passed under tolerance, so nothing was rewritten and the job printed `No baseline changes to commit`.
  I read that line as a NEGATIVE RESULT. It is not a result at all — it is the gate declining to have an opinion. The /about positive control was real and correct (its hamburger IS in its baseline, because that baseline was captured after ADR-1118 ADDED it, not because the gate can detect one being added). Two true observations, one false conclusion drawn from their conjunction.
  WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: the probe was still wrong. A grep of site-header.tsx for `MobileMenu` passes on a change that exists, and would have passed equally on one that did not render. The evidence that settles this row is the served HTML, and the verify block now names that rather than a source string. Being right for the wrong reason is not being right. The instrument gap this exposed is LIVE-125.

verify.evidence: Settled 2026-08-25 on the SERVED HTML, not on source and not on the visual suite. Production /discover and /discover/topics at commit 06bf0e5 each contain exactly one `aria-label="Open menu"` inside `<div class="shrink-0 md:hidden">`, immediately after the auth cluster, and exactly one `md:hidden` in the document. The desktop /discover baseline independently shows ViewerPrimaryNav rendering (Home / Community / The Quest / The Lab / Spaces / About), which confirms the client-auth path and ViewerProvider both work on this tree. 🔴 The @visual suite is NOT evidence either way here: maxDiffPixelRatio 0.02 on a 390x9675 page permits 75,465 pixels of drift and a 40x40 control is 1,600 — see LIVE-125. Re-verify by fetching the page and grepping for the aria-label, never by grepping the component.

entries.title: Editor E0 task 9: upgradeLayout enters the read path
entries.detail:
lib/entity-blocks/node-tree.ts ships upgradeLayout - pure, total, idempotent, deterministic, and proven over the 37 frozen production shapes in scripts/entity-layout-corpus.json (ADR-1129). Nothing calls it. Task 9 calls it at the top of parseEntityLayout, which is EDITOR-E0 §1.5's stated safe halfway point: every reader becomes node-shaped and nothing is written.

What to expect, so it is not mistaken for a bug:
  • layout-equal.ts is a BYTE comparison and powers the 'unpublished changes' badge, so every Space reads dirty exactly once. Harmless, but it will be noticed.
  • layout-equal.test.ts:94-111 asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of actions.ts, so it fails on any rename.
  • upgradeLayout is deliberately MORE permissive than parseRows in one way - it preserves a block type the registry no longer knows (ADR-978), leaving legality to sanitizeRows / resolveRows, which run after. Keep that property; do not 'fix' it by dropping unknown types at the upgrade.
  • EntityLayout gains the node shape here; the sibling content/style maps are NOT removed until task 11.

Not a migration. All five stores are opaque JSONB and §1.6 rules a SQL transform out (the transform needs the registry, and SQL does not have it). ✅ DONE 2026-08-25. `parseEntityLayout` calls `upgradeLayout(raw)` at the top and attaches the result as a read-path-only `EntityLayout.nodes`. 🔴 TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN NOTES WERE WRONG, both re-measured before the work: (1) `layout-equal.ts` is NOT a byte comparison - it was rewritten to compare the RENDER (`layoutRenderKey` -> `resolveRows` + content + style) and its own header calls the byte version 'THE BUG THIS EXISTS FOR'; and (2) the 'unpublished changes' badge does not go through `parseEntityLayout` at all - it compares raw `profileLayoutDraft` vs `profileLayout` on the stored preferences (owner-space-layout-preview.tsx). So NO Space reads dirty, not even once. The row's prediction should not be looked for. (3) The section reference was also off: §1.5/§1.6 are in docs/EDITOR-E0.md, not EDITOR-ARCHITECTURE.md. ⚠️ THE REAL HAZARD WAS ELSEWHERE AND IT IS ORDERING: `upgradeLayout` returns NON-NULL for every object, so attaching `nodes` before the emptiness gate makes `parseEntityLayout` never return null - disarming `?? starterEmailLayout()` on two LIVE email send paths, which would compile an empty body. The gate runs first and a test pins it. A second test pins that `sanitizeEntityLayout` (the WRITE path) never carries `nodes` through, which caught a real mistake during this very change. A third pins the ADR-978 divergence: `rows` drops a de-registered type and `nodes` preserves it, on purpose.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='lib/entity-blocks/layout.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const s=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');const i=s.indexOf('export function parseEntityLayout');if(i<0){console.error('parseEntityLayout is gone from '+F);process.exit(79)}const j=s.indexOf(String.fromCharCode(10)+'}',i);const body=j>i?s.slice(i,j):'';if(body.indexOf('upgradeLayout(')<0){console.error('parseEntityLayout does not call upgradeLayout - the read path is still block-id shaped');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.title: Seven block renderers still draw a button at '#' when the operator leaves the destination blank
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while working LIVE-109 (ADR-1125). The 18 dead Space buttons had a root cause one level below the seed the row blamed: `SpaceCalloutBlock` gated its button on `ctaLabel` alone and rendered `href={ctaHref || '#'}`, so an operator who typed a label and left the link box empty got a button that went nowhere — and blanking the seed could not have removed it. That is fixed for `SpaceCallout` and its twin `SpaceCTA`. THE SAME SHAPE SURVIVES IN SEVEN MORE PLACES, all in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx (lines 200, 203, 496, 514, 526, 623, 711), and four of them say so in their own comments: "a missing link falls back to '#' until the operator sets one".

⚠️ NOT ALL SEVEN ARE THE SAME BUG, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A TRIAGE ROW RATHER THAN A SWEEP. Three (496, 514, 526) sit behind `safeHref()`, so '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to — a deliberate stored-XSS fallback that must not be removed, only separated from the empty-field case. The other four (200, 203, 623, 711) are the plain LIVE-109 shape. Two further sites in profile.tsx (290, 2349) are NOT in scope: their href comes from live identity data, not an authored text field.

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE, and said plainly so the row is not read as an outage: the census (scripts/stored-links.json) records no '#' target in either marketing store, so no stored marketing document trips this today. It is one blank field away in the editor, on any of the seven.

THE DURABLE FIX IS AN EDITOR ONE and belongs with the PROG-E series rather than here: a link field that offers the page's real anchors and routes instead of a free-text box cannot be left in a state that renders '#'. This row is the interim — make the renderers decline to draw a button they cannot point anywhere, the way MediaText, SpaceCallout and SpaceCTA now do. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1147). Six renderers in components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx now require BOTH a label and a destination, and the seventh was a FALSE POSITIVE worth recording: the card title link at ~496 already sat inside `safeHref(card.href) ? …`, so its `|| '#'` was DEAD CODE the type checker forced rather than a route any visitor could reach. It is gone too, so the site stops reading as a seventh instance. ⚠️ THE THREE BEHIND safeHref() ARE NOT A SEPARATE CASE, which is what made this a triage row: '#' is ALSO what an unsafe url degrades to there, and withholding the link is the correct answer to BOTH — a blocked destination and a missing one are equally not somewhere to send someone. One wrapper bug went with it: `hasActions` counted LABELS, so withholding every button still drew the empty mt-8 action row and left a gap under the copy; it now counts buttons that will actually render. components/page-editor/blocks/design.cta-href.test.tsx adds 11 arms, the twin of the profile file from ADR-1125, including an UNSAFE-url arm proving the two cases converge. Mutation-proven three ways.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='components/page-editor/blocks/design.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const t=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(!/CtaButton/.test(t))process.exit(79);const strip=s=>s.split('\n').filter(l=>!/^\s*(\/\/|\/\*|\*)/.test(l)).join('\n');const hits=[...strip(t).matchAll(/href=\{[^}]*\|\|\s*\x27#\x27\}/g)];if(hits.length){console.error(hits.length+' renderer(s) in '+F+' still fall back to href \x27#\x27, so a button with no destination is drawn rather than withheld');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in the renderer — a button whose href degrades to '#' — not the row's title, and not the seed values (LIVE-109 owns those). Comment lines are stripped first so prose describing the defect cannot hold the row open. Reads 7 today; passes at 0. The three safeHref() sites must be RESOLVED rather than deleted: '#' is also their stored-XSS degradation path, so the fix separates 'unsafe url' from 'empty field' instead of dropping the fallback.

entries.title: 24 IndexTemplate pages still have no hero band, and adopting one is a layout change on every one of them
entries.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF PROG-P4 2026-08-25 (ADR-1127), because it is the half that CHANGES WHAT RENDERS. 24 files still compose IndexTemplate with no hero band: app/(help)/help/page.tsx, app/(help)/help/[category]/page.tsx, /circles/templates, /crew/leaderboard, /drafts, /housing/roommates, /lead/training-library, /market/manage, /messages, /orders, /partners, /partners/collaborators, /partners/join, /search, /spaces/[slug]/journeys, /spaces/[slug]/loom, /spaces/[slug]/manage/circles, /spaces/[slug]/podcasts, /spaces/[slug]/practices, /spaces/operating, /support, /discover/partners, /discover/practices, /discover/practices/pillar/[slug].

Adopting is mechanically one line each (`const hero = await resolveIndexHero(route)` + `{...hero}`), but it is NOT a no-op the way PROG-P5's detail adoption is: resolveIndexHero always returns heroOverlay: true, so an unmapped route gets a LARGE GRADIENT BAND and the page's h1 moves onto it. Contrast detail-hero.ts, whose unmapped tail is 'none' — an adoption there is invisible until the section is mapped. So each of the 24 needs an INDEX_HERO_DEFAULTS row FIRST, classifying it discovery (large + a section cover) or utility (short + the gradient), per the short/large product decision already written into that map.

Three things to settle in that PR, not here:
  (a) Whether the index ladder should grow a 'none' tail like the detail one, so adoption can be staged. If it does, this row shrinks to adding map rows.
  (b) The /spaces/[slug]/* tab pages (5 of the 24) sit INSIDE a Space profile that already has its own hero above them; a second band may be wrong there regardless of size.
  (c) Visual baselines move on every surface adopted. Expect pr-compare diffs and re-baseline deliberately.

entries.title: Retire DISCOVER_NAV: a hand-maintained parallel nav list nothing renders any more
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-24. Its last renderer was the marketing phone sheet, which now projects the `header` menu instead (ADR-1118), so DISCOVER_NAV is exported, tested, and drawn by nothing. All five of its links (/discover, /discover/circles, /discover/events, /discover/journeys, /discover/topics) are rows of the nav registry already. It is exactly the second-source shape lib/nav exists to retire. ── NOT deleted in ADR-1118 on purpose: three ADRs (ADR-352 area, ADR-352 area, and the OPEN-THREADS B4 note) name it as a CONCEPT - 'the shared community core' the public and in-app navs were meant to keep in sync - so retiring it is a small ruling about whether that concept still has a job, not a drive-by deletion inside a PR about phone reachability. Removing it also touches lib/site.test.ts, which has four cases pinned to it.

── ✅ RETIRED 2026-08-25, AND THE RULING IS THE INTERESTING PART. The row said correctly that this is a small ruling, not a drive-by deletion: the record (ADR-352 on the shared mega menu, plus the OPEN-THREADS B4 note) name DISCOVER_NAV as a CONCEPT — "the shared community core", the surfaces the public menu and the in-app nav were meant to keep in sync.
  THE RULING: the concept keeps its job and loses its implementation, because the implementation was the weakest possible way to do that job. Keeping two navs in sync was the goal, and a SECOND hand-kept list only achieves it while someone remembers to edit both. All five destinations are rows of the one nav registry every header already projects, so they are now in sync BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline. That is the concept being honoured, not abandoned. Its last renderer was the marketing phone sheet, which has projected the `header` menu since ADR-1118, so by 2026-08-24 the export was tested and drawn by nothing.
  THE FOUR TESTS MOVED RATHER THAN WENT, and that is what keeps this honest. Deleting them alongside the export would have quietly dropped the guard on the concept — which is exactly how a retirement turns into a regression nobody notices. lib/site.test.ts now asks the SAME five destinations of NAV_REGISTRY: /discover, /discover/circles, /discover/events, /discover/journeys, /discover/topics. A list nothing renders cannot drift in a way anyone notices; the registry can, and now says so. 19 cases green in that file, tsc clean.
  Reversible in one commit: the removed block is quoted in full in the migration-note comment left at its old site in lib/site.ts.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='lib/site.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);if(/export const DISCOVER_NAV/.test(fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8'))){console.error('lib/site.ts still exports DISCOVER_NAV, a second hand-maintained nav list beside the one registry');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Probes for the export that must be GONE, which is the consequence itself: while it exists there are two declarations of the same five destinations and either can drift. Not a grep for the row's title words.

entries.title: The weekly job can see menu drift; the operator standing in the Menu manager still cannot

source.ref: no per-item drift state anywhere in components/admin/menu/

entries.detail: PULLED OUT OF HYG-010 2026-08-25: it sat inside a clause about 'menu polish' and it is a feature, not a badge. ADR-860 asked for three things and TWO AND A HALF have shipped: syncMenuFromDefaults is the non-destructive re-check (lib/menus/actions.ts:459), identity rides `synced_default_keys` (20260801140000), and LIVE-107 added scripts/maintenance/menu-drift.mjs on the weekly sweep. What is still missing is the half that faces a PERSON: nothing in components/admin/menu/ shows an operator, per item, whether it is SYNCED (matches the code default), EDITED (label/subheading/gating diverged), RETIRED (its href is in synced_default_keys with no live row, so the inserts-only sync will NEVER resurrect it) or MISSING (a new default the next sync will inject). 🔴 A WEEKLY CI JOB IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE, and LIVE-107 is the proof rather than the refutation: the mislabelled 'Spaces directory' row was created BY AN OPERATOR IN THIS EDITOR, and the person who created it had no way to see that the row they were editing had left its default behind. A weekly job tells a maintainer afterwards; a drift column tells the author at the moment of the edit. Why it is S and not XS: the classification is a pure function of (resolved menu, defaultMenu(surfaceKey), synced_default_keys), but the third input is DB state the 900-line client editor does not receive, so the fix threads a prop from the server page as well as rendering the state. Do the derivation in lib/menus/ where it can be tested without a browser, and reuse menu-drift.mjs's comparison rather than writing a second one that can disagree with it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const E='components/admin/menu/menu-groups-editor.tsx';if(!fs.existsSync(E))process.exit(79);if(!fs.existsSync('lib/menus/drift.ts')){console.error('no lib/menus/drift.ts: the synced/edited/retired/missing derivation does not exist');process.exit(1)}if(!/synced_default_keys/.test(fs.readFileSync('lib/menus/drift.ts','utf8'))){console.error('lib/menus/drift.ts does not read synced_default_keys, so it cannot tell RETIRED from MISSING');process.exit(1)}if(!/menus\\/drift/.test(fs.readFileSync(E,'utf8'))){console.error('the Menu manager does not consume the drift derivation, so no operator can see it');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence in two halves: the derivation must exist AND read the field that distinguishes a retired default from a new one, and the manager must actually consume it. A derivation nobody renders is the shape-not-truth failure this list names, and it is the exact state the row is complaining about, since menu-drift.mjs already computes most of this for a cron nobody is looking at.

entries.title: pages.space_id can take its NOT NULL contract step: the ruling it waited on has an empty subject

source.ref: the column comment at :93 says 'Still NULLABLE (no NOT NULL contract step yet)'

entries.detail:
PULLED OUT OF HYG-010 2026-08-25. The item had sat as 'info-grade' behind a stated blocker — 'needs the untenanted-rows ruling' — and the blocker has NO SUBJECT: `public.pages` holds 4 rows and 0 of them have a null space_id (measured against the live database, 2026-08-25). That is the ADR-1082 pattern: a blocker phrased as a pending decision, where the thing to be decided does not exist. Nothing needs ruling on; the column can simply take the constraint. It is safe by construction as well as by count: every read and write goes through lib/page-editor/data.ts, which defaults spaceId to loadRootSpaceId(), and space_id already carries `on delete cascade`. 🔴 SHIP IT ALONE, NOT INSIDE A SWEEP. Merging deploys to production (AGENTS.md), and a NOT NULL that finds an unexpected row fails the migration and the deploy with it — so this wants its own PR, re-counting the untenanted rows immediately before it goes, not a line in somebody else's diff. Update the column comment in the same change: it currently states the opposite.

── ✅ SHIPPED 2026-08-25 as migration 20270341000000, alone, exactly as this row demanded. Re-counted immediately before writing it (a count taken a week ago is a guess): public.pages holds 4 rows, 0 untenanted. Applied to production and verified — information_schema now reports is_nullable = NO — and the ledger version was repaired to match the filename.
  THE COLUMN COMMENT WAS UPDATED IN THE SAME CHANGE, which the row asked for and which mattered more than it sounds: it read 'Still NULLABLE (no NOT NULL contract step yet)'. A comment asserting the opposite of what is true is worse than no comment, because it is documentation that gets believed. It now records the constraint, why the application cannot produce an untenanted row (lib/page-editor/data.ts defaults spaceId to loadRootSpaceId() on every write), and that the unique key's NULLS NOT DISTINCT clause is now inert rather than wrong.
  TWO CONTROLS, and the first is deliberately NOT a safety device. A NOT NULL fails on a null all by itself, so the before-arm exists to make that failure LEGIBLE — a bare 'column contains null values' names neither the count nor the table's size, and whoever reads a failed production deploy should not have to go and query for both. The after-arm is the one that catches a subtler thing: an ALTER on an already-NOT-NULL column also succeeds, so without it this migration could read as having done work it did not do.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const D='supabase/migrations';if(!fs.existsSync(D))process.exit(79);const files=fs.readdirSync(D).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.sql'));if(files.length<50)process.exit(79);const re=/alter\\s+table\\s+(?:only\\s+)?public\\.pages\\s+alter\\s+column\\s+space_id\\s+set\\s+not\\s+null/i;const hit=files.filter(f=>re.test(fs.readFileSync(D+'/'+f,'utf8').replace(/^\\s*--.*$/gm,'')));if(!hit.length){console.error('no migration makes public.pages.space_id NOT NULL');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the tree consequence: one ALTER TABLE public.pages statement that sets the constraint, comment lines stripped first. The first draft matched any migration that mentioned public.pages AND set space_id NOT NULL anywhere, and passed on 20260920000000_library_dam.sql, which does both about DIFFERENT tables. The DB half is re-counted by hand at ship time, which is why the row says so.

entries.title: check:authz is per-export for route handlers and still whole-file for 'use server' actions

source.ref: gateSoundness — one soundness model, both scans

entries.detail: PULLED OUT OF HYG-010 2026-08-25 (filed on #2267) with its expected yield measured first. CLOSED the same day (ADR-1135): the ACTION scan now judges every export of a 'use server' admin-client file on its own, through the SAME gateSoundness (R1 per-export / R2 dominance / R3 precedence) the route scan uses — parametrised, not duplicated. The row's diagnosis was one layer off: vocabulary (contactsOwnerId, now in ACTION_GATE) explained ~19 of the 112 naive false positives; ~90 were bodyAfterParams reading a guard helper's braced RETURN TYPE as its body (requireMarketer(): Promise<{ id: string } | string>), and the rest were maskLiterals lexer holes (regex literals, nested template interpolations) that could hide real exports from BOTH scans. R3 was sharpened once for both scans (a pre-gate admin query fires only when it can mutate or a pre-gate return is not denial-shaped) instead of annotating 16 sound lookup-then-gate exports — the ADR-970 boundary held: no allowlist. Final yield 5: one real gap fixed (activeSeasonJourneys now behind requireCurator), the row's predicted stopActingAsMember plus stashPendingInduction / conciergeTurn / startBuild carry per-export authz-ok reasons. entries.title: The visual suite's surfaces are inherited from the page editor, so most of the tree is unwatched and reads as covered

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='test/e2e/surfaces.ts';if(!fs.existsSync(S))process.exit(79);const src=fs.readFileSync(S,'utf8');const admin=new Set((src.match(/'\\/admin[^']*'/g)||[]));if(admin.size<6){console.error('the visual suite watches '+admin.size+' operator route(s); its surfaces still come from EDITABLE_PAGES, which is the page editor\\'s list, not a coverage list');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by PROG-DAWN3 slice 1 (ADR-1119), and found the only way it could be — by a sweep moving pixels and CI mostly not noticing. Slice 1 changed 37 sites; EXACTLY ONE of them rendered on a surface the visual suite watched (the event approval controls, mounted by the space console), and that one produced 4 real failures. The other 36 moved with nothing looking at them, so the run's '140 passed' was never evidence the sweep held still.

THE CAUSE WAS STRUCTURAL. test/e2e/visual.spec.ts took its surfaces from test/e2e/surfaces.ts, which parsed EDITABLE_PAGES out of lib/page-editor/data.ts at run time plus one hand-maintained extra ('/discover'). EDITABLE_PAGES exists to say WHICH PAGES THE PAGE EDITOR MAY EDIT, so the camera pointed wherever an unrelated product decision happened to point it. Measured 2026-08-25: ZERO '/admin' literals in the file, i.e. no operator surface in the product was visually watched at all.

── CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1128). The visual suite now has its OWN list, coverageSurfaces(), with three inputs: the parsed EDITABLE_PAGES routes (the parse was never the bug — Lift 5c conversions must keep joining automatically, so it stays as ONE INPUT), the public extras, and OPERATOR_PATHS — seven /admin routes chosen by CENSUS, not by taste. scripts/visual-surface-census.mjs is committed so the argument re-runs. Measured on the tree AFTER slice 1 landed, so these are live numbers and not pre-sweep ones: 99 of the repo's 463 frozen raw-button-bg sites (21.4%) and 518 of its 1,799 raw <button> tags (28.8%) live in app/(main)/admin/** + components/admin/**, and the seven picked routes hold 47/98 and 256/481 of what all 92 static admin routes can be credited with — 48% of the operator raw-button-bg and 53% of its buttons for 7.5% of the routes, at ~1.5 minutes of added runner time per pixel-moving PR. The share is stable under a sweep: slice 1 retired 43 sites repo-wide and the operator share of raw <button> did not move off 28.8%, which is what makes this structural rather than a snapshot.

THE MEASUREMENT HAD ITS OWN TRAP AND THE ADR RECORDS IT: a FULL transitive import closure credits fourteen unrelated admin routes with the same 71 debt-bearing files, because a registry deep in the graph imports most of the product. An import is not a render, so the census basis is deliberately shallow (route directory + two import hops) and every number is stated as an UPPER BOUND.

WHAT WAS CUT, NAMED RATHER THAN TRUNCATED SILENTLY: the other 85 static admin routes (368 captures, ~18 min/PR, for the remaining 51 sites), every dynamic route (no stable seeded id survives a new preview hostname — the app-room failure), the seeder/demo consoles, and the @a11y + overflow suites (an operator surface with no a11y-baselines.json row is held to $defaultMax, so widening those needs its own seeded capture — HYG-027).

🔴 NOT MERGEABLE UNTIL THE BASELINES ARE CAPTURED ON A RUNNER: e2e-manual.yml → workflow_dispatch → base_url=<preview>, capture_shell ✔, update_baselines ✔ writes the 28 admin* PNGs. The operator surfaces ride the SAME PW_STORAGE_STATE as the member shell (no second auth path); what they need on top is the /admin role floor, and whether the e2e account clears it is the subject of HYG-027.

entries.title: The stored-links census has no checker and no freshness rule, so its two probes carry duplicated inline logic
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while working LIVE-104/108/109 (ADR-1125). ADR-1115 modelled scripts/stored-links.json on scripts/stored-block-types.json and copied the census but NOT the instrument around it. The block census has scripts/check-stored-blocks.mjs (integrity floors, a pure classifier, loud degradation, a `--probe` mode) plus scripts/check-stored-blocks.test.ts driving it against broken fixtures, so the DETECTOR is proven to fire rather than assumed to. The link census has neither. Three consequences, all live in the tree today:

  • THE LOGIC LIVES IN THE ROWS. LIVE-104's probe is ~1.5 KB of `node -e` that parses the census, parses next.config.ts's redirect table, follows redirect chains and re-derives four counts. LIVE-108's re-implements the same census walk and the same redirect parse. Two copies, written in JSON string escapes, where neither can be unit-tested and a fix to one silently misses the other.
  • THE DETECTOR IS UNPROVEN. Its arms have been exercised by hand — mutation controls are recorded in ADR-1115 and ADR-1125 — which is better than nothing and is exactly the manual ritual check-stored-blocks.test.ts exists to replace.
  • THERE IS NO FRESHNESS RULE. `capturedAt` is written but nothing reads it, so a census months behind production reads exactly like one taken this morning. The block census at least asserts the field is PRESENT. ⚠️ Stated rather than glossed, because it does not go away: neither census can see a document written AFTER its capture date — only a credentialled re-capture can, and this repo has no credentialled CI job. A freshness rule cannot fix that; it can only stop a stale reading from passing quietly as a fresh one.

THE WORK: lift the shared walk into scripts/check-stored-links.mjs (census I/O, integrity floors, the redirect-table parse, the classifier), give it a test that drives it against broken fixtures, and reduce both row probes to a `--probe` call. Do NOT weaken what those probes currently assert while doing it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const S='scripts/check-stored-links.mjs',T='scripts/check-stored-links.test.ts',B='docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json';if(!fs.existsSync(B))process.exit(79);const miss=[];if(!fs.existsSync(S))miss.push(S+' does not exist: the census has no instrument, only two hand-rolled row probes');if(!fs.existsSync(T))miss.push(T+' does not exist: the detector is unproven');let b;try{b=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(B,'utf8'))}catch{process.exit(79)}const rows=(b.entries||[]).filter(e=>e.id==='LIVE-104'||e.id==='LIVE-108');if(rows.length!==2)process.exit(79);for(const r of rows){const c=(r.verify||{}).cmd||'';if(/next\.config/.test(c)&&!/check-stored-links/.test(c))miss.push(r.id+' still re-implements the census walk and the redirect-table parse inline ('+c.length+' chars of node -e) instead of calling the shared checker')}if(miss.length){console.error(miss.join('\n'));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE — the shared instrument exists, it has a test, and the two row probes actually CALL it instead of each carrying a copy of the census walk and the redirect-table parse. A file that merely exists does not close it: the probes must stop re-implementing next.config.ts parsing inline. Exits 79 if the backlog or the two rows cannot be read, so 'I could not look' never spells the same as 'I found nothing'.

entries.title: listing_saves: superseded by SCAN-508 — the retirement was correct and the callers came later
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 04:14 UTC while running the migration finale, and the premise CHANGED once it was measured. A ledger row `20270327000000 restore_listing_saves` appeared in production between 04:00 and 04:14, applied from OUTSIDE the session driving the merge queue, with no file in supabase/migrations and none on any of the 20 most recently pushed branches. Because ledger-parity computes inParity as repoOnly === 0 AND ledgerOnly === 0, that one orphan row turned check:migrations red on NINE open branches at once, none of them for a reason their own diff could explain.

🔴 THE RETIREMENT WAS WRONG, and that is the finding. 20260925000000_retire_orphaned_tables_and_functions.sql dropped public.listing_saves as an orphan -- 'no reader, no writer'. It has BOTH, and they are reachable: lib/listings/index.ts declares saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds against `listing_saves`, and app/(main)/housing/[id]/edit/actions.ts exports saveListingAction and unsaveListingAction over them, with app/(main)/housing/[id]/page.tsx batching listSavedListingIds for the browse grid. So from 2026-09-25 until tonight's restore, a member hearting a housing listing was writing to a table that did not exist. Nobody filed it, which says the path is cold in practice -- but it was live code against a missing table, not dead code.

WHO restored it is still unknown: the owner was asked on 2026-08-25 and answered that it was not them. The repair direction was chosen from the live catalog rather than from the row -- the table EXISTS (profile_id, listing_id, created_at; composite PK; both FKs cascade; RLS with one policy, listing_saves_self, FOR ALL on profile_id = private.get_my_profile_id(); 0 rows), so deleting the ledger row would leave a fresh replay without a table production has. 20270327000000 reconstructs it field-by-field off the live catalog, idempotent, and scripts/table-grants.txt carries its `authenticated` verdict.

THE WORK: (1) write the ADR recording the un-retirement and AMEND 20260925000000's 'orphaned' claim, which production and the code both contradict; (2) decide whether the saves feature is wanted -- if yes it needs a test so the table cannot be retired out from under it again, and if no, the honest end state is retiring the CODE first and then the table in a new higher-versioned migration; (3) audit the REST of 20260925000000: if it was wrong about this table it may be wrong about its siblings, and that is the cheap check to run now.

⚠️ DO NOT close this by deleting the ledger row, and do not edit 20270327000000 -- it describes an apply that already happened. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 AS SUPERSEDED BY SCAN-508 / ADR-1144, AND THIS ROW'S HEADLINE WAS WRONG. It says 'THE RETIREMENT WAS WRONG, and that is the finding'. It was not. The local clone was SHALLOW (71 commits) so nothing here could order the events; git fetch --deepen=500 reaches 681 and settles it: 20260925000000 landed 2026-07-07 (#1606) verifying 0 code references, and lib/listings/index.ts gained its four .from('listing_saves') sites on 2026-07-27 (#1967), TWENTY DAYS LATER. The EFFECT this row describes is real and was real — a member hearting a housing listing wrote to a table that did not exist — but the diagnosis is backwards: a feature was built on an already-dropped table, so it never worked rather than having broken. The 'WHO restored it' question is answered too: the restore was deliberate and correct, recorded in 20270327000000 and explained in the AMENDED note now carried by 20260925000000. Two rows described one thing and one of them asserted something the other disproves; the one list keeps the accurate one.

verify.evidence: Superseded by SCAN-508 (done) and ADR-1144. Timeline established from git after `git fetch --deepen=500`: retirement migration first appears 2026-07-07 in #1606; the listing_saves call sites first appear 2026-07-27 in #1967. Production: public.listing_saves exists with 0 rows and 1 policy. SCAN-508's probe is the live one — it holds the AMENDED note in the retirement migration and the throw-path tests in lib/listings/saves.test.ts.

entries.title: The operator surfaces have no a11y ratchet rows, and the e2e account may not clear the /admin role floor

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json';if(!fs.existsSync(F))process.exit(79);const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8'));const keys=Object.keys(j.surfaces||{}).filter(k=>k.startsWith('/admin'));if(keys.length===0){console.error('the a11y ratchet holds 0 operator rows, so the seven /admin surfaces the visual suite watches are still held to $defaultMax and cannot join the a11y matrix');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.detail:
FILED 2026-08-25 by ADR-1128, which deliberately left both halves out of its own change.

HALF ONE — THE A11Y RATCHET. ADR-1128 added seven /admin routes to the VISUAL suite only. a11y.spec.ts and overflow.spec.ts still read publicSurfaces()/appSurfaces(). A surface with no row in test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json is held to $defaultMax (0 serious+), so adding the operator routes there without first SEEDING the ratchet would fail pull requests on debt that predates them — exactly what update-a11y + capture_shell exists to prevent. The seed is a dispatch: e2e-manual.yml → base_url=<preview>, capture_shell ✔, update_a11y ✔. The probe measures the consequence: at least one '/admin' key in the ratchet.

HALF TWO — THE ROLE FLOOR, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN CALLED UNCHECKABLE. requireAdminFloor() (lib/admin/guard.ts) admits platform staff (web_role admin/janitor) or a team_members staff role that sees an admin group, and redirects everyone else to /feed. PW_MEMBER_EMAIL is an owner-held secret, but its CONSEQUENCE is readable: test/e2e/a11y-baselines.json carries '/spaces/danieltyack/manage' rows, so the e2e account manages that Space, and exactly two profiles do — danieltyack (web_role janitor, clears the floor) and awesomepossum (web_role none, does not). Repo-wide only danieltyack and moderation hold a staff web_role and team_members holds one row. So the outcome is one of two and the first capture run settles it in one line of the job summary: if the seven /admin rows appear under 'Still unphotographed', the account is the second one and the fix is a single grant (web_role='admin', or a team_members staff role that sees an admin group). Until then operatorDenialReason() skips those tests WITH THE CAUSE NAMED and shell-reporter.ts lists every one of them on every run — loud, never silent.
