entries.title: Vercel builds intermittently stall at 'Collecting page data' for tens of minutes, and merging deploys to production

source.ref: the cold-compile path a trim leaves behind — NOT established as the cause

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 05:26-05:36 UTC while driving the merge queue. Preview build dpl_DYMk7sVcpW8n7xCfupmUmbtbnjqB (#2285, efad250) printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 05:26:05 and emitted NOTHING for the next 10 minutes, against a control that did the whole build in 2m10s. Three builds hung the same way earlier the same night. 🔴 WHY THIS IS LIVE AND NOT HYGIENE: main is protected and merging DEPLOYS, so the same stall on a production build is a production deploy that never lands. ── WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, from the two builds' own logs. They are the SAME BRANCH one docs-only commit apart, so the code is not the variable: (a) ca95b0a restored cache 8erA4jNs, compiled in 46s, finished 2m10s, green; (b) efad250 restored cache 92GM6pY7 — the build whose postbuild had just trimmed .next/cache/turbopack (1621 MiB) — compiled COLD in 113s, then stalled. The cold compile is expected and documented ('Next build: warm install, cold compile'); it costs CPU by design. The STALL is at a later stage and is NOT explained by it. ── 🔴 THREE HYPOTHESES TESTED AND RULED OUT, recorded so nobody re-runs them: (1) NOT the ADR-1064/ADR-1086 fetch-cache deletion. check-cache-budget.mjs protects it — NEVER_TRIM_DIRS = ['fetch-cache','images'], the trim walks only COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS = ['turbopack','rspack','webpack','swc'], an OVERLAP assertion refuses to trim if the lists ever meet, and check-cache-budget-trim.test.ts reconstructs the old bad trim. The gate's '.next/cache 0 MiB' line is not a deleted fetch cache: the 'holds:' line shows the directory contained only .previewinfo, config.json and .rscinfo, so there was no fetch-cache directory to lose. (2) NOT database saturation, which WAS the proven cause of the ~02:40 incident: measured mid-stall at 34/60 connections, 1 active, 0 blocked, no lock waits. (3) NOT build concurrency, the other proven cause: efad250 was the only build running. ── WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: the cause. The leading untested hypothesis is memory pressure — the builder is 4 cores / 8 GB, page data prerenders ~330 routes across 3 workers, and a cold compile denies them every warm module cache; a hung build never reaches the 'Build system report' line that would print 'No memory or disk space problems detected', so absence of that line is not evidence of health. NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: correlate hung builds against whether their restored cache had been trimmed (the Vercel log's 'Restored build cache from previous deployment (<id>)' line gives the lineage for free), and if the correlation holds, test the memory hypothesis by raising the builder or lowering worker count before touching the trim. Do NOT 'fix' check:cache-budget on this row's suspicion alone: its trim is proven correct by mutation test, and breaking it re-opens the 1.50 GB ceiling that killed two builds. ── 🔴 AMENDED 2026-08-25 05:46: THE CACHE-LINEAGE CORRELATION IS FALSIFIED. When this row was filed, three builds were consistent with 'restored a trimmed cache -> stalls'. A direct control killed it: theme/p5-adoption was re-pushed as 71c9913c5, Vercel restored THE SAME trimmed cache (92GM6pY7 — branch-scoped restore, so the re-push could not escape it), the build cold-compiled exactly as efad250 had, and then COMPLETED — 'Build Completed in 2m', READY in ~2m50s, finishing with 'Uploading build cache [1.26 GB]'. Same branch, same cache, same cold compile, opposite outcome. So the trimmed cache does NOT cause the stall, and the 'branch is trapped on a poisoned cache' reading that followed from it is wrong too — the trap does not exist, because a build on that very cache succeeded and replaced it. FOUR hypotheses are now dead (fetch-cache deletion, DB saturation, build concurrency, cache lineage), and the stall stands as an UNEXPLAINED TRANSIENT: one occurrence, not reproducible on demand, no known trigger. 🔴 DO NOT re-run the four dead hypotheses, and do not treat the cold compile as the fault: it is documented, intended, and costs CPU only. The honest next step is not a fix but an OBSERVATION: this needs a second occurrence before it can be diagnosed at all, so what would actually help is capturing whether a stalled build ever reaches BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME and what its 'Build system report' says — a hung build never prints that line, which is why the memory hypothesis below remains untested rather than untrue. ── 🔴 CORRECTION 2026-08-25 06:16, and it retracts this row's own advice: RETRY IS NOT A RELIABLE WORKAROUND. The row said so on the strength of #2285, which stalled once and went green on its first retry. #2283 then stalled THREE TIMES IN A ROW on the same branch — dac3a9d96 (05:51, terminal error captured), 0f294a89d first attempt, and 0f294a89d again after a re-push — so the earlier sentence described a coin flip, not a fix. Occurrence rate on the night: 4 of ~16 preview builds. ── WHAT THE THREE #2283 FAILURES ADD: they were NOT all cold compiles (81s, 77s and 113s across the set, against a 46s warm control), NOT all concurrent with another build (one ran alone), and NOT cache-lineage bound (#2285 succeeded on the very cache #2283 keeps failing on). The one thing every failure shares is the stage: page-data collection, 3 workers, dying without output. 🔴 APPLICATION CODE IS RULED OUT, and this is the cleanest evidence in the row: PR #2287 is DOCS-ONLY — two files, docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json and AGENTS.md, zero code, zero dependencies — and its build stalls identically (0942e50, 11m+ at page data). A build with no code change cannot be crashed by code, so every application-level lead dies with it, including the astronomy-engine one #2283 invited. ── THE REMAINING ASYMMETRY, worth a look but NOT yet a cause: in the same window, builds on a branch based on OLD main (claude/frequency-codebase-audit-vii214, base 10c2f0b3) went READY in 2m54s and 3m29s, while every branch based on TONIGHT's main stalled. That points at something that entered main during the 11-PR merge run rather than at any one PR's diff — but main's own production build after #2285 (591bcc1) went READY in 2m6s, which argues against it, so the asymmetry is unexplained rather than damning. The concrete lever remains worker count or builder size. ── ✅ CARRIED OVER FROM THE HANDOFF BRANCH, and it is the most diagnostic fact in this row: THE STALL IS NOT A STALL. Established at 06:01, BEFORE the 06:16 correction above, and folded in here on 2026-08-25 08:5x when the two records were reconciled. The #2283 build was allowed to run to its natural end — the one thing no earlier occurrence had done — and it did not time out silently, it FAILED with a real error: `Error: The file "/vercel/path0/.next/routes-manifest.json" couldn't be found`, emitted at 23:01:36 UTC against 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 22:51:47. So the ~10 minutes of silence is not a hang: page-data collection DIES, produces no routes-manifest.json, and Vercel only surfaces it after its own wait. That reframes the row — the thing to explain is a CRASHING collector, not a blocked one, and 'it hung' was the wrong question for four hypotheses in a row. 🔴 IT ALSO MAKES THE MEMORY HYPOTHESIS THE LEADING ONE and is consistent with every observation: the builder is 4 cores / 8 GB, page data prerenders ~330 routes across 3 workers, a worker killed by the OOM reaper writes nothing and prints nothing, and the 'Build system report' line that would say 'No memory or disk space problems detected' is only reached by builds that COMPLETE — which is exactly why every healthy build shows it and no failing one does. NEXT STEP, concrete: reduce the page-data worker count (or raise the builder) and see whether the rate goes to zero. The misconfigured-distDir causes Vercel's own error text suggests are ruled out by the same commit and config building green on a retry. ── ⚠️ FIFTH OCCURRENCE 2026-08-25 08:12, on the meta-scan split: dpl_9WWrdz7onHuhx32cisXkTXeUmHtL (#2289 split/b-seo, 571aac085) compiled normally in 78s and then sat at 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' from 08:12:57 with no further output. It matters for the rate rather than the diagnosis: the SAME session's other three split branches built green (#2288, #2290, #2291 all READY), so it is still intermittent and still not branch-, code- or cache-bound. Running total on the two sessions: 5 of ~20. The workaround that worked here was not a retry but a re-push carrying a main merge, which is a new build rather than a re-run of the same one. ── 🔴 SIXTH OCCURRENCE 2026-08-25 11:17, AND IT IS THE FIRST ON PRODUCTION — THIS ROW'S OWN PREDICTION CAME TRUE. dpl_7Dbat8ebPxAkzpWrpC8sx1nAWiYg is the PRODUCTION build of 2f4b1cd93, the merge commit of #2287, and it is in state ERROR. Compiled successfully in 84s, completed runAfterProductionCompile in 83s, printed 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 11:17:42 and emitted nothing further. postbuild never ran, so that build produced NO gate readings. CONSEQUENCE, which is the part that matters: production is serving ee1aacf99 and main's HEAD IS NOT DEPLOYED. The row opened by arguing it was LIVE rather than hygiene because 'the same stall on a production build is a production deploy that never lands' — that is no longer a forecast. ✅ AND IT IS THE CLEANEST CONTROL IN THE ROW, better than the #2287 preview it already cites: 2f4b1cd93 differs from ee1aacf99 — the last GREEN PRODUCTION build, same target, same branch, same builder class — by exactly TWO FILES, AGENTS.md and docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json, and neither is read by any app or script the build runs (grep across app/lib/components finds only comment prose mentioning AGENTS.md; prebuild is copy-maplibre-worker.mjs alone). Every byte the compiler and the collector see is identical. A build input that cannot differ, succeeding and then failing on the same target, retires 'something about this tree' as a class of explanation, not just the four hypotheses already dead. Running total 6 of ~21. THE NEXT STEP IS UNCHANGED AND NOW HAS A COST ATTACHED: set experimental.cpus in next.config.ts to lower the collector's worker count (Next 16.3.2's getNumberOfWorkers at node_modules/next/dist/build/index.js:369 treats any value differing from the default as a user override; the config does not set it today, so the 3 in the log is Vercel's own modifyConfig choosing for a 4-core builder), or raise the builder. ⚠️ Do NOT wire that from this row's suspicion in a change that cannot observe it: at a ~29% failure rate ONE green build proves nothing, so the change and the reading of its rate belong together. ── ✅ THE GAP CLOSED 2026-08-25 12:36, WITHOUT ANYONE FIXING THIS ROW. The production build of 1386abe6c (#2293) went READY, so production is current with main's HEAD again and the 'not deployed' consequence recorded above is over. It is a data point, NOT a fix: the failure is intermittent by definition, and one green build at a ~27% rate proves nothing about the cause. Running total 6 of ~22. ⚠️ TWO THINGS THAT BUILD PRINTED AND A FAILING ONE NEVER DOES. (1) 'Build system report • No memory or disk space problems detected' — exactly as this row predicts, that line is reached only by a build that COMPLETES, so its presence here is not evidence against the memory hypothesis and its absence on the six failures is not evidence for it. It stays untested. (2) postbuild ran all four gates, which a failing build never reaches: build-budget 6.67 GB / 498 fns (83%), og-trace 69/100, shell-weight 1011 KB / 21 chunks (72%), cache-budget 1.28 GB predicted against 1.27 GB actually uploaded — a THIRD paired reading, accurate to 1%, on the same mix as the c8b5ee97 exact one. 🔴 ONE NEW OBSERVATION WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME: this build took NINE MINUTES ('Build Completed in /vercel/output [9m]') against the 2m-2m50s controls this row quotes throughout, and still finished. So slowness at this stage is not itself the failure, and a build sitting quiet for several minutes is not yet a stalled one — which is worth knowing before anyone cancels another and destroys the evidence.

⏳ A LEAD, NOT A FINDING, from the 2026-08-25 21:43Z production build (e3cec7af2, #2308). Stated as a lead deliberately: nothing here is measured against a stall, and writing it up as a cause would be the shape-not-truth error this file exists to prevent.
  THE OBSERVATION: check:cache-budget printed 1.34 GB packed, up from 1.27 GB twelve hours earlier on the same day. Raw .next/cache went 1359 -> 1476 MiB while node_modules held flat at 934 MiB, so ALL of the growth is turbopack compiler cache. That is 89% of the 1.50 GB ceiling and roughly 96% of the trim point. The paired reading was EXACT (predicted 1.34, `Uploading build cache [1.34 GB]`), so the number is not an artifact of PACKED_PER_RAW.
  WHY IT BEARS ON THIS ROW. A trim is not free: AGENTS.md records 113s cold against a 46s warm control on the build AFTER one, and LIVE-048's history is a trim that hung two builds until BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME at 46 minutes. That failure mode is FIXED — the trim now iterates a named compiler-cache list and cannot reach the incremental fetch cache, proven by mutation tests — so this is not a prediction that the old bug returns. It is narrower: the cache is about to start crossing the trim line regularly, trims make the next build cold, and this row is about builds intermittently taking tens of minutes. Those two facts have not been put beside each other.
  🔵 THE TEST, so this lead can be settled rather than repeated. For each known stall window, check whether the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING build's log carries a `check:cache-budget` trim line. Trims are logged by the gate itself, so the evidence already exists in build logs and needs no new instrumentation. CONFIRMING means stalls follow trims; REFUTING means they do not, and the lead should be struck from this row rather than left to look like a partial explanation. Note the prior is genuinely uncertain: this row's own earlier finding is that the stalls are ANTI-correlated with DB outages, and both stall windows returned zero runtime errors, so the cause is still open.
  ⚠️ DO NOT PRE-EMPT IT BY LOWERING THE TRIM POINT. A gate that has burned this repo twice is the wrong place for a speculative change, and trimming earlier trades a rare cold compile for a frequent one. Measure first.

🔵 THE CACHE-TRIM LEAD IS REFUTED, 2026-08-25, ON ITS FIRST TEST — and the test was run because the row said what would settle it. Striking it rather than leaving it to look like a partial explanation, which is what that paragraph asked for in its own words.
  A LIVE STALL WAS CAPTURED the same evening the lead was written. Preview deploy 6kWwu78AzjQW2FZYe5yDYD2WYQ4W (PR #2309, commit c64daed09):
    21:56:16  next build starts
    21:57:44  ✓ Compiled successfully in 83s
    21:58:33  ✓ Completed runAfterProductionCompile in 50s
    21:58:35  Collecting page data using 3 workers ...
    ~22:39    deployment state ERROR — roughly 41 MINUTES with no further log line
  The compile was healthy and fast. Nothing after 'Collecting page data' was ever written. That is this row's signature exactly, and it is the same phase LIVE-105's 46-minute death reached.
  THE TEST, AND ITS ANSWER. The lead asked: does the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING build log a check:cache-budget trim? The preceding deploy on this branch is 89pdWs69cq6R8pGUZFKqsqoj4EaA, which completed at 21:55:37 — one minute before the stalled build started. Its log carries the cache-budget gate printing a NORMAL reading and NO TRIM LINE: `.next/cache holds: turbopack 1370 MiB`, then `Uploading build cache [1.27 GB]`, under the ceiling and under the trim point. It also printed shell-weight 1012 KB / 22 chunks and completed in 4m.
  🔴 SO A TRIM DID NOT PRECEDE THIS STALL, and the mechanism the lead proposed — trim makes the next build cold, cold build stalls — did not operate here. The lead is struck. It was a reasonable hypothesis from a real measurement and it is simply wrong, which is the useful outcome: this row's cause is still open and the cache is no longer a candidate worth re-proposing.
  ⚠️ NOTE THE CACHE OSCILLATES, which is worth keeping even though it explains nothing here: the 21:43Z production build uploaded 1.34 GB and this 21:55Z preview uploaded 1.27 GB, twelve minutes apart. The AGENTS.md series should be read as a band rather than a trend line.
  ⚪ WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND STILL UNEXPLAINED: the stall lands at 'Collecting page data', after a successful compile, on a build whose predecessor was healthy, with zero runtime errors in the window and no DB outage. Four candidate causes are now excluded — DB outage, runtime errors, the cache trim, and the compile itself.

🔵 A SECOND STALL THE SAME EVENING, AND THE TWO TOGETHER POINT SOMEWHERE NEW. 2026-08-25. Framed as a LEAD with a stated test, not a cause — the cache lead was refuted hours earlier and the discipline that produced that refutation is the only reason this one is worth writing down.
  THE TWO STALLS, side by side:
    6kWwu78AzjQW2FZYe5yDYD2WYQ4W   compiled 83s · afterCompile 50.0s · PAGE DATA 21:58:35 · ERROR ~22:39 (~41m)
    5DeA3axUMHeadQkdgN4seFzoA8Uv   compiled 87s · afterCompile 29.2s · PAGE DATA 21:58:47 · ERROR ~22:42 (~44m)
  🔴 THEY ENTERED 'Collecting page data using 3 workers' TWELVE SECONDS APART, AND BOTH HUNG. Two builds were in that phase simultaneously, each spawning 3 workers, on the same account. Neither wrote another log line.
  AND THE BUILDS THAT DID NOT OVERLAP FINISHED FINE, on the same branch and the same tree, within the same hour: 89pdWs69cq6R8pGUZFKqsqoj4EaA completed 21:55:37 in 4m, ATBWn9KKmcxnxY4o5HRNPaCJQVUK was READY at 22:22. Tonight reads 2 of 2 concurrent stalled, 3 of 3 non-concurrent green.
  THE HYPOTHESIS: page-data collection does not tolerate a CONCURRENT sibling build. Six worker processes rather than three, competing for memory or CPU on shared capacity, with no timeout that fires — which fits the two facts this row could never place, namely that the compile is always healthy and that nothing is ever logged after the phase begins. A deadlock or a thrash produces exactly that silence; a slow build would still print.
  🔵 WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: a single stalled build looks like an infrastructure shrug. It took two in one window, with timestamps, to show they were CONCURRENT — and they were concurrent because two commits were pushed a few minutes apart and Vercel did not cancel the older build.
  🔵 THE TEST, and it is cheap. For every stall in this row's history, check whether ANOTHER deployment was in 'Collecting page data' at the same moment. Build logs carry that timestamp already, so no new instrumentation is needed. CONFIRMING means the fix is a project setting rather than code — Vercel's automatic cancellation of superseded preview deployments, or a concurrency cap — and LIVE-105's 46-minute production death should be re-read for a concurrent sibling too. REFUTING means tonight's pairing is a coincidence and this gets struck like the cache lead did.
  ⚠️ DO NOT ACT ON THIS BEFORE TESTING IT. Two stalls is two data points, and the last confident reading in this row lasted four hours.

🔴 THE CONCURRENCY LEAD HAS A COUNTER-EXAMPLE, FOUND FORTY MINUTES AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN. 2026-08-25. Narrowed, not confirmed, and the narrowing matters more than the original claim.
  TWO CONCURRENT BUILDS AT PAGE DATA BOTH SUCCEEDED: 4PEA2KVqdjGYxzuPzQFnQHeNmu4K and Dmsy6UyyvdzHeAcdsMMbMdXUy9Kx, both READY at 22:44. Dmsy6Uyy entered 'Collecting page data using 3 workers' at 22:43:52 and was generating static pages by 22:44:00 — EIGHT SECONDS. 4PEA2KV's whole build was 42s and it finished at 22:44:12, so its page-data phase overlapped Dmsy6Uyy's. Concurrency at that phase therefore does NOT predict a stall on its own.
  🔵 AND THE MECHANISM I PROPOSED IS RULED OUT OUTRIGHT. The lead guessed at six worker processes competing for memory or CPU 'on the same account'. Every Vercel deployment gets its OWN machine — the log's first lines say so: `Build machine configuration: 4 cores, 8 GB`, printed per deployment. There is no shared box for two builds to thrash. I reasoned about infrastructure I had not read, which is the same error as every other wrong reading in this file today.
  ⏳ WHAT THE FOUR BUILDS ACTUALLY SEPARATE ON IS CACHE WARMTH, not concurrency:
    STALLED  6kWwu78  compiled 83s     (cold)   · concurrent · page data 21:58:35 · died ~41m
    STALLED  5DeA3ax  compiled 87s     (cold)   · concurrent · page data 21:58:47 · died ~44m
    GREEN    Dmsy6Uy  compiled 16.8s   (WARM, restored from ATBWn9KK) · concurrent · page data 8s
    GREEN    4PEA2KV  whole build 42s  (WARM)   · concurrent · fine
    GREEN    89pdWs69 whole build 4m   (coldish) · ALONE · fine
  So the surviving shape is COLD **and** CONCURRENT, which is one observed conjunction and not a finding. A cold build alone (89pdWs69) was fine; warm builds concurrent were fine.
  🔵 THE BETTER MECHANISM TO TEST NEXT, since the machine is private but the DATABASE is not: page-data collection is the first phase that runs application code, so it is the first phase that opens Supabase connections. A cold build has every route to evaluate; two of them together may exhaust a connection pool or deadlock against it. That fits the silence exactly — a pool that never hands back a connection logs nothing and times out at nothing. It also fits why a warm concurrent pair survives: eight seconds of page data barely touches the pool.
  ⚪ THE TEST IS UNCHANGED IN SHAPE: for each historical stall, was another deployment in page data at the same moment AND was the stalled build cold? Both facts are already in the build logs. Supabase connection metrics for the stall windows would settle the mechanism.
  ⚠️ THIS ROW HAS NOW HAD TWO LEADS WRITTEN AND BOTH WEAKENED WITHIN HOURS. That is the process working, not failing — but nobody should act on the third one before it is tested either. ── 2026-08-29, TWO MORE MEASURED INSTANCES, AND THE STRONGEST EXCLUSION YET. dpl_FL6voNiRTh2AjcpL8uqxwuXaCJLm (#2318, 4a560f9) died BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME after 2770615 ms with 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' as its last line; the very next build of a tree differing by 37 lines of JSON finished in 39 min, green. Then dpl_AnGdPo5f2mABgHHBDgxoHuFpvLuT (#2321, c8de0ca) died the same way after 2770479 ms. THE TWO DURATIONS ARE 136 ms APART, so the 46-minute figure is a hard platform ceiling the stall runs into, not a variable cost. THE EXCLUSION: c8de0ca's ENTIRE diff against main is 120 baseline PNGs under test/e2e/__screenshots__ plus two markdown files. Not one line of source, config, dependency or route changed. A build that stalls on that tree cannot be blamed on any source change, on bundle growth, or on route count. Whatever the variable is, it is in the platform or the cache, not in what the diff contains.

── 2026-08-31, A THIRD CAPTURE — AND IT RUNS THE ROW'S OWN NEXT STEP ──
dpl_FWSFE4L6TJSZfqynZunFmqpPm6ZC (PR #2328, f6a77d25, cle1, 4 cores / 8 GB):
  22:52:41  Restored build cache from previous deployment (AdqbQDtqDpM4U4Zc3JmKpugGNKg2)
  22:54:38  ✓ Compiled successfully in 109s          <- COLD (this row's warm control is 46s)
  22:54:54  Collecting page data using 3 workers ... <- LAST LINE
  23:38:18  deployment FAILED, 43 minutes with no further output

This row's stated NEXT STEP was to 'correlate hung builds against whether their restored cache had been trimmed'. Done, for free, from the parent's own log — and the answer is YES. AdqbQDtqDpM4U4Zc3JmKpugGNKg2 logged at 20:47:44: 'check:cache-budget trimmed the build cache before Vercel could reject it ... 2.48 GiB raw, about 1.41 GB packed, over the 1.40 GB trim point ... drops compiler caches instead: .next/cache/turbopack (1602 MiB) ... Next build: warm install, cold compile.'

So the ledger of captured stalls now reads:
  A  2026-08-25, efad250   parent TRIMMED -> cold compile 113s -> stall
  B  2026-08-25 (AGENTS.md refutation)  parent did NOT trim   -> stall
  C  2026-08-31, f6a77d25  parent TRIMMED -> cold compile 109s -> stall (this entry)

⚠️ READ THAT CAREFULLY, BECAUSE IT DOES NOT REINSTATE THE TRIM HYPOTHESIS. Case B still refutes 'a trim is NECESSARY for a stall', and that refutation stands — do not re-run it. What C adds is that a trim is not IRRELEVANT either: two of the three captured stalls follow one. The factor common to A and C is not the trim itself but the COLD COMPILE it forces, which is also the row's leading untested hypothesis (memory pressure: a cold compile denies 3 page-data workers every warm module cache on a 4-core/8 GB builder). Whether case B also compiled cold was never recorded, and that single unknown is now the cheapest thing standing between this row and a testable cause — it is one line in an existing log, not a new experiment.

🔵 NOT A REPO-WIDE BREAK, measured the same night: PR #2327 built the same repo green in ~2-2.5 minutes repeatedly across b4v9ZDo8M9msAP15TNmECUb5xB2B, 3dBXXfSmTtVPFyEym9P2neEDsH5Q and H37nncTVZPTj2gH5kkR5zujk8zxC. The stall is intermittent, exactly as this row says.

🔵 INCIDENTAL CORROBORATION for the PACKED_PER_RAW note in AGENTS.md: that parent build predicted 'about 0.52 GB packed' post-trim and its own 'Uploading build cache' line reported 257.30 MB — a ratio of ~0.26 on a node_modules-only mix, which is precisely the 0.264 AGENTS.md documents for that mix, and precisely why the 0.53 constant must NOT be lowered toward it.

── 2026-09-01, CAPTURES D AND E, AND THE FIRST DIRECT EVIDENCE FOR THE MEMORY HYPOTHESIS ──
This row said the memory hypothesis was untested, and named exactly why nobody could test it: "a hung build NEVER REACHES the 'Build system report' line that would print 'No memory or disk space problems detected', so absence of that line is not evidence of health."

🔴 CAPTURE D — dpl_9dC94yezTttm78hzDKEeMeGRErm5 (#2326, 6bc8c5e3) DID reach that line, because it did not hang: it was OOM-KILLED mid-compile, so `next build` exited without writing routes-manifest.json and Vercel reported the failure. The report reads:
    Error: "/vercel/path0/.next/routes-manifest.json" couldn't be found
    ▲ Build system report
    • At least one "Out of Memory" ("OOM") event was detected during the build.
      Build cache: <1 MB   Node modules: 1560 MB   Input source: 2996 MB
~19 minutes inside "Creating an optimized production build". Build cache <1 MB — no warm modules at all.

CAPTURE E — dpl_HRQttjaD1recLY1tHx6s1cuntZAT (#2328, 58353f39): compiled COLD in 118s at 23:43:41, "Collecting page data using 3 workers ..." at 23:45:29, failed 00:27:13. Forty-two minutes, no further line. The SECOND consecutive stall on that branch.

THE CORRELATION, measured across one night on one repo:
    WARM (~2 min build)   #2327 x3 (b4v9ZDo8, 3dBXXfSm, H37nncTV)  -> all GREEN
    COLD (109s / 118s)    #2328 x2 (FWSFE4L6, HRQttjaD)            -> both STALLED at page data
    NO CACHE (<1 MB)      #2326    (9dC94yeze)                     -> OOM, explicitly reported
    WARM again            #2328 x2 (CKH3guPR, 4DZFo9R6, ~2-3 min)  -> both GREEN, and it merged

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. D failed during COMPILE; A, C and E hung during COLLECTING PAGE DATA. Same resource, different stage — this is strong evidence for the MECHANISM, not proof the two are one event. D also carried 23 dependency bumps (node_modules 1560 MB), so it is not a clean control. Case B (parent did not trim, still stalled) still stands: a trim is not NECESSARY. Whether B compiled cold was never recorded and remains the cheapest open question — one line in an existing log.

WHAT IS NOW ACTIONABLE. This row's own next step was "test the memory hypothesis by raising the build machine size". That no longer rests on inference: Vercel's own report names OOM, and its own remedy line says "To expand your machine size to get additional memory and disk space, consider enabling Enhanced Builds." That is an owner/billing decision, not a code change — which is why this row stays OPEN and in the `live` lane rather than being closed by evidence alone.

🔵 #2326 did eventually land: dpl_8L8pMbNbTVky4ECwC257UiMUhLBT was a REDEPLOY of the OOM build and went READY, and the group merged as cd8a299e. So the failure is intermittent on the same tree, which is itself consistent with a resource ceiling rather than a code defect.

verify.evidence: 2026-08-25: a live stall CAPTURED with timestamps (preview 6kWwu78AzjQW2FZYe5yDYD2WYQ4W, commit c64daed09) — compiled successfully in 83s, runAfterProductionCompile in 50s, then 'Collecting page data using 3 workers ...' at 21:58:35 and no further log line before the deployment errored ~41 minutes later. THE CACHE-TRIM LEAD ADDED EARLIER THE SAME DAY IS REFUTED on its own stated test: the immediately preceding deploy (89pdWs69cq6R8pGUZFKqsqoj4EaA, completed 21:55:37, one minute before) logged NO trim — turbopack 1370 MiB, 'Uploading build cache [1.27 GB]', under both the ceiling and the trim point. Cause still open; DB outage, runtime errors, cache trim and the compile are all now excluded. — A SECOND STALL captured the same evening (5DeA3axUMHeadQkdgN4seFzoA8Uv: compiled 87s, page data 21:58:47, ERROR ~22:42), entering page-data collection TWELVE SECONDS after the first. Both hung; both had healthy compiles; neither logged another line. Non-overlapping builds on the same branch and tree finished normally in the same hour (89pdWs69 in 4m at 21:55, ATBWn9KK READY 22:22). New LEAD, untested: page-data collection may not tolerate a concurrent sibling build (6 workers, not 3). Test is whether every historical stall had a concurrent deployment in the same phase — build logs already carry the timestamp. — COUNTER-EXAMPLE 40 minutes later: 4PEA2KV and Dmsy6Uy were BOTH at page data around 22:43:52 and both succeeded (Dmsy6Uy: 16.8s compile off a restored cache, page data done in 8s). So concurrency alone does not predict a stall, and the proposed mechanism is ruled out outright — every Vercel deployment gets its own machine (`Build machine configuration: 4 cores, 8 GB`, per deployment), so there is no shared box to thrash. The four builds separate on CACHE WARMTH: both stalls were cold (83s/87s compiles), both concurrent survivors were warm. Surviving shape is cold AND concurrent, one observed conjunction, not a finding. Next mechanism to test: page data is the first phase to open Supabase connections, and a pool that never returns one logs nothing.

entries.title: lib/database.types.ts carries a hand-added spotlight_guestbook block — regen from production to prove parity
entries.detail:
ADR-1132 added the spotlight_guestbook types by hand in the generated style (the same way spotlight_top_friends arrived) because a full regen against production folds in every drift from every in-flight sibling branch — a diff that does not belong in a feature PR. The debt: nothing has machine-checked that the hand-written block matches what supabase gen types would emit. Next integrator regen (the standing 'regen + drop the untyped admin-handle casts' step BUILD-LIST already names) closes this: run the regen, diff, and mark this row done with the commit as evidence.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 BY MEASURING THE PROPERTY, NOT BY RUNNING THE METHOD. The row names a regen as the closing move, and a regen is still the right STANDING step for the reason the row gives (BUILD-LIST's 'regen + drop the untyped admin-handle casts'). But the property this row protects is narrower than that step: does the hand-written spotlight_guestbook block match what `supabase gen types` would emit? A regen answers it by folding in every unrelated drift from every in-flight branch — which is exactly the diff ADR-1132 declined to put in a feature PR, and declining it again here would leave the row open forever. `gen types` derives its output from the live schema, so the schema can be asked directly.
  MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-08-25, on every axis gen types derives:
  • COLUMN SET — six, exact, no extras: id/owner_profile_id/signer_profile_id uuid NOT NULL, message text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL, hidden_at timestamptz NULL. Row types match, and hidden_at is the only `| null`.
  • INSERT OPTIONALITY — gen types marks a field optional iff it is nullable OR carries a default. Production: id and created_at have defaults, hidden_at is nullable; the other three have neither. The block marks exactly id, created_at and hidden_at optional and leaves owner_profile_id, signer_profile_id and message required. Exact.
  • UPDATE — all six optional, hidden_at nullable. Exact.
  • RELATIONSHIPS — two foreign keys, both to profiles, both with referenced column `id` (confirmed by reading pg_constraint.confkey, not assumed from the PK). `isOneToOne: false` is correct for BOTH and is the one value that could plausibly have been wrong: the table does carry a unique constraint, but it is COMPOSITE on (owner_profile_id, signer_profile_id), so neither FK column is unique on its own. A single-column unique on either would have made that side true.
  • The two CHECK constraints (message_len, not_self) correctly do not appear — gen types emits Relationships for foreign keys only.
  So the hand-add is machine-checked now, which is what the row asked for; only the instrument differs. The standing regen step remains worth doing for the OTHER drift it would catch across the whole file, and that is a different concern from this row.

verify.evidence: Measured against production 2026-08-25 rather than by regen, because a regen folds in unrelated in-flight drift — the diff ADR-1132 declined. information_schema.columns gives the six columns with nullability and default presence; pg_constraint gives both FKs and their referenced column (profiles.id) plus the COMPOSITE unique that makes isOneToOne false on both sides. The block matches on column set, Row nullability, Insert optionality (nullable OR default), Update optionality, and Relationships. The standing BUILD-LIST regen stays worthwhile for whole-file drift; that is not this row.

entries.title: Regenerate lib/database.types.ts once the train lands
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 0. listing_saves was restored to production (20270327000000) and the natal/guestbook tables land with the open train, but lib/database.types.ts is train-owned mid-flight, so the restore ships with the code casting around the missing types (how the original ghost compiled). entries.title: Rule how pending-approval seats interact with capacity and the waitlist
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 1. The approval-gate fixes exposed a design tension nothing has ruled on: a pending (unapproved) seat holds status 'going' and consumes capacity (lib/events/capacity.ts:27-38), and promoteFromWaitlist promotes a still-pending waitlist row into a confirmed seat. Either behavior may be intended; neither is recorded. One ruling, then a small code follow-through if it changes. ── ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1148). OWNER RULING: APPROVAL GATES THE SEAT. A pending request does NOT consume capacity; only an approved (or ungated) 'going' seat counts, and on approval a full event sends the person to the waitlist. That matches content/help/groups/events.md verbatim — 'A full event still sends approved people to the waitlist. Approving says yes, you are welcome, not there is room' — which was only true if approval, not the request, consumes the seat. THE DEFECT IT REMOVES: twenty unapproved REQUESTS could fill a twenty-seat event the host had not said yes to, and the host could then not approve anyone, because their own event read as full. THREE PLACES, kept in lockstep because they answer the same question: getCapacityInfo (lib/events/capacity.ts), the paged fallback in lib/events/going-counts.ts, and the event_going_counts RPC (20270333000000_going_counts_exclude_pending.sql, applied; ledger repaired to the repo version, 641 ⇄ 641). AND PROMOTION NO LONGER BYPASSES THE GATE: promoteFromWaitlist took the oldest waitlist row whatever its approval state, so a still-pending request could be lifted into a confirmed seat by someone else's cancellation — approval granted by timing rather than by the host. ✅ approval_status is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none' (verified on production), so a plain <> 'pending' is COMPLETE rather than merely careful, and a null branch would suggest a state the column cannot hold. ⚠️ MEASURED BEFORE CHANGING: 0 gated events, 0 pending rows, 'none' the only value present — so this changes no current count and closes the rule before the first gated event exists. lib/events/capacity.test.ts adds 5 arms that assert THE FILTER IS SENT rather than that a number came back, because the bug was never in the arithmetic; mutation-proven both ways.

verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in all three places that answer 'how many seats are taken': both filters in capacity.ts (the count AND the waitlist pick), the paged fallback, and the RPC's own body. Comment lines are stripped first, so the prose explaining the rule cannot satisfy the probe that enforces it.

entries.title: Twenty other reads still count a pending request as an attendee
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while closing SCAN-105, by measuring the NEIGHBOURS of the read being fixed rather than stopping at it — the habit that found SCAN-211. SCAN-105 settled the CAPACITY question: a pending request does not hold a seat. It deliberately did NOT touch the other ~20 sites that filter `.eq('status','going')`, because they answer a different question and each needs its own answer. THE LIST, grouped by what they drive: NOTIFICATIONS — app/api/cron/event-reminders (x2), lib/events/cancellation.ts, lib/digest.ts, app/api/zap-prompt. Should someone the host has not approved get a reminder for an event they may not be attending, or a cancellation notice? ATTENDANCE + REWARDS — lib/achievements.ts, lib/onboarding/founder-tasks.ts, lib/events/connectors.ts, lib/events/matching.ts. Does an unapproved request count toward an achievement or a connection suggestion? OPERATOR/AI READS — lib/ai/poster-observer.ts, lib/ai/event-blurb.ts, lib/events/poster-quality.ts, app/(main)/admin/events/load-posted.ts, lib/spaces/tickets.ts (x3), lib/events/store.ts. ⚠️ THE HONEST POSITION IS THAT THESE ARE NOT ALL THE SAME BUG, which is why this is a triage row rather than a sweep and why it was not smuggled into SCAN-105: a cancellation notice probably SHOULD reach a pending requester (their request is moot either way), while an achievement probably should not. Latent today at 0 gated events. Rule each group, then apply. ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1152). 🔴 THE ROW'S OWN ENUMERATION WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS, all caused by its grep matching only the literal `.eq('status', 'going')`. (1) event-reminders is x1, not x2 — the RECIPIENT read was already fixed alongside SCAN-105; only the warm-proof count was open. (2) lib/spaces/tickets.ts x3 is a FALSE POSITIVE: it queries space_ticket_rsvps, a different table with no approval_status column, so the 'fix' would have errored. (3) It MISSED eight sites that filter in JS or in SQL, and two of those were the highest-impact findings in the whole row: `enforce_event_rsvp_capacity()` still counted requests as seats — answering SCAN-105's question the OLD way one layer BELOW the app, so getCapacityInfo said '1 spot left' and the trigger silently rewrote the member's RSVP to waitlist — and it never fired at approval time at all, making rsvp-depth.ts's comment 'the capacity trigger still applies' false for the whole life of the feature. `event_calendar_feed` leaked a hide_address venue to an unapproved requester, through the exemption 20270331000000 granted it on the premise 'every row in it is an event the subscriber is ATTENDING' — a premise approval-gating falsified. Both defects were REPRODUCED against production before the fix: the trigger demoted a third pending request on a two-seat event with zero seats taken, and the feed returned '123 Secret St'. Twelve sites ruled wrong and fixed; the host queue, cancellation notices, the member's own digest and RSVP badge, host-facing reach, the dispatch audience and the GDPR export were ruled CORRECT and deliberately left alone.

entries.title: Vera's dispatch is keyed on the UTC day, so it rolls over at 5pm Pacific

source.ref: dispatchDay(); read by lib/vera-dispatch.ts, app/api/zap-prompt/route.ts, app/(main)/on-air/dispatches/page.tsx

entries.detail: DONE 2026-08-25. PREMISE RE-TESTED AND IT HELD: todayUTC() was still at line 43 and still used at line 230. The key now comes from dispatchDay() = dayInZone(new Date(), HOME_TZ), exported from the leaf module lib/on-air/dispatch-day.ts so there is exactly ONE mint. IT IS A LEAF DELIBERATELY: defining it in lib/vera-dispatch.ts (where it started) would have dragged lib/ai/complete.ts -> lib/ai/client.ts, which VALUE-imports the Anthropic SDK, into the Zap route bundle - the AGENTS.md fan-out rule, and a contradiction of that routes own header saying it has no AI dependency. THE ROW UNDER-COUNTED THE READERS: two other surfaces derived the same key with their own toISOString().slice(0,10) and would have silently disagreed with the new one. app/api/zap-prompt/route.ts backs the most-tapped button in the app and looks up todays cached Dispatch by day - left as it was it would have missed every Dispatch after ~5pm Pacific and fallen back to the template line; it now imports dispatchDay. Its nudge-line hour had the same 5pm bug (getUTCHours put the tonight copy on screen 9am-4pm Pacific and never in the evening) and now reads the community hour via zoneOffsetMinutes. app/(main)/on-air/dispatches/page.tsx labels Today/Yesterday against the same imported function, and its 5-paragraph comment explaining why the label had to stay UTC is replaced (it was honest when written; SCAN-106 moved the key and the label together, which is what it asked for). COMMUNITY DAY, NOT MEMBER DAY, deliberately: lib/member-day.ts exists and is right for practice_logs.logged_for, which MEASURES a members own behaviour. This is a DELIVERY key under UNIQUE (profile_id, day) with no zone column stored beside it, so it must mean the same thing on every read forever. profiles.home_timezone is NULLABLE and MUTABLE (written from the browser by app/(main)/timezone-actions.ts), so a member-keyed day changes meaning between two reads minutes apart - unset zone mints under UTC (leaving this bug unfixed for exactly those members), the client then persists America/Los_Angeles, and the next session that evening finds no row and mints a SECOND Dispatch; travel does it in reverse and SKIPS a day. dayInZone(now, HOME_TZ) is a pure function of the instant. SHIPPING NOTE, unchanged from the original row and deliberately NOT papered over: members served in the 5pm-midnight Pacific window before the deploy can be minted one extra Dispatch, and (second-order, not in the original row) that orphaned tomorrow-keyed row will replay as tomorrows instead of a fresh one. Both one-time, copy valid either way. A dual-key read was rejected as permanent code for a one-day transition.

Comments are stripped first so a note quoting the old expression cannot pass or fail it. Verified to FAIL on the pre-fix tree.

entries.title: Answer the reconstructed listing_saves migration's open question, and amend the 2026-09 retirement claim it contradicts
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 0. That migration file was reconstructed from live state by the session running the merge queue (#2276) after the 2026-08-25 meta-scan applied the restore to production ahead of its file, which turned check:migrations red on every open branch until the reconstruction landed. Its header records what it could not establish and asks for two things. Both are answerable now. (1) WHY: the restore was DELIBERATE. 20260925000000 dropped listing_saves on the claim '0 code references', and that claim was false - lib/listings/index.ts holds four live .from('listing_saves') sites (saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds / listSavedListings) reached from components/marketplace/save-listing-button.tsx on the /housing index and detail pages. Every path failed SAFE (the write discarded its error, the reads fell back to an empty set), so the heart flipped and silently reset on reload, and the saves tests mock the client so nothing caught it. THE READER THAT NEEDS THE TABLE is that button. (2) The retirement claim in 20260925000000 is contradicted by production and wants amending in place - not by editing the reconstructed file, which correctly describes an apply that already happened. An ADR recording the restore + the false-orphan lesson belongs with it. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1144). 🔴 AND THIS ROW'S OWN ANSWER WAS WRONG, which is the finding. It asserted the retirement claim 'was false'. It was TRUE. The local clone was SHALLOW - 71 commits - so the order could not be read; `git fetch --deepen=500` reaches 681 and settles it: 20260925000000 landed 2026-07-07 (#1606) verifying 0 code references, and lib/listings/index.ts gained its four .from('listing_saves') sites on 2026-07-27 (#1967), TWENTY DAYS LATER. So the defect is the mirror of a bad retirement: a feature was built against a table that had already been dropped, and it NEVER WORKED - the heart flipped on click and reset on reload from the day it shipped, which is also why the restored table holds zero rows. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and both generalise. (1) IT COMPILED: db() in lib/listings/index.ts returns createAdminClient() typed as a bare SupabaseClient with NO Database generic, so the generated types - which were CORRECT, having dropped the table - were never consulted. A typed client would have failed the build that introduced the calls. (2) IT WAS SILENT: the writes discarded their error, the reads fell back empty, and lib/listings/saves.test.ts drove a stub whose resolve() hardcoded error: null, so it could not produce a database error of ANY kind. #2288 had already fixed half of it by making the writes throw - but that branch shipped with no test, because the stub could not reach it. This change gives the stub an error channel and adds the three arms (save throws, unsave throws, the reads still fail safe), each mutation-proven. The amendment lands in 20260925000000 as a NOTE rather than a retraction, since its premise held on the day it was written. The other five tables in that sweep were re-checked: zero .from(...)/.rpc(...) sites across app/, lib/ and components/. ⚠️ THE GENERAL HAZARD IS THE UNTYPED HANDLE, NOT THE SWEEP: '0 references' is a fact about one day, and nothing stopped a later branch from writing against the dropped table.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const R="supabase/migrations/20260925000000_retire_orphaned_tables_and_functions.sql";if(!fs.existsSync(R)){console.error("the retirement migration is gone: "+R);process.exit(1)}const r=fs.readFileSync(R,"utf8");if(r.indexOf("listing_saves")<0){console.error("the retirement migration no longer mentions listing_saves; re-point this row");process.exit(1)}if(r.indexOf("AMENDED")<0||r.indexOf("20270327000000")<0){console.error("the retirement migration still stands alone, with no note that listing_saves was later restored - the two files contradict each other again");process.exit(1)}const S="supabase/migrations/20270327000000_restore_listing_saves.sql";if(!fs.existsSync(S)){console.error("the restore migration is gone: "+S);process.exit(1)}const t=fs.readFileSync("lib/listings/saves.test.ts","utf8");if(t.indexOf("const errors: unknown[] = []")<0){console.error("the saves stub lost its error channel, so it can no longer produce a database error and the throw branch is untestable again");process.exit(1)}if(t.indexOf("errors.shift()")<0){console.error("the stub declares an error queue but no longer reads it");process.exit(1)}if(!/rejects\.toThrow\(\/saveListing failed\//.test(t)||!/rejects\.toThrow\(\/unsaveListing failed\//.test(t)){console.error("the write helpers lost their throw-path tests - the branch #2288 added would ship uncovered again");process.exit(1)}const i=fs.readFileSync("lib/listings/index.ts","utf8");if(!/throw new Error\(.saveListing failed/.test(i)||!/throw new Error\(.unsaveListing failed/.test(i)){console.error("a write helper went back to swallowing its error, which is how a dropped table no-opped every save invisibly");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE on both halves. The record half: the retirement migration carries an AMENDED note naming the restore file, so the two stop contradicting each other. The code half: the stub still HAS an error channel and still READS it (a declared-but-unused queue would be the same blind spot wearing a disguise), both write helpers still have throw-path tests, and both still throw. Mutation-proven: reverting either helper to swallow its error, or making a read throw, turns it red.

entries.title: The beta referral contest is removed: the owner ruled there is no contest
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while re-deriving SCAN-502's index, by classifying the dead functions instead of counting them. lib/beta/referral-contest.ts exports runContestSweep, whose own doc reads 'Catch up the contest tally: record any newly-activated referrals and any Circles that have crossed the starter threshold since the last run. Idempotent + bounded, so it is safe to run on a schedule. No-op when the contest flag is off.' It has ZERO callers anywhere in the tree, and none of the 27 crons declared in vercel.json is a referral-contest path. So the catch-up never happens: referrals that activate outside whatever inline path records them, and Circles that cross the starter threshold, are never added to the board. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and wants an owner ruling rather than a patch: whether the contest is meant to be live at all. The function no-ops when betaReferralContestEnabled() is false, so wiring a cron is safe either way — but wiring a schedule for a contest the owner has parked would be building on a decision nobody made. THE FIX IF IT IS LIVE: an /api/cron/referral-contest route wrapped in withCronHeartbeat, plus its vercel.json entry — the same shape as the 27 that exist. THE FIX IF IT IS NOT: delete the sweep, and say so, so the next dead-export pass does not re-find it. ── 🔴 CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, BEFORE THIS ROW SHIPPED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE ROW. The sentence above says the catch-up never happens; an earlier draft of it, and the PR body that carried it, went further and said THE CONTEST NEVER TALLIES. That is FALSE, and I wrote it by reading one function's callers instead of its siblings'. BOTH RECORDERS ARE WIRED INLINE: recordReferralActivation is called from lib/qr/referral.ts:121 inside releaseReferralReward, which /api/cron/referral-release runs on a schedule that DOES exist; and recordCircleStarterMilestone is called from app/(main)/circles/actions.ts:233 on a membership change. So the contest tallies fine on the happy path, and the board is not empty. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the SAFETY NET: runContestSweep exists precisely because someone expected the inline hooks to miss cases — an activation that arrives without passing through releaseReferralReward, or a circle that crosses ten actives by a path that does not run that action — and nothing re-checks for those. Severity drops from 'a feature does not work' to 'a reconciliation pass nobody runs', which is a real but much smaller gap. ⚠️ THE LESSON IS THIS SESSION'S OWN, TURNED ON ME: I classified a dead export by reading its doc comment and its own caller count, and did not check whether its siblings covered the same ground. ADR-1145 says a doc comment is not evidence of a caller; it is equally not evidence of ABSENCE of one elsewhere. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 BY OWNER RULING: there is no beta referral contest. That settles the fork this row named, and it settles it at the wider scope, because the whole feature was provably inert: platform_flags.beta_referral_contest was FALSE, beta_referrals held 0 rows, reward_grants held 0 beta_contest.* grants, and app/(main)/referral/page.tsx called notFound() while the flag was off, so no member could reach it. REMOVED: lib/beta/referral-contest.ts (423 lines) and its test, the /referral route (page + its copy-link client component, which nothing else imported — components/spaces/invite-form.tsx has its own local CopyLink), the recordReferralActivation call in lib/qr/referral.ts and the recordCircleStarterMilestone call in app/(main)/circles/actions.ts, three now-pointless vi.mock lines in the circles tests, and a stale cross-reference in lib/zaps.ts. ⚠️ THE TABLE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT: public.beta_referrals (0 rows) stays for now, because the repo's own sequencing — stated in 20260925000000's header about commerce_variants — is drop the WRITE, deploy, THEN drop the table. Doing both in one change is exactly the shape ADR-1144 was written about. Filed as SCAN-511.

entries.title: eslint warnings were never ratcheted, so the two that existed could never be the last two
entries.detail: MS25 close-out. Verifying merged main turned up two eslint warnings and, behind them, the reason there were exactly two: `pnpm lint` was bare `eslint`, with no --max-warnings, so a warning has NEVER failed the required `lint` job. Zero warnings was a state nobody was holding, not a floor. BOTH WARNINGS WERE REAL DEFECTS, not noise. (1) app/(main)/events/admin-actions.ts declared a `PlaceTimeRow` type nothing referenced, under a heading claiming when/where lived in its own admin module, `event-place-time-module`. No such module exists and none ever did for events: `place` is a spine slot only `circle.placeAndTime` fills (lib/admin/modules/registry.ts), and an event edits its when/where in event-settings-module.tsx against lib/studio/entities/event.ts. The type was a strict subset of EventAdminRow kept in step with it by nobody - a second declaration of the same row shape, which is the drift class the Studio contract exists to prevent. Type deleted, heading corrected to describe the one live thing under it (readRsvpWindow). (2) lib/qr/client-download.ts fell back to `window.location.href = <relative /api/qr URL>` when client-side rasterisation failed. The rule that flagged it was right to flag it and WRONG IN ITS REMEDY: it suggests router.push(), which at an /api route client-navigates and downloads nothing. A code download is a file fetch, so it wanted an <a download> all along - and the anchor is strictly safer, because assigning location unloads the page and depends on the server's Content-Disposition to bring the member back, so a missing header dropped them on a raw PNG instead of on the code they were downloading. THE RATCHET IS THE ACTUAL FIX: --max-warnings=0 added to the lint script CI already runs as a required context, proven green on the merged tree BEFORE wiring (0 errors, 0 warnings) and proven to FIRE by a mutation - a re-added unused `DeadShape` type turned it red at exit 1. The first mutation attempt used `_Unused` and did not fire, because the rule exempts /^_/; recorded because a control that cannot fail reads as coverage (ADR-970) and this one nearly shipped as exactly that. ADR-1142 records it, including the half that turned inward: this row's own probe was written in the safer single-quoted style and check:backlog REFUSED IT, because its quote rule counted double quotes unconditionally - blind to a bare single quote inside a single-quoted body, and rejecting the very style its own failure message recommends. The rule now derives the hazard from the quote that OPENED the body, with all four cases pinned in backlog-contract.test.ts.

That is the consequence - the ratchet is what holds the tree at zero on every future PR, so re-running eslint here would cost minutes and prove only today. The two instance arms are paired positive/negative, so deleting a file wholesale fails instead of passing. ⚠️ IT STRIPS COMMENT LINES FIRST, and must: the fix's own comments name `PlaceTimeRow` and location.href verbatim to explain why they are gone, so a naive grep would flag its own explanation. ⚠️ AND IT IS `node -e` UNDER SINGLE SHELL QUOTES with indexOf rather than regex. The first version used double quotes and escaped regex classes, the escaping mangled the -e argument, node fell through to reading stdin, and the probe HUNG - which check-backlog correctly scored `unprovable` rather than passing. It sat in the unprovable bucket looking like coverage. Same family as the SCAN-210 probe that carried a double quote.

entries.title: /events loader: serial settings cluster + counting RSVPs by fetching every row
entries.detail: DONE 2026-08-25. HALF THE ROW HAD ALREADY EXPIRED. (a) THE SERIAL SETTINGS CLUSTER WAS FIXED BEFORE THIS ROW WAS WORKED, by #2290 (922febc66, Meta-scan phase 3) - the four awaits the row cites at :350/:370/:382/:388 are real, but they are the PRE-#2290 file; the current loader already gathers all five reads (resolvePageContent, eventsListingHorizonDays, demoModeEnabled, viewerHidesDemo, getSeriesDisplayConfig) into one Promise.all. Confirmed by running the new probe against 922febc66^, where all five arms fire, and against HEAD, where none do. Nothing to do; the probe now guards it against regression. (b) THE RSVP COUNT WAS REAL AND WAS WORSE THAN A PERF ROW. The loader pulled every going row for up to 3 x SERIES_WIDE_READ = 1,500 events to tally integers in JS, and PostgREST caps a response at max_rows (1,000) SERVER-SIDE, which neither service_role nor .limit() escapes - so past 1,000 going rows in one listing the counts silently under-reported with no error, flipping the Has open spots facet ON for a full event and mis-ordering the Most going sort. Now lib/events/going-counts.ts: prefers a grouped-count RPC, chunks ids 500 at a time so a full response can never be a truncated one, and FAILS SAFE to the original tally - now PAGED with .range() over the PK - whenever the RPC is absent or errors. A partial RPC result is discarded rather than merged, so it can never double-count. 13 unit tests in lib/events/going-counts.test.ts, including a fake client that reproduces the max_rows cap. THE MIGRATION IS WRITTEN AND UNAPPLIED: supabase/migrations/20270329000000_event_going_counts_rpc.sql (owner applies). The fallback is what makes merging it before the apply safe. OTHER .in() READS IN THE SAME WAVE, MEASURED: myRsvpRows is safe by the event_rsvps_event_profile_uniq constraint (<=1 row per event per profile); circlesRows is bounded by distinct hosting circles (theoretical only); tierRows is STILL EXPOSED - active ticket tiers scale as events x tiers with no bound, so past 1,000 the trailing events silently lose their From  price stat. That last one is out of this rows scope and is documented in the loader, needing its own row.

entries.title: Verify-then-add loading.tsx on the hot child routes that block above the shell
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 4. Verify-first, and the verify was most of the answer. The inventory looked for a loading.tsx IN each folder; Next 16 puts the boundary at the SEGMENT — loading.js wraps page.js and every NESTED layout.js below it, never the layout in its own folder. So three of the six named routes were already covered by an ancestor: channels/[id] by app/(main)/channels/loading.tsx, messages/r/[roomId] by messages/loading.tsx, journeys/[slug] by journeys/loading.tsx. A fourth, bare "spaces", is not a route at all — there is no app/(main)/spaces/page.tsx; the index is /spaces/directory. drafts and spaces/directory have no ancestor boundary and need none: both open their own <Suspense> around everything expensive, with only the request-cached caller above it, and no awaiting layout in between. ONE route genuinely blocked: spaces/[slug]. Its (profile) layout resolves the caller, the manage grant, tagline, visibility, follow state, founding badge, capabilities, reviews and the profile nav before rendering a node, with no boundary anywhere between it and app/(main)/layout.tsx {children} — the page own <Suspense> sits UNDER that layout, so it never gets to paint. Added app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/loading.tsx, at [slug] rather than inside (profile) for the same reason circles/[slug]/loading.tsx sits where it does (a file in the layout own folder renders inside it), which also covers the Space owner routes. entries.title: The four commerce sitemap reads cap at 100 rows with no paging
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 2. store/market/housing/classifieds read limit:100 (circles 200) with no follow-up paging. PREMISE EXPIRED THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN: the row offered two remedies (page it, or record the cap with a threshold that reopens it) and #2289 shipped the second one hours later in the same file — the cap note at sitemap.ts:60-105, named COMMERCE_SITEMAP_CAP / CIRCLE_SITEMAP_CAP constants, and atCap(), which warns per section naming the reader to page. Paging is genuinely out of reach from here and the note proves it per reader (three clamp server-side, classifieds takes no offset, circles is an RPC SQL ceiling), so the ONLY thing missing was a gate that notices the fail-safe fired. Added: four tests in app/sitemap.test.ts that drive the real route. They pin the warning at the cap, the silence one row below it (a positive control, so silence means not-at-cap rather than never-warns), and the invariant that makes a silent regression possible — the shared constant must equal the clamp the readers enforce, because raising it would leave the three clamped verticals returning 100 while atCap compared against the bigger number and never fired again. entries.title: One trim sweep over the ~154 lib modules carrying dead exports
entries.detail:
MS25 Phase 5. RE-SCOPED 2026-08-25 by an exact-identifier index over the whole tree (the original number came from a token-presence scan, which under-reports by construction). Two findings changed the row. (1) THE ORIGINAL SCAN MISSES .mts: lib/help/drift.ts and lib/ai/autodoc.ts scored fully dead and are both LIVE, consumed by scripts/help-drift.mts and scripts/help-autodoc.mts. Any sweep that skips .mts/.cts/.cjs/.yml deletes live code — this is the load-bearing correction. (2) ~85% of the row is not deletable: of 860 dead value exports across 707 lib modules, 734 are used INSIDE their own file, so the sweep for those is dropping the `export` keyword, not deleting. Only 126 are declaration-only. Exactly one module is fully dead — lib/help/drift.ts — and that one is the false positive above. So this is an API-surface trim plus a small delete list, not the M-sized code sweep the row described. A ranked 15 is scoped (each with all four searches clean), with three flagged for a ruling before touching, not a sweep: lib/verticals/registry.ts, lib/nav/admin-rail.ts and lib/admin/modules/spine.ts are registry/menu-adjacent — a parallel rail registry with no consumer is a MENU-CONTRACT finding in its own right. Two items carried over from SCAN-501: useEditMode().toggle (no caller since EditModeButton went) and offersPeriod (internal-only now; unexport, and its own test updates with it). Excluded on purpose: lib/profile/spotlight-flags.ts belongs to SCAN-501. ── ⚠️ RE-DERIVED AND RE-CLASSIFIED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1145). The index is now a committed, documented report — scripts/maintenance/dead-exports.mjs — rather than a number in a row, so the next reader re-runs it instead of trusting this sentence. Reading: 6,137 files walked, 5,765 consumers (INCLUDING .mts/.cts/.cjs/.mjs/.yml/.json/.md/.sql), 1,213 lib modules, 7,688 attributable exports, 1,343 dead outside their own file, 45 DECLARATION-ONLY. 🔴 AND THE ROW'S FRAMING NEEDS A CORRECTION: 'an API-surface trim' is only two thirds true. Classifying the 19 unreferenced lib FUNCTIONS by hand splits them three ways, and only one third is safe to delete blindly. (a) BUILT BUT NEVER WIRED: runContestSweep (lib/beta/referral-contest.ts) documents itself 'idempotent + bounded, so it is safe to run on a schedule' and NONE of the 27 crons in vercel.json calls it, so the beta referral contest never tallies. Deleting it removes a finished feature; filed as SCAN-510. (b) GENUINELY RETIRED WITH A STALE DOC: spaceTrailingProcessedCents still cites ADR-552 for the "you'd have saved $X" upgrade nudge, but billing-body.tsx records that ADR-811 RETIRED that nudge. The code is dead and its own comment advertises a feature that no longer exists — which is exactly how it reads as a gap when it is not. (c) CONVENIENCE WRAPPERS, the majority: dropping the `export` keyword is the whole change. ⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the same one SCAN-508 landed on from the other side: a doc comment is not evidence of a caller. Two of the three categories are indistinguishable from their comments alone.

── 🔎 RE-RUN AND TRIAGED 2026-08-25, no code moved yet; this is the scoping the sweep needs before it touches anything. `scripts/maintenance/dead-exports.mjs` now reads 6,150 files / 5,778 consumers / 1,213 lib modules / 7,678 attributable exports / 1,343 dead outside their own file / **45 declaration-only**. Two of the row's named examples are already gone from that list: `runContestSweep` went with SCAN-510, and `spaceTrailingProcessedCents` no longer appears.
  THE 45 SPLIT THREE WAYS BY RISK, and the split is the point — a single sweep over all of them would be wrong in two directions at once:
  • 6 are under `resonance/` and belong to DEF-RESON, which is GO-gated. NOT this row's to touch.
  • 7 are declared in a `types.ts`. A type exported from a module literally named types.ts is plausibly deliberate public surface, and 'nothing imports it yet' is not the same as 'nothing should'. Each needs a per-item read, not a rule.
  • 32 are the rest, and those are where the sweep actually lives.
  ⚠️ TWO OF THE 32 LOOKED LIKE UNENFORCED GATES AND WERE CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because a gate nothing calls is a correctness bug, not hygiene. Both came back clean:
  • `aiDepthFor` (lib/spaces/function-access.ts) is a re-export of `spaceAiDepth`, and the real one IS live — app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/crm/crm-body.tsx:150 and lib/spaces/entitlements.ts:246. Safe wrapper, category (c).
  • `canSellTickets` wraps `ticketSellerVerdict`, and THAT one has no real caller either: its only other mention in the tree is a COMMENT in lib/pricing/gates.ts:74 saying the predicate 'is what Phase 1 reversed' (ADR-914). The live wall is elsewhere and is stronger — lib/billing/tickets.ts checks `payoutsLive()` at BOTH money entry points (:162 create, :690 refund) and reads `getConnectStatus`. **No hole; do not read this row as a payout finding.**
  🔴 BUT IT IS A REAL CATEGORY-(b) FINDING, and a worse-than-average one. THREE separate comments in the tree point the next reader at this module as the place the rule lives — components/marketplace/events-header-actions.tsx:17, components/crew/upgrade-lightbox.tsx:18 and app/(main)/events/index-data.ts:305 all say 'the wall now lives at the price field (lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts)'. The half of that module they would land on (`ticketSellerVerdict`, `canSellTickets`, `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT`, and the three types feeding them) is dead. The module is NOT dead — `TICKETS_NOT_READY` is imported by lib/billing/tickets.ts:31 — so this is a partial retirement with three signposts still pointing at the retired half. Deleting the dead half means fixing three comments in the same change, or the signposts start pointing at nothing.
  NEXT: work the 32, item by item, with the three-way category call recorded per item. The types.ts seven and the resonance six stay out of scope until someone rules on them.

── ✅ ALL 32 CLASSIFIED 2026-08-25, each one independently verified rather than trusted from the report: a whole-tree grep across .ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.mjs/.cjs/.json/.md/.sql returned **exactly one reference for every one of the 32 — its own declaration line**. No consumers, no tests, no docs, no SQL. The report's 'declaration-only' call is confirmed.
  🔴 AND THAT IS WHY MOST OF THEM MUST NOT BE DELETED. Reading each one's own doc comment splits the 32 far more sharply than the row's three categories did:

  (a) FINISHED CAPABILITY, NEVER WIRED — 13 of 32. Deleting these removes working code and the only record that the capability was built. Each is a product question, not hygiene:
      · uncompleteLesson          'Undo a lesson completion (toggle off)' — a member can complete a
                                  lesson and cannot un-complete it.
      · updateBlock               'Edit a block's title/body' — Journey blocks can be created and
                                  not edited.
      · setEventIntakeInputs      persists the intake INPUTS jsonb (consent, source notes). A
                                  consent persister with no caller is worth its own look.
      · listRelationships         the ACTIVE relationships for a CRM contact.
      · listAcceptedSharesForSpace  'the events another host brought here'.
      · getRecording / listAttachmentsOfRecording  Airwaves reads; the second one's comment names a
                                  view ('used in N places') that does not exist.
      · saveSplashOverride        the writer beside a getter.
      · resolvePlaceSelectorProfileIds  messaging place-selector resolution.
      · memberInRecovery          'should surface a banner' — the dunning banner is unbuilt (billing
                                  is OFF, so this one is expected-dark).
      · resolveViewerGamification 'e.g. the leaderboard compete affordance'.
      · THEME_PRESETS             'One-tap starting points' for the Spotlight editor — a whole preset
                                  feature with no consumer.
      · PREFILL_THRESHOLD         the 'pre-select the guess but flag it for review' tier of the CRM
                                  import confidence system. AUTO_THRESHOLD beside it IS live, so the
                                  two-tier design shipped as one tier.

  (b) RETIRED WITH LIVE SIGNPOSTS — the ticket-eligibility half. Escalated to its own row, LIVE-126,
      because it turned out not to be dead code at all. See that row.

  (c) GENUINELY INERT — the remainder: appendSignature, aiDepthFor, resolvedAmounts, locationSummary,
      resetGoogleMapsLoaderForTests, BLURHASH_ALPHABET, JOURNEY_FULL_MESSAGE, DEFAULT_BLOCK_MARGIN,
      DEFAULT_FUNNEL_STYLE, the vocabulary arrays (STAGE_KINDS, TASK_FILTERS,
      FOLLOWER_REMINDER_LEADS, COLUMN_VALUES, SPACE_LOCATION_PRECISIONS, AI_DEPTH_CAPABILITY_KEYS)
      and the three types (StoredHarvest, DesignBlockType, FieldChoices). Even here two carry a
      claim worth noting rather than deleting silently: BLURHASH_ALPHABET is 'exported so a validator
      can check a string' and there is no validator, and locationSummary is 'the one-line summary the
      settings form shows back' and the form does not show it.

  🔵 THE ROW CANNOT CLOSE ON A SWEEP ANY MORE, and that is the finding. 'Trim ~154 lib modules carrying dead exports' assumed a hygiene task. Thirteen of the 32 are finished features nobody wired; deleting them is a product decision about whether the capability is wanted, and it needs an owner ruling per group rather than a blanket answer. The (c) list is the only part a sweep can take, and it is worth roughly twenty lines.

── ✅ setEventIntakeInputs INVESTIGATED FIRST, ON THE OWNER'S RULING, AND IT IS NOT A CONSENT GAP. I flagged it as 'a consent persister with no caller' above; that framing was wrong and the investigation is the correction.
  • CONSENT IS CAPTURED AT CREATION. `createEventIntake` (lib/events/seed/store.ts:83) inserts `inputs: input.inputs`, and `inputs` carries `consent`. Both live doors build it — from-scan.ts:62 and from-chat.ts:53. `setEventIntakeInputs` is only the UPDATE path, i.e. 'change the consent or source notes afterwards'. Nothing calls it, which is an unwired edit, not a missing capture.
  • THE POSTURE IS SAFE BY DEFAULT, and it is stated in both doors' headers: 'Every staged event is a DEMO (consent.isDemo): the apply materializes it as an unlisted [event]'. Everything read out of a scan or a chat is marked demo and lands unlisted, so third-party material cannot become a public listing by omission.
  • WHAT IS GENUINELY UNBUILT is the PROMOTION path. `organizerConfirmed` — 'Set once the real organizer has confirmed they want this event listed' — appears exactly ONCE in the whole tree, its own type declaration at lib/events/seed/intake.ts:40. It is never set and never read, so there is no way to record that an organiser agreed and nothing that would act on it. That is the missing half, and it is a feature gap rather than a compliance one, because the default is unlisted.
  • AND NOTHING HAS GONE THROUGH THE DOOR: `public.event_intake` holds **0 rows**. The seeder has never run in production. So this is latent, to be closed before the seeder is first used, not an incident to chase.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: `setEventIntakeInputs` stays in group (a) as unwired, but it is the LOWEST-urgency member of that group, not the highest as I first read it. Whoever builds the promotion path wires it and `organizerConfirmed` together; whoever decides the seeder is not coming back deletes all three.

── 📋 THE 13 TRIAGED BUILD-OR-DELETE, 2026-08-25, per the owner's ruling. Method: for each, ask whether the SURFACE that would call it exists, is half-built, or was never started — by grepping app/ and components/ for the sibling writer, the table name and the module path. Nothing deleted; this is the list to rule on.

  BUILD — the surface exists and only this half is missing (4):
   1. uncompleteLesson      `completeLesson` IS wired at app/(main)/journeys/[slug]/learn/
                            actions.ts. A member can tick a lesson and cannot untick it. The
                            smallest real member-facing gap in the whole list.
   2. listAcceptedSharesForSpace  event-share is live on three surfaces including
                            spaces/[slug]/settings/calendar/page.tsx. A Space's calendar can share
                            OUT and cannot show what other hosts shared IN.
   3. THEME_PRESETS         lib/spotlight/theme is imported by three surfaces, so the Spotlight
                            theme editor is live; the 'one-tap starting points' it was built with
                            are simply never offered.
   4. PREFILL_THRESHOLD     confirmed: AUTO_THRESHOLD is used inside map.ts:334 and by its test,
                            so the auto-apply tier IS live and the 'pre-select but flag for review'
                            tier is not. The wizard (components/crm/import/import-wizard.tsx) is
                            the surface. A two-tier design shipped as one tier.

  DELETE — a second, unused way to do something the live code already does (4):
   5. memberInRecovery      resolveMemberPaymentState is called DIRECTLY by

                            The banner exists; this is a redundant convenience over it.

entries.title: Route chunks have no weight gate: the shell gate's documented blind spot
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 5. check:shell-weight watches the app shell's eager JS and named admin fingerprints, but a heavy library statically imported by a route-level client component (SCAN-302's react-markdown) is invisible to it. A small fingerprint gate over the member hot-route chunks (feed/events/circles/messages) closes the class, not just the instance. CLOSED 2026-08-25 as ARM C of check:shell-weight, and it is a FINGERPRINT arm, never a budget: from each member hot route page.tsx (feed/events/circles/messages — page, not layout, because the layout IS the shell Arms A/B already measure) it walks the static import graph, marks everything below the first `use client` boundary as client code, and fails if a NAMED heavy module is statically imported inside that subtree. What it can prove without a build is the half a build cannot prove cheaply: a static import below a client boundary is not code-split by any bundler setting, so "statically reachable" IS "in that route first-load JS". dynamic() and bare import() are not static edges and are correctly invisible. It CANNOT see bytes or a chunking change — only Arms A/B can, and only on the artifact. Reading on the real tree: 0 leaks, 668 client modules walked across the four routes, 2 detector controls firing. IT LIVES IN THE CI HALF (scripts/check-shell-weight.test.ts), NOT in postbuild, for two reasons: main() only runs on Vercel, i.e. after the merge, and a filesystem-only arm has no reason to wait for a build; and in postbuild it broke the artifact arms own mutation fixtures, which run the script from a cwd that is deliberately not this repo, where its controls do not exist. Teaching it to skip when the source tree is absent would have given it a way to pass without looking (ADR-970). Two controls keep it honest: two REAL client files that genuinely import a heavy library today, and a 150-module walk floor against 668 measured. Proven by mutation: a static react-markdown import added to components/feed/post-replies.tsx turns it red and names the chain feed/page.tsx -> feed-list.tsx -> post-card.tsx -> post-replies.tsx.

entries.title: The app-space-console visual baseline is 21px stale, so pr-compare is red on every PR that reaches it
entries.detail: MS25 Phase 0. The @visual suite's four app-space-console checks (/spaces/<slug>/manage, dawn-light + dawn-dark, desktop + mobile) fail on EVERY branch that runs them, with the baseline 21px shorter than what the app now renders. entries.title: Every public event advertised a start time seven hours early to search and answer engines
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving the real builders and reading their OUTPUT rather than their source. `events.starts_at` stores the WALL CLOCK as UTC parts (lib/time/zone.ts), and eventSchema published it raw. Measured against production: `breathe-connect-expand-2026-08-27` starts 6:30pm Pacific and its Event node said `2026-08-27T18:30:00Z`, which every consumer reads as 11:30am. All five upcoming public events were wrong, and so was the /events ItemList. This is SCAN-101 on the SEO surface — the same convention read as an instant, which in SQL closed the guest RSVP door before lunch. CLOSED: lib/time/zone.ts gains eventIsoWithOffset, which keeps the host wall clock and attaches the zone offset AT THAT INSTANT, and both builders use it. Its own test found a defect while being written — reading the offset independently disagreed with eventInstant by an hour inside the spring-forward gap — so the offset is now derived from eventInstant own answer and the two cannot disagree by construction. THREE ASSERTIONS IN lib/jsonld.test.ts WERE PINNING THE BUG and were updated. ⏳ FOLLOW-UP: public_events / public_event_by_slug do not return time_zone, so the /discover pages fall back to the community zone. Correct for 61 of 61 events today; widening those RPCs is the durable fix.
