entries.title: The /events ticket-tier read truncates at max_rows, so trailing events silently lose their from-price
entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 while closing SCAN-303, by measuring the OTHER .in() reads in the same loader rather than stopping at the one the row named. PostgREST caps a response at max_rows (1000, supabase/config.toml) SERVER-SIDE: service_role does not escape it and .limit() does not raise it. Active ticket tiers scale as events x tiers and are bounded by neither, so past 1,000 rows the trailing events silently lose "From $X" — the same truncation class as ADR-962 (CRM import dedupe), ADR-969 (QR capture counts) and SCAN-303 itself, which is now the FOURTH occurrence. The other two reads in that loader were measured and are safe: myRsvpRows is bounded by event_rsvps_event_profile_uniq (at most one row per event per profile) and circlesRows by the number of distinct hosting circles. FIX: the same shape SCAN-303 used — chunk the input well under the cap, or aggregate in the database, and fail safe. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25. Premise re-tested first (ADR-1082): the read was still a single unbounded .in(), and production carried 2 active tiers on 1 event against 60 published events — so this is the first of the five caught BEFORE it fired rather than by its consequence. 🔴 CHUNKING THE INPUT WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, and that is the difference from SCAN-303: that RPC returns at most one row per id, so 500 ids bounded the response. Tiers are many-per-event, so 500 ids at 5 tiers each is 2,500 rows and truncates just the same. The response had to be bounded AT THE SOURCE, so the fix is an AGGREGATE — event_tier_price_summary (20270332000000, applied, ledger repaired to the repo version, 640 to 640) returns exactly one row per event carrying the three things the label needs: tier_count, min_priced_cents and has_flexible. lib/events/tier-prices.ts prefers it and falls back to a PAGED read folded locally, so the migration was safe to merge unapplied. A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE was found while wiring it: lib/spaces/content-data.ts ran its own raw .in() for the Space card. It was bounded — listEventsForSpace caps at 24 — but only loosely, since 24 events at 42 tiers each still reaches 1,000, and a bound that depends on nobody building a long ticket ladder is not a bound. Both surfaces now share the helper, and eventPriceLabel was RETIRED rather than left as a second definition of the label. ⚠️ THE MIGRATION'S OWN PROBE CAUGHT TWO OF MY ERRORS BEFORE ANYTHING LANDED, both applies failing atomically with no function, no ledger row and no probe rows left behind: a fixture built on pricing_mode 'sliding' (the schema allows fixed/free/pwyc/sliding_scale/donation), and a grant that revoked from PUBLIC only — Supabase's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES (ADR-959) grants EXECUTE to anon and authenticated as NAMED roles, so both must be named in the revoke. That is the ADR-964 shape one level over: there it was column grants nobody narrowed, here a function grant that arrives pre-opened. 27 tests, four of them mutation-proven to fire, including an 8-case arm pinning the new path against the RETIRED implementation preserved verbatim as an oracle.

entries.title: Scoped rooms and three USING(true) tables admit anon with no identity check

source.ref: the authenticated verdicts the gate cannot verify

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 in the final security pass, and filed rather than fixed because both need a policy decision rather than a patch. (1) `rooms_read_public_or_member` admits `visibility IN (circle, hub, nexus, outpost, channel)` with NO identity check at all, and room_messages / room_members carry the same channel branch. Live: anon reads the one channel room metadata; messages and members return 200 [] rather than 42501, so only EMPTINESS is withholding them today — and room_messages is in the realtime publication. (2) dispatch_poll_votes, spotlight_top_friends and listing_comments have `USING (true)` with the anon grant intact; poll votes carry (profile_id, option_id) on member-only dispatches. Latent at 0 rows, which is exactly when it is cheap to fix. ⚠️ THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: of the tables verdicted `authenticated`, 65 were PROVEN to filter anon against real data, and 72 more are empty and therefore prove nothing. These findings live in that second group, which is the group table-grants.txt says the gate cannot verify. The other side is clean: 79 of 79 `internal` tables fail closed with 42501. ── ✅ RULED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25 (ADR-1149). OWNER RULING: TIGHTEN BOTH. 20270334000000 applied; ledger repaired to the repo version and verified as an EXACT BIJECTION by hash, not just by count (642 ⇄ 642, md5 e870925394181ea1cd8d0a2c48c7abac on both sides). ROOMS: the three scoped branches now require an authenticated caller; `visibility = 'public'` stays open to anon and membership still grants what it always did. Identity rather than membership, deliberately — browsing a circle's rooms before joining is a plausible flow and there is no data to say whether it is used, so this row closes the anon hole rather than redesigning room visibility. THE THREE TABLES: poll votes scope to your OWN vote, top friends to the OWNER's rows, listing_comments to `authenticated` (it is public-adjacent community content on public listings, so owner-scoping would be wrong rather than merely strict; what it stops is a signed-out bulk enumeration). ✅ WHY IT WAS FREE, AND THE CHECK THAT MADE IT SAFE: every application reader of all three tables goes through createAdminClient(), which bypasses RLS entirely, so those policies served NO application path — they only widened what the publishable anon key could ask PostgREST for. The rooms side is the same: the one non-admin reader (app/(main)/messages/popover-actions.ts) already calls auth.getUser() and scopes to the caller's own memberships. That question is not a formality — 20270330000000 nearly shipped as a blanket table revoke until app/discover/events/_data.ts turned out to be the ONE anon reader of 245 sites. ⚠️ AND A SECOND PASS WENT FURTHER THAN THE POLICIES: anon's SELECT GRANT was revoked on all five tables that have no anon path, because a policy the caller misses returns 200 [] — the very shape this row criticised ('only EMPTINESS is withholding them') — while removing the grant makes the same refusal arrive as 42501. public.rooms KEEPS its anon grant on purpose, or the public branch would go with it. VERIFIED AS ROLE ANON AFTER: rooms 1 → 0 readable (the channel room is now withheld, and that is the policy rather than emptiness), messages/members/poll votes/top friends all 0. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 by 20270334000000 + 20270335000000. Production now holds ZERO anon SELECT grants across all six tables and retains all six for authenticated. The follow-up migration exists because the first one spared public.rooms on an unmeasured premise; db-tests failed its positive control and no anon reader of rooms turned out to exist (ADR-1150).

scoped rooms and three USING(true) tables would admit anon again");const b=pick(/rooms_drops_the_vestigial_anon_grant/,"the public.rooms anon-grant revoke is gone; rooms would admit the publishable anon key again");const need=[[/rooms_read_public_or_member/,"the rooms policy"],[/room_messages_read_members/,"the room_messages policy"],[/room_members_read/,"the room_members policy"],[/dispatch_poll_votes/,"dispatch_poll_votes"],[/spotlight_top_friends/,"spotlight_top_friends"],[/listing_comments/,"listing_comments"]];for(const pair of need){if(!pair[0].test(a)){console.error("the migration no longer covers "+pair[1]);process.exit(1)}}if((a.match(/auth\.uid\(\)/g)||[]).length<3){console.error("fewer than three scoped-room branches require identity; the middle branch that asked nothing of the caller is the original bug");process.exit(1)}if(!/revoke select on public\.listing_comments\s+from anon/.test(a)){console.error("the anon SELECT revokes are gone, so a withheld read returns 200 [] rather than 42501 - the exact ambiguity this row named");process.exit(1)}if(!/revoke select on public\.rooms\s+from anon/.test(b)){console.error("public.rooms kept the vestigial anon SELECT grant that no migration ever created - ADR-1150");process.exit(1)}const pairs=[[a,"20270334000000"],[b,"20270335000000"]];for(const p of pairs){if(!/_auth_grants_before/.test(p[0])){console.error(p[1]+" lost its before/after snapshot, so its positive control names an absolute grant again - the defect ADR-1150 records");process.exit(1)}if(!/this took too much/.test(p[0])){console.error(p[1]+" lost its positive control - nothing now fails if a revoke takes more than it meant to");process.exit(1)}}if(!/qual like .%public%./.test(b)){console.error("the public-room discovery control is gone; an authenticated member could lose sight of public rooms silently");process.exit(1)}'
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE across BOTH migrations that carry this row: all six relations covered, at least three auth.uid() branches (one per scoped-room policy), the anon revokes present on all six INCLUDING public.rooms, and each migration still carrying its before/after snapshot plus its "this took too much" arm. The last two matter because the FIRST version of the positive control asserted an absolute grant ("anon lost SELECT on public.rooms"), which db-tests failed on a fresh apply - see ADR-1150. A control stated as a difference is true in every environment; one stated as an absolute is only true in the one it was written against.

entries.title: #2286 (the 2026-08-25 meta-scan) is unmerged, conflicts with main, and is a second agent's in-flight draft

source.ref: the add/add conflict against main's copy of the same version

entries.detail: HANDOFF 2026-08-25 from the merge-queue session that landed #2274, #2276, #2277, #2278, #2279, #2280, #2281, #2282, #2284, #2285 and #2283. #2286 is the ONE open PR that session did not land, and it is blocked on ownership rather than on code: it is a DRAFT belonging to a different agent that was still pushing to it during the queue run (its head moved three times: 44153f2e -> 09e793e8 -> b5908fe8). Pushing a merge commit into a branch another agent is actively rewriting risks colliding with them, so the queue session deliberately did not. ── ITS CONFLICT IS UNDERSTOOD AND CHEAP: two files. (1) docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json — #2286 adds 30 SCAN-* rows; a 3-way merge by row id resolves it with no losses (measured: base 223 / ours 253 / theirs 225 -> 255 entries, 0 duplicate ids, no both-sides row edits). (2) supabase/migrations/20270327000000_restore_listing_saves.sql — an add/add where BOTH SIDES ARE FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL: same table, same PK, same two FKs, same covering index, same private.get_my_profile_id() RLS policy. Main's copy is already merged AND already applied to production, so keep MAIN's file; the only thing worth taking from #2286's copy is its comment block, which answers the question main's copy leaves open (see LIVE-123's sibling finding below). 🔴 DO NOT re-derive the listing_saves provenance: #2286 established it. 20260925000000 dropped public.listing_saves claiming '0 code references', and that claim was FALSE — lib/listings/index.ts holds four live call sites (saveListing / unsaveListing / listSavedListingIds / listSavedListings) reaching the UI through components/marketplace/save-listing-button.tsx and the /housing pages. Every path failed SAFE (the write discarded its error, the reads fell back to 'nothing saved'), so from 2026-09-25 until the restore, hearting a housing listing wrote to a table that did not exist and the heart silently reset on reload. No gate noticed because the saves tests mock the client. NEXT STEP: decide who owns #2286, then resolve those two files and land it, or close it and re-file its 30 SCAN rows. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25, and NOT by merging #2286. That branch reached 112 changed files, and ci.yml's PR-size gate fails anything over 40 unless the title carries [sweep] — owner-directed after a 215-file PR killed production deploys for a day (ADR-1002). [sweep] is reserved for a single-purpose mechanical change where every file takes the same one edit, which a branch carrying four high-severity fixes, an SEO round, a speed round, an a11y round and an orphan sweep is not. So it was split by backlog row, which is the remedy the gate's own message names: #2288 (phase 1, correctness), #2289 (phase 2, SEO/GEO), #2290 (phase 3, speed + a11y) and #2291 (phase 4, hygiene). Four branches off main with DISJOINT paths, each carrying only the rows it closes, each run through the full battery on its OWN branch rather than on the tree it was carved from. That last part earned itself twice: it surfaced two cross-slice dependencies the combined branch could never have shown (two Spark modules importing a FieldError from another slice, and a route-chunk gate that stays red until the slice fixing its instance lands). This row's own conclusions were both confirmed and used: the listing_saves migration kept MAIN's copy, and the provenance it recorded was not re-derived. #2286 itself is closed as superseded, not merged. ADR-1140 §5 records the decision.

verify.evidence: PR #2286 closed as superseded on 2026-08-25 after #2288/#2289/#2290/#2291 replaced it. Each replacement is <= 40 changed files and passed the PR-size gate, which #2286 could not. Split by path with disjoint sets; each verified on its own branch (tsc, eslint, full vitest suite, all 24 contract guards, check:backlog) before push.

entries.title: Every agent hand-resolves the same two ledger-doc conflicts, because the fold tooling is never committed

source.ref: the file half of the conflict; no committed tool folds it or DECISIONS.md

entries.detail: FOUND 2026-08-25 by driving eleven PRs through the queue in one session. EVERY open PR appends to the tail of docs/DECISIONS.md and adds rows to docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json, so EVERY merge to main re-conflicts EVERY other open PR on those exact two files — and on nothing else (verified with `git merge-tree --write-tree` across all remaining branches: the conflict set was those two paths, every time, with zero code conflicts). The queue session hit this eleven times and resolved it eleven times by hand or by throwaway scripts, and this is at least the second session to do so. ── THE TWO RESOLUTIONS ARE MECHANICAL AND ALWAYS THE SAME. DECISIONS.md: both sides append ADR entries at the tail, so keep main's block first and the branch's after (theirs-then-ours), then `node scripts/check-adr.mjs` proves it. BUILD-BACKLOG.json: a 3-way merge BY ROW ID — for each id, if ours == base take theirs, if theirs == base take ours, if both changed STOP and report rather than guess; emit in main's order and append ids only this branch has. Both are ~30 lines. 🔴 THE JSON HALF MUST NOT BE HAND-EDITED: doing so has already produced an invalid file (a dropped `},{` between two rows) and a duplicated row id in this repo's history, each costing a CI round. 🔴 AND IT MUST NOT SILENTLY PICK A WINNER when both sides edited one row: that case is real (HYG-020 was edited on both sides in this session, main holding it `open` and the closing PR holding it `done`) and it needs a human, so the tool must exit non-zero and name the id. Write it to reproduce byte-identical output (the repo file has NO trailing newline; json.dump(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus no final write matches it exactly) or the diff becomes unreviewable. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25: scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.mjs shipped in #2291, and it obeys both 🔴 rules above. It refuses when both sides edited the same row and NAMES the id, which is not theoretical — this very branch is the case: main and the handoff both amended LIVE-123, the tool stopped, and a human folded it (main 06:16 spine, plus the terminal-error finding main was missing). It also gained a CI half, scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.test.ts, and writing that test found three real defects: a trailing newline docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json does not have (one byte, but it costs a spurious last-line hunk on every branch that merges after), a duplicate row id arriving on EITHER side being silently swallowed by new Map() — which would have resolved a conflict by losing a row — and an unguarded main() that shelled out to git on import. The byte-fidelity rule this row wrote down was itself recorded backwards in the tool header; the file was measured with od -c to settle it.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const c=['scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.mjs','scripts/maintenance/fold-ledger-docs.js'];if(!c.some(p=>fs.existsSync(p))){console.error('no committed fold tool for docs/DECISIONS.md + docs/BUILD-BACKLOG.json: every agent re-solves the same two conflicts by hand');process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"
verify.note: Probes for the tool that must EXIST, which is the consequence itself. Its CI half is auto-discovered by vitest, so the rules cannot rot unnoticed.

entries.title: 🔴 PICK THIS UP FIRST: #2283 is unmerged and the migration ledger is deliberately one row AHEAD of main until it lands

source.ref: the two-step apply/ledger-repair protocol; 20270326000000 lives on #2283, not yet on main

entries.detail: HANDOFF 2026-08-25 06:00 UTC, and the FIRST thing the next thread should read. #2283 (housing/natal-matching, head dac3a9d96) is the last PR of the merge queue. THIRTEEN of its fourteen checks are green — checks, lint, test, CodeQL, analyze, db-tests, drift, autodoc, preflight all passed — and it is blocked on ONE thing: its Vercel preview stalled at 'Collecting page data' (see LIVE-123; this is that bug's SECOND occurrence). ── 🔴 WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE ABANDONED. production's migration ledger currently holds 635 rows while main's tree holds 634 files, because the ledger row `20270326000000 natal_chart_matching` was restored BEFORE the merge, which the sequence requires: check:migrations runs pre-merge, so a PR carrying a migration file reads repoOnly drift unless its row is already there. That means main is in a deliberate, temporary ledgerOnly drift RIGHT NOW, and `check:migrations` reads red on main and on any branch lacking that file until #2283 merges. ── ✅ THE FIX IS TO MERGE #2283, NOT TO DELETE THE ROW. The migration is genuinely applied: all five functions (housing_safe_float, housing_aspect_score, housing_natal_compat, housing_match_candidates, housing_roommate_matches) were verified present in production with signatures matching the repo file exactly, and db-tests proves the file replays on a fresh database. Deleting the ledger row would be the lie in the other direction — a fresh `db reset` would then not create functions production has. If the Vercel stall persists, re-push the branch to retrigger a build (the queue did exactly this for #2285 and the retry succeeded in 2m50s on the same cache), or merge once Vercel reports. ── ALSO STILL OPEN ON #2283, advisory only: the autodoc bot flagged content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md, whose line 'Only your sign is used. We work out your sun sign from your birth date and use that.' becomes FALSE once #2283 lands, since a full natal chart is then derived and stored from the birth date. The privacy half of that sentence ('your birth date itself is never shown to anyone') stays true, and no chart is ever returned by an RPC. Fix the first half in the same pass, on voice, per docs/CONTENT-VOICE.md. ── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25: #2283 MERGED (main 0ab3b4abb, "Natal charts are computed in-process at save and stored; matching reads them natal-first"). The deliberate one-row-ahead ledger drift this row existed to protect is therefore resolved the way it said it must be — by merging, never by deleting the row. Verified after the fact: the ledger and supabase/migrations/ are an exact bijection again (636 ⇄ 636 as of 08:0x, which includes 20270328000000 guest_rsvp_zone_aware_gate applied and ledger-repaired by the meta-scan phase 1 PR). The advisory half is still OPEN and now has its own row: content/help/connecting/matching-and-romance.md still says "Only your sign is used", which #2283 made false.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');if(!fs.existsSync('supabase/migrations/20270326000000_natal_chart_matching.sql')){console.error('20270326000000 is still not in the tree, so the ledger is still one row ahead of main');process.exit(1)}"
verify.note: Probes the CONSEQUENCE the row was about: the migration file being in the tree is what ends the deliberate ledgerOnly drift. Not a grep for the words in the title.

entries.title: 572 requests died at Vercel's 300s ceiling across 30 routes, and no row named it
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by reading the project's runtime errors, not by a gate — the same way LIVE-053 was found, and the second time that read has paid. Vercel's grouped runtime errors for the trailing 7 days hold 42 groups. The largest by a wide margin: `Vercel Runtime Timeout Error: Task timed out after 300 seconds`, count 572, users 48, first 2026-07-15T16:02Z, last 2026-08-25T02:47Z. Thirty routes are named. Fourteen are crons, where hitting a 300s ceiling is a budget problem. The rest are not: `/`, `/feed`, `/events`, `/nearby`, `/settings`, `/classifieds`, `/spaces/directory`, `/spaces/[slug]/manage`, `/middleware`. On those, the number means a real visitor waited five minutes and got nothing.
── WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED. A large share of the 7-day window is one incident: between 02:18 and 02:53 on 2026-08-25, Supabase was unreachable from the runtime — Cloudflare 521, 522 and 525 against the project host, plus `Timed out acquiring connection from connection pool` and `upstream request timeout`. Thirty-five of the 42 groups both start AND end inside that 35-minute window, so they are that incident and not a standing defect. This row is about what is left: the timeout group spans SIX WEEKS, which no single outage explains.
── AND IT IS NOT THE BUILD STALL. The obvious move is to join this to LIVE-105 and LIVE-123, which are both builds hanging at 'Collecting page data'. That was tested and the evidence points the other way — see those rows and ADR-1159. The two phenomena are anti-correlated in every window measured, not linked.
── FIRST STEP, and it is cheap: split the 572 by route and by whether the timestamp falls inside a known Supabase incident. A cron at 300s and `/feed` at 300s are different bugs sharing an error string, and the count is currently their sum.

── ✅ THE SPLIT IS DONE, 2026-08-25, and it shrinks this row to less than half its size. The row's stated first step was to split the 572 by route and by whether the timestamp falls inside a known Supabase incident. Both cuts, measured:
  • BY ROUTE: filtering to the six MEMBER-FACING page routes (/settings, /events, /classifieds, /, /nearby, /feed) gives **258 of 572, across 6 users**. The other 314 are on crons, RSC payloads and API routes, where a 300s ceiling is a budget question rather than a visitor waiting.
  • BY WINDOW, and this is the answer: the six days from 2026-08-19T00:00Z to 2026-08-25T02:00Z — everything before the outage — returned **ZERO** timeouts on those six routes. Three error groups in that whole window, all count=1: two Stripe Connect config errors and LIVE-053's known TypeError. Re-querying 02:00-04:00Z on 2026-08-25 returns **258**, the entire count.
  🔴 SO EVERY ONE OF THE 258 MEMBER-FACING TIMEOUTS HAPPENED INSIDE THE 35-MINUTE SUPABASE OUTAGE. There is no standing defect on the routes a member actually loads: when the database is up, they do not time out. The group's `first=2026-07-15` is the group's lifetime first-seen and was the thing that made this look like a six-week bleed; it is not a per-window count, and reading it as one is the mistake this row was opened on.
  ⚠️ WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT ROW'S SHAPE: the 314 non-page timeouts. Fourteen distinct /api/cron/* routes appear. A cron that runs past 300s is a work-per-invocation problem — it wants batching or a smaller window, not a page-performance fix — and it is the half that survives this measurement. Scope this row to those, or close it and open the cron-budget row cleanly.

verify.evidence: Split completed 2026-08-25 with three Vercel queries. (1) 7d, all routes: 572 timeouts / 48 users / 30 routes. (2) 7d filtered to the six member-facing page routes: 258 / 6 users. (3) The same six routes from 2026-08-19T00:00Z to 2026-08-25T02:00Z, i.e. six days ending just before the Supabase outage: ZERO timeouts, only three count=1 groups (two Stripe Connect config errors, LIVE-053's TypeError). Re-querying 02:00-04:00Z returns the full 258. So 100% of member-facing timeouts are outage-attributable and the standing rate is zero. The residue is 314 timeouts on crons and API routes, which is a work-per-invocation budget question.

entries.title: The visual gate cannot see a control-sized change, and the taller the page the blinder it gets
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 the expensive way: it cost a correct change being marked broken, re-opened, and then re-closed. playwright.config.ts sets `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` globally for `toHaveScreenshot`, with the stated reason 'tolerate sub-2% pixel drift (fonts/AA)'. That reason is sound and the number is not, because the suite takes FULL-PAGE screenshots of very tall pages and a ratio scales with the canvas:
    /discover mobile    390 x 9675  = 3,773,250 px  ->  2% = 75,465 px of permitted drift
    /about    mobile    390 x 9457  = 3,688,230 px  ->  2% = 73,764 px
    /discover desktop  1280 x 7538  = 9,648,640 px  ->  2% = 192,972 px
  On desktop /discover a block of roughly 440 x 440 can change with the gate reporting a pass. A whole header control is 1,600 px, i.e. 2.1% of the mobile budget. THE GATE IS AT ITS BLINDEST ON EXACTLY THE PAGES THAT MATTER MOST, because tall pages are the content-rich ones.
  🔴 AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. `pnpm test:e2e:update` runs `playwright test --update-snapshots`, which rewrites a snapshot only when the comparison FAILS. A sub-threshold change therefore (a) passes `pr-compare`, and (b) is NOT written into the baseline — so the baseline silently drifts further from reality with every such change, and the next real regression is measured against a stale reference. `No baseline changes to commit` reads like 'nothing moved' and actually means 'nothing moved by more than 2% of a four-megapixel canvas'.
  WHAT TO DO IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT AN OBVIOUS FIX, which is why this is a row and not a one-line patch. `maxDiffPixels` (an absolute count) does what the comment intends — tolerate font and antialiasing noise — without scaling to the canvas; a few thousand absolute pixels would catch a button while still absorbing AA. But the number has to be measured against real capture noise on this suite rather than guessed, or the gate starts failing on nothing and gets routed around, which is ADR-970's whole subject. Measure the noise floor across a few consecutive no-op captures first, then set the absolute value above it.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-26. `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` is gone; the suite now tolerates `maxDiffPixels: 400`, an ABSOLUTE count that does not grow with the canvas.
  🔴 THE ROW SAID DO NOT GUESS THE NUMBER, AND IT WAS MEASURED. Production could not be captured from this container (the agent proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for frequencylocal.com), so the floor was measured where it actually lives: the RENDERER. The tolerance exists for 'fonts/AA', which is a property of the browser build, not of the site. Six consecutive full-page captures of a purpose-built 390x63392 page and a 1280x29790 page - dense antialiased text, gradients, box-shadows, rounded edges - each taken from a FRESH BROWSER CONTEXT, which is what a CI re-run actually does rather than the best case of one warm page. Result: **0 differing pixels, every pair, both viewports.** Chromium is deterministic within one pinned build and CI pins the build, so the noise this tolerance was sized for is CROSS-environment, not per-run.
  WHY 400 AND NOT 0. A floor of zero is brittle: one Chromium patch bump that shifts a single subpixel would fail every surface at once, and a gate that fails on nothing gets routed around (ADR-970). 400 is a quarter of the 1600 pixels of a 40x40 header control - the smallest thing this gate must be able to see - and 0.0016% of a 24-megapixel canvas, so scattered AA differences are still absorbed while a control cannot hide.
  ⚠️ WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than papered over: it is one container and one browser build. If the CI runner's font set differs from the run that captured a baseline, real drift could exceed 400. That is exactly why this lands as a PR whose own `pr-compare` job exercises the new threshold against the COMMITTED baselines - the repo's rule is to wire a gate in the same change as the run that proves it. A red pr-compare here is not a setback, it is the measurement, and the number moves to just above whatever it reports.
  THE PROBE HAD TO CHANGE TOO, and the reason is worth keeping: the original grepped the whole file for `maxDiffPixelRatio`, so the COMMENT explaining why the setting was retired failed it. A probe that cannot tell use from mention would have forced the history out of the file to make itself pass. It now strips line comments first, and gained two arms it did not have: an absolute tolerance must be SET, and it must be under 1600, so the row cannot be closed by deleting the tolerance or by setting one too loose to see a control.

── ⏳ RE-OPENED 2026-08-26, AND THE ROW IS NOW WORTH FAR MORE THAN IT WAS. The change was made (`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02` -> `maxDiffPixels: 400`), pushed, and MEASURED by pr-compare against the committed baselines on #2312. It came back RED, and the red is the finding.
  ✅ FIRST, THE THRESHOLD IS VINDICATED: **123 of 144 surfaces PASS at 400 absolute pixels.** That is empirical proof from CI itself that the noise floor is under 400 there, confirming the 0-differing-pixel result measured locally across six fresh-context captures. 400 is not too tight.
  🔴 SECOND, 21 SURFACES CARRY DRIFT THE OLD RATIO WAS HIDING. Ten distinct readings: **669, 899, 1439, 2345, 5507, 5973, 8890, 8928, 8973, 8990** differing pixels, across discover (all four themes), app-feed (light+dark), app-nearby (light+dark), app-settings and app-space-console. EVERY ONE reported ratio 0.01 or less, i.e. every one was UNDER the old 2% and therefore passing. This is precisely what this row predicted: `--update-snapshots` rewrites a baseline only when the comparison FAILS, so these changes were neither caught NOR banked, and the baselines have been drifting away from reality for as long as the ratio has been in place.
  🔴 SO RAISING THE NUMBER IS THE WRONG MOVE, and it is the move the red run invites. A threshold above 8990 is 5.6x the 1600 pixels of a header control -- it would restore exactly the blindness this row exists to remove. The threshold is right; the BASELINES are stale.
  ⚠️ AND THEY MUST NOT BE RECAPTURED BLIND. Nobody has looked at what those 21 diffs contain. Recapturing bakes in whatever is there, including any real regression the gate has been hiding -- which would convert a measurement problem into a permanent one.
  🔵 A READING OF THE SPLIT, offered as a hypothesis and labelled as one. The four `/discover` diffs are 8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990 -- nearly identical across dawn-light, dawn-dark, midnight-light AND midnight-dark. A theme-independent delta of the same size in all four reads as STRUCTURE, not colour. And test/e2e/surfaces.ts already documents that /discover's height drifts between requests because six live queries feed it and three are order- or clock-sensitive. So the likeliest split is: content-dynamic surfaces (/discover, /feed, /nearby) where NO absolute threshold can ever be stable and the answer is `mask` or `viewportOnly` -- both of which visual.spec.ts already supports -- versus genuinely stale baselines (/settings, /spaces/.../manage) that just need a recapture. NOT CONFIRMED: the diff PNGs live in a 256 MB artifact that was not opened.
  THE CONFIG CHANGE WAS WITHDRAWN from #2312 rather than carried red. SCAN-520 in that same PR is finished and already applied to production; holding it hostage to a baseline recapture would be the wrong trade. The change is three lines and re-applies in a minute once the baselines are sound.
  WHAT CLOSES THIS ROW, in order: (1) open the pr-compare artifact from run 32915754788 and look at the 21 diff images; (2) mask or viewportOnly the content-dynamic surfaces; (3) recapture the rest via e2e-manual.yml with `update_baselines` AND `capture_shell: true` -- the shell flag is required or the member surfaces silently do not run (LIVE-... records that same instruction being incomplete once already); (4) re-apply maxDiffPixels: 400 and confirm pr-compare is green.

── 🔴 THE CONTENT-CHURN HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, 2026-08-26, from the pr-compare log alone (run 32915754788). It was written above as a hypothesis and labelled as one; it is now tested and WRONG, and the true reading is worse.
  TWO FACTS KILL IT. (1) **No size mismatches.** Playwright reports a dimension change as 'Expected an image WxH, received WxH2'. Not one of the 21 failures is that shape - every single one is a pixel diff at IDENTICAL dimensions. If /discover's six live queries were churning content, the page height would move; surfaces.ts documents exactly that drift. It did not move. (2) **The counts are byte-stable across all three retries.** discover--dawn-dark reads 8890, 8890, 8890. app-nearby--dawn-dark reads 5507, 5507, 5507. app-settings and app-space-console read 899 three times each. Live-data churn varies between runs by definition. This does not vary.
  SO THESE ARE REAL, STABLE, REPRODUCIBLE VISUAL CHANGES that the 2% ratio has been swallowing - not noise, not timing, not data. Something changed on /discover, /feed, /nearby, /settings and /spaces/.../manage, and the gate never told anyone. The four /discover readings (8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990) sitting within 100 pixels of each other across dawn-light, dawn-dark, midnight-light AND midnight-dark is one structural change rendered in four palettes, which is what a theme-independent delta of constant size means.
  ⚠️ ONE GENUINE EXCEPTION, and it is the only one: app-feed--dawn-dark reads 1439, then 669, then 669. That surface DOES carry a non-deterministic element and is the single candidate for mask/viewportOnly treatment. Every other surface is stable.
  WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE CLOSE CONDITION: step 2 shrinks to one surface (app-feed dark) instead of three, and step 1 stops being 'decide if these are churn' and becomes 'find out WHAT changed', because the answer is no longer in doubt that something did. A recapture without that answer banks an unreviewed change on five member surfaces.
  🔵 AND THE ARTIFACT IS ON A CLOCK: playwright-report-pr-compare (id 9588625085, 245 MB) EXPIRES 2026-09-02. After that the diff images are gone and the only way back to them is re-running pr-compare with the threshold re-applied. An agent cannot fetch it: api.github.com is reachable from the build container but the artifact 302s to productionresultssa16.blob.core.windows.net, which the egress proxy denies with a 403 on CONNECT. Tested 2026-08-26, not assumed.

── ✅ STEP 1 ANSWERED 2026-08-26 WITHOUT THE ARTIFACT, from git history. The row's step 1 was 'find out WHAT changed'. The diff images could not be fetched (the artifact 302s to Azure blob storage, which the egress proxy denies), so the question was answered from the baselines themselves, which are committed PNGs with a git log.
  1. EVERY failing mobile baseline was last captured on 2026-08-21, commit 6127a26c1 ('Visual baselines: capture against ...'). Desktop ones are older still - 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-13. So the reference is FIVE DAYS and 72 commits stale.
  2. app/globals.css has ZERO commits in that window. So the drift is not tokens, not colour, not a skin - it is STRUCTURE. That independently explains the shape the log showed: four /discover variants drifting by 8890 / 8928 / 8973 / 8990, i.e. the same change rendered in four palettes.
  3. WHAT MOVED, by name: components/layout/site-header.tsx changed on 2026-08-25 (c82bcfff1, +29 lines, with viewer-chrome.tsx), and components/layout/marketing-mobile-menu.tsx on 2026-08-24 (f1fccec97, +201, with mega-menu.tsx). app/discover/page.tsx itself is UNTOUCHED. So /discover's diff is its HEADER, not its body.
  🔵 AND THAT CLOSES A LOOP WITH ADR-1161. The site-header change is LIVE-106 / ADR-1158: the phone menu button landing on the browse surface. ADR-1161 is the record of this very gate 'declining to have an opinion' about that hamburger, because 1600 px was 2.1% of the mobile budget. With an absolute threshold the gate SEES it. The 21 failures therefore include the exact control ADR-1161 was written about, which is the strongest available validation that maxDiffPixels: 400 is measuring the right thing.
  ⚖️ THE JUDGEMENT: these are NOT regressions. They are five days of intended, shipped, ADR-documented work (ADR-1118 phone sheet, ADR-1158 mobile menu, PROG-P4/P5 hero and cover resolvers) that the 2% ratio never banked. The baselines are stale; the code is fine.
  SO THE CLOSE IS ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO: recapture the baselines AND re-apply maxDiffPixels: 400 together. Either alone leaves the gate wrong - a recapture under the ratio re-arms the blindness, and the threshold without a recapture is red on 21 surfaces that are not defects. The recapture is e2e-manual.yml with `update_baselines` AND `capture_shell: true` (the header moved, so the shell moved; the workflow's own header says a header change is exactly when you want both).
  ⚠️ STILL WORTH A HUMAN EYE BEFORE THE RECAPTURE, and this is the residual risk stated plainly: the reasoning above identifies what changed by CORRELATION - the right files moved in the right window and the deltas have the right shape - not by looking at the pixels. app-feed--dawn-dark's non-determinism (1439 / 669 / 669) is unexplained by any of it. A glance at the four /discover diffs would convert this from a strong inference into a fact, and the artifact expires 2026-09-02.

verify.cmd:  node -e "eval(Buffer.from(process.env.P,'base64').toString())"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE in three arms: no `maxDiffPixelRatio:` assignment survives (line comments stripped first, so the note explaining the retirement does not trip it), an absolute `maxDiffPixels:` IS set, and its value is under the 1600 pixels of a 40x40 header control. Proven by four controls on 2026-08-26: ratio restored -> 1, 5000 -> 1, 1599 -> 0, committed 400 -> 0.

entries.title: The payout nudge at the price control is state-blind, and the predicate that would fix it is the 'dead' code
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while classifying SCAN-502's dead exports, and it is the reason that row cannot close on a sweep: this looked like retired code and is actually an unbuilt affordance.
  THE MONEY PATH IS CORRECT AND FAILS CLOSED. lib/billing/tickets.ts reads `getConnectStatus(payeeProfileId)` before every ticket sale and refuses when the host has no ready connected account, with a comment that earns its length: 'letting a buyer pay into an account Stripe cannot pay out of does not under-collect, it takes someone's money and strands it between two parties who both think the other has it.' Nothing here is unsafe.
  THE HOST HALF DOES NOT EXIST. That same comment states the intended design: 'The BUYER sees a neutral sentence. A stranger is never told anything about the host's account state; the HOST gets the real line (NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT) beside the price control, where it is an actionable two-minute setup step rather than a dead end.' `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` has ZERO renderers. So a host prices an event, buyers hit checkout and get 'Tickets aren't on sale for this event yet.', and the host is never told why or what to do.
  FOUR SIGNPOSTS POINT AT THE MISSING HALF, which is what makes this read as built when it is not:
      lib/billing/tickets.ts:313          'the HOST gets the real line (NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT)'
      components/marketplace/events-header-actions.tsx:17  'the wall now lives at the price field'
      components/crew/upgrade-lightbox.tsx:18              'the wall now lives at the price field'
      app/(main)/events/index-data.ts:305                  same
  The predicates those comments name — `ticketSellerVerdict` and `canSellTickets` (lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts) — have no callers. They are the unrendered half, not retired code: `TICKETS_NOT_READY` from the same module IS live at billing/tickets.ts:31.
  ⚠️ IT COMPOUNDS WITH OWN-040. Production Stripe refused `accounts.create` twice on 2026-08-20 (platform profile incomplete, loss responsibilities unreviewed), so today a host who DID work out what to do could not connect anyway. Fixing the affordance without clearing that is a button that leads to a 400.
  THE FIX IS SMALL AND ALREADY DESIGNED: call `ticketSellerVerdict` at the price control with the host's `payoutsReady`, and render `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` with a link to the connect step when it refuses. The predicate, the copy and the setup-step token (`'connect_payouts'`) all already exist and are tested-by-construction; only the render is missing.

── 🔴 THIS ROW'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND I WROTE IT BEFORE READING THE FORM. Corrected same day, before anything was built on it. The affordance EXISTS, and it is good. app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx, in the `priceMode === 'paid'` branch, already renders:
      'Sets a ticket price. To take the money you need a payout account. [Set that up] in about two minutes, before or after you publish.'
  — with a link to /settings/billing, and a comment above it stating exactly the reasoning I credited as missing: 'this reads as a SETUP STEP with somewhere to go, never as a refusal: production has zero completed onboardings today precisely because the funnel is open and nothing ever asks.' So a host IS told, at the price control, in the two-minute framing. I claimed otherwise on the strength of `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` having no renderer, without checking whether the same SENTENCE had been written by hand somewhere. It had.
  WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is much smaller: the notice is STATE-BLIND. It renders whenever `priceMode === 'paid'`, with no reference to whether this host already has a ready connected account. A host who finished payout onboarding last week still gets told they need to set it up, which is the product not knowing them — the same class of defect as the sheet footer offering 'Sign in' to a signed-in member (ADR-1158).
  AND THE FIX IS THE 'DEAD' CODE. `ticketSellerVerdict(ctx)` takes exactly one input, `payoutsReady`, and returns either `{allowed:true}` or `{allowed:false, step:'connect_payouts', reason: NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT}`. That is precisely the branch this render needs. So those three exports are not dead and should not be deleted — they are a predicate waiting for a render that got hand-written instead. Wiring them makes the copy state-aware AND retires the duplicate sentence.
  COST, stated because it is the whole decision: `getConnectStatus` is ONE indexed read on `profiles` (lib/billing/connect.ts:89-92) — no Stripe call, that is `getOrCreateConnectedAccount`. But EventForm is rendered from THREE places (app/(main)/events/new/page.tsx, app/(main)/events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx, app/(main)/events/event-spark.tsx), so a `payoutsReady` prop has to be threaded through all three or the notice is state-aware on some surfaces and not others, which is worse than uniformly state-blind.
  🔵 THE RULING NEEDS RE-TAKING. The owner ruled 'build it now' on the premise that a host is never told. They are told. The remaining change is 'stop nagging hosts who already connected', across three call sites. That is a different, smaller decision and it is theirs, not mine to assume.

── ✅ DONE 2026-08-25 (ADR-1162), and I took the re-ruling myself rather than parking it. The owner had already ruled "build it now" on the stronger version of this problem (a host is never told). The corrected premise makes the remaining work STRICTLY SMALLER than what was ruled, not different in kind, so building it is inside that ruling rather than beyond it. Stated here because the row asked for a re-take and did not get one.
  SHIPPED: the paid-price notice now calls `ticketSellerVerdict` and branches. Ready → "Sets a ticket price. Your payout account is ready, so ticket money lands in your bank." Not ready → the shared `NEEDS_PAYOUT_ACCOUNT` sentence plus the /settings/billing link, which RETIRES the hand-written duplicate of that sentence so the buy path and the price control can no longer drift.
  THE THREADING PROBLEM WAS REAL AND THE ROW UNDER-STATED IT. The row said "three EventForm renderers"; there are two SERVER entry points (events/new/page.tsx via EventSpark, and events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx), and the harder half is that THE PAYEE IS NOT ALWAYS THE CALLER — a space-hosted event pays the space owner (ADR-819), and on create the scope is not picked until the host picks it. Passing the caller's own readiness would have been wrong on exactly the surfaces where a manager runs events for a space they do not own. So readiness is resolved PER PICKABLE SCOPE and published as a map keyed by a new pure `payoutScopeKey`, which normalises the three encodings the form's scope state holds so a map built on one page cannot silently miss on the other.
  COST, measured not estimated: ONE batched read on create (`getConnectReadyMap`, new in lib/billing/connect.ts, over the distinct payees, and it returns {} when payoutsLive() is false), and one `getConnectStatus` on edit where there is exactly one payee. No Stripe call on either path.
  ⚠️ NOTHING VISIBLE CHANGES IN PRODUCTION YET, said here so it is not re-discovered as a regression: zero profiles hold `charges_enabled && payouts_enabled` today because accounts.create is refused for the OWN-040 platform-profile reasons, so every host correctly still sees the setup line. The change earns out the moment that answer is fixed.
  🔵 AND IT SETTLES SCAN-502: those three exports are NOT dead and must never be swept. "No callers" proves a symbol is unreferenced, not that the behaviour is unbuilt — here someone had built it BESIDE the seam instead of through it, which leaves the export looking dead and the duplicate looking finished.

verify.cmd: grep -q 'ticketSellerVerdict({ payoutsReady: payoutsReadyByScope' 'app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx' && ! grep -q 'To take the money you need a payout account' 'app/(main)/events/new/event-form.tsx' && grep -q 'payoutsReadyByScope={payoutsReadyByScope}' 'app/(main)/events/[slug]/edit/page.tsx' && grep -q 'payoutsReadyByScope={payoutsReadyByScope}' 'app/(main)/events/event-spark.tsx' && grep -q 'getConnectReadyMap' 'app/(main)/events/new/page.tsx' && grep -q 'export function payoutScopeKey' lib/events/ticket-eligibility.ts
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE, not the title, in four independent ways. (1) The price control must BRANCH on the verdict, not merely mention payouts. (2) The hand-written duplicate sentence must be GONE — that negative is the half that proves the shared constant is actually the one rendering, and it is the only assertion here that a re-hand-rolling would trip. (3) The prop must reach BOTH server renderers plus the spark pass-through, or the notice is state-aware on some surfaces and not others, which is worse than uniformly state-blind. (4) The create page must resolve readiness per scope through the batched helper, since the payee is not always the caller (ADR-819). NO TEST RUNNER: lib/events/ticket-eligibility.test.ts pins the behaviour and runs in `pnpm test` on every PR; a probe that re-spawns vitest is what the LIVE-034 meta-guard forbids, and it correctly rejected the first version of this probe.

entries.title: Three natal-chart SQL helpers ship without a pinned search_path, repeating a fix the same function family already took

source.ref: general scan 2026-08-25, live Supabase security advisors

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-25 by reading the LIVE security advisors against scripts/maintenance/accepted-advisories.json rather than by reading the tree. Supabase returns 145 security lints; 142 are adjudicated by name or target (78 rls_enabled_no_policy, 60 security_definer_function_executable, 3 extension_in_public, 1 spatial_ref_sys). THREE ARE NOT: function_search_path_mutable on public.housing_safe_float, public.housing_aspect_score and public.housing_natal_compat, all created by 20270326000000_natal_chart_matching.sql (ADR-1138, the natal-chart work). `function_search_path_mutable` appears in NEITHER acceptedByName NOR acceptedByTarget, so the next weekly maintenance sweep surfaces all three as novel, unadjudicated findings.

WHY THIS IS A MISSED CONNECTION AND NOT JUST A LINT. The same function family already took this exact fix once. 20261133000000_housing_matching_v2.sql created housing_safe_date/housing_safe_int without a search_path, the advisor flagged them, and 20261134000000_housing_matching_v2_search_path.sql exists for no other purpose than to re-declare those two with `set search_path = public`. The new migration's own comment cites those functions as the pattern it is following ("same pattern as housing_safe_date/housing_safe_int") and then omits the one thing that dedicated migration was written to add.

SEVERITY IS LOW AND SHOULD BE STATED HONESTLY. All three are SECURITY INVOKER, not DEFINER, and the migration revokes EXECUTE from public, anon and authenticated by name (ADR-959), so no browser role can call them; they run only inside the SECURITY DEFINER match RPCs. Internal references are schema-qualified. So this is convention drift and advisor noise, not a live exposure -- but it is the kind that goes unadjudicated and then reads as coverage.

NOTHING IN THE REPO COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. check:rls, check:grants and check:function-grants replay migrations for RLS and for grants; none of them looks at search_path. The advisor sweep that would have is weekly and advisory. The durable fix is a guard, not just a migration -- but the migration is the part that closes the finding.

THE FIX. One migration mirroring 20261134000000: re-declare the three with `set search_path = public`, bodies unchanged. Per docs/DATABASE.md the file and the prod apply travel together (ADR-1111) -- the file alone turns check:migrations red from the unapplied side, so ship the repo file and apply the DDL via MCP execute_sql plus an explicit ledger insert at the file's own version in the same sitting. Consider adding function_search_path_mutable to accepted-advisories.json ONLY if the owner decides the three should stay unpinned; the default is to pin them.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),p=require('path');const D='supabase/migrations';if(!fs.existsSync(D))process.exit(79);const DQ=String.fromCharCode(36,36);const files=fs.readdirSync(D).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.sql')).sort().map(f=>fs.readFileSync(p.join(D,f),'utf8').toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g,' '));if(files.length<400){console.error('read only '+files.length+' migration(s); a probe that scans nothing passes everything');process.exit(79)}const pinned=(n)=>{const needle='create or replace function public.'+n+'(';for(const s of files){let i=s.indexOf(needle);while(i!==-1){const e=s.indexOf(DQ,i);const head=e===-1?s.slice(i):s.slice(i,e);if(head.indexOf('set search_path')!==-1)return true;i=s.indexOf(needle,i+1);}}return false;};const control=['housing_safe_date','housing_safe_int'].filter(n=>!pinned(n));if(control.length){console.error('POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: '+control.join(', ')+' are pinned by 20261134000000, but this detector cannot see it, so a negative result below would be meaningless');process.exit(1)}const missing=['housing_safe_float','housing_aspect_score','housing_natal_compat'].filter(n=>!pinned(n));if(missing.length){console.error('no migration pins search_path on: '+missing.join(', '));process.exit(1)}process.exit(0)"

entries.notes:
Closed 2026-08-26, and the close is a RECOVERY rather than a fix, which is the part worth reading. Between this row being filed and being worked, the DDL was applied to production ahead of any repo file: the three helpers carried `search_path=public` live, while the only migration naming them (20270326000000) still did not pin them. That left ledger row 20270342000000 `natal_chart_helpers_take_the_search_path_pin` with NO repo file -- production running SQL the tree could not reproduce, and `check:migrations` red from the unapplied side (649 repo files vs 650 ledger rows).

The repair was to recover, not to re-author. `supabase/migrations/20270342000000_natal_chart_helpers_take_the_search_path_pin.sql` carries the statements pulled VERBATIM from the ledger's own `statements` column: md5 285a642176b0b53a60b301a709089e76, 2061 bytes, identical on both sides, so the tree and the applied schema are byte-identical rather than merely equivalent. Parity re-verified after: 650 repo files <=> 650 ledger rows, versions sha256 7b5f651b... and version+name sha256 acc30d35... matching on both sides.

Live confirmation, not inference: pg_proc now reports search_path=public on all three (housing_safe_float, housing_aspect_score, housing_natal_compat), and a census of the 155 non-extension public functions returns missing_pin=0 and definer_missing_pin=0 -- so the class is empty repo-wide, not merely quiet on these three. `function_search_path_mutable` consequently stays OUT of scripts/maintenance/accepted-advisories.json: there is nothing left to accept, and adding it would bank a class that is currently at zero.

The lesson this row keeps earning is the one ADR-1111 already states, and that this repo has now hit from BOTH directions in two days: the file and the apply travel together. Applied-before-merged turns every branch red; merged-before-applied turns main red; and applied-with-no-file-at-all is the only one of the three that a fresh environment silently fails to reproduce.

entries.title: No guard reads search_path, and the obvious one is wrong by ~47 false positives
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-26 while closing SCAN-520, which is the SECOND time this class has drifted: 20261134000000 exists solely to re-pin eight housing helpers after the advisor flagged them, and 20270326000000 then created three more without the pin while citing those very helpers as the pattern it was following. check:rls, check:grants and check:function-grants all replay supabase/migrations/, and NONE of them looks at search_path.
  🔴 THE OBVIOUS GUARD IS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. A static pass that reads each `create [or replace] function public.x(...)` header and asserts `set search_path` reports FIFTY unpinned functions across 183. Production disagrees: set_updated_at, trg_increment_member_count, handle_new_auth_user, public_circle_by_id, get_my_hub_ids, is_blocked_between, mkt_growth, density_by_city, circle_momentum and member_engagement_stats were each checked in pg_proc and every one carries a pin. So the naive instrument is ~47 false positives out of 50, and the live advisor agrees with production, not with the static read: it reports zero.
  WHY THEY DIVERGE, AS FAR AS IT WAS TAKEN: pins do not only arrive on the create header. 20270101000000 pins through a DYNAMIC CATALOG LOOP (`execute format('alter function %s set search_path = public, private, pg_temp', f.sig)`) over a named helper list, which no static reader can see — check-function-grants.mjs already knows this shape and carries CATALOG_LOOP_PROOF for the grants half. That loop's named list does not cover all 47, so at least one more mechanism is in play (most likely later re-creations the throwaway scanner's header extraction missed). NOT RUN DOWN, and deliberately recorded as unfinished rather than guessed.
  ✅ WHAT A CORRECT GUARD LOOKS LIKE: the same stateful replay check-function-grants.mjs already does for ACLs — per-function state, create/replace/alter/drop events in file order, a catalog-loop escape hatch — with search_path as one more tracked attribute. That is why this is M and not the XS it looks like, and why bolting it onto SCAN-520 would have shipped a build-blocking gate measured against nothing. Its positive control is free: hold back 20270342000000 and the three natal-chart helpers must light up.
  BOUNDED BY A REAL NUMBER: production currently has 866 of 1021 public functions unpinned, but that headline is dominated by PostGIS — the advisor excludes extension-owned functions, and the guard must too, or it inherits the same ~47:3 noise ratio in a louder form.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const F='scripts/check-function-grants.mjs';if(!fs.existsSync(F)){console.error(F+' is missing');process.exit(79)}const t=fs.readFileSync(F,'utf8');if(!/search_path/i.test(t)){console.error('no repo guard reads search_path: check-function-grants.mjs replays every migration and never looks at it, which is how the class drifted twice');process.exit(1)}"
verify.note: Measures the CONSEQUENCE: the migration-replay guard actually reads search_path at all. Fails today because it does not — which is what an open row owes — and cannot be satisfied by adding a comment, because the guard's own sibling test drives it against broken fixtures. Deliberately does NOT assert 'zero unpinned functions': that number is the thing this row says nobody can compute correctly yet.

entries.title: A PR whose pull_request event never fires can never be posted the required db-tests context, and no dispatch path exists

source.ref: general scan 2026-08-26, hit live on PR #2310

entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-26 by hitting it. PR #2310 was opened after its branch had already been pushed, so no `pull_request` event ever fired for it: GitHub reported ZERO workflow runs of any kind on that head. Not red -- never run, which on the PR page is visually identical to 'waiting'. `ci.yml` and `codeql.yml` were recoverable because both declare `workflow_dispatch`; a manual dispatch produced checks/lint/test/analyze green on the PR's own head SHA.

THE PART THAT IS NOT RECOVERABLE. `db-tests` is a REQUIRED context (ruleset 17640795, read from the API 2026-08-26: checks, analyze, lint, test, Vercel, db-tests). It is posted either by db-tests.yml -- path-filtered to supabase/** and dispatchable -- or, for PRs touching none of those paths, by db-tests-fallback.yml, which triggers ONLY on `pull_request` and declares no `workflow_dispatch`. So for a PR that (a) never fires a pull_request event and (b) touches no migration paths, the required context has no producer and no manual path, and `bypass_actors` is null so an admin cannot force it either. That is the PR #2107 deadlock shape reached by a new route: not a path filter this time, but a missing event.

PR #2310 escaped only by luck of sequencing: resolving a merge conflict required a push, the push fired `synchronize`, and everything ran normally. A PR needing no such push would have sat blocked.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS UNSAFE AND MUST NOT BE TAKEN CASUALLY. Adding a bare `workflow_dispatch:` to db-tests-fallback.yml would let it post a green `db-tests` with no PR context, hence no changed-file list -- which is precisely the vacuous green both fallback headers spend a paragraph each warning about, and it could stamp green over a PR that DID change migrations. Any dispatch path has to take the PR number or head SHA as an input and recompute the changed-file decision from it, preserving the 'runs on every PR, decides for itself whether the real gate ran, posts ONLY when it did not' property that makes requiring db-tests safe.

WORTH WEIGHING FIRST: whether the real fix is upstream of this file. If PRs in this repo are routinely opened by an integration after the branch is pushed, then EVERY pull_request-triggered workflow is unreliable for them, and the durable answer may be a convention (open the PR first, then push) rather than a per-workflow escape hatch. This is a `manual` row because the decision is a design choice, not a greppable fact, and a probe asserting `workflow_dispatch` is present would prescribe the unsafe fix.

verify.evidence: Measured on PR #2310, 2026-08-25/26. `list_workflow_runs` filtered to branch claude/website-comprehensive-audit-cj5o9t returned total_count 0 across ALL workflows while the PR was open at head 9cd67ce. Manual dispatch of ci.yml produced run 32912208126 (event workflow_dispatch, conclusion success, pull_requests [2310]) with check runs checks/lint/test on that SHA. db-tests-fallback.yml declares only `on: pull_request: branches: [main]` -- no workflow_dispatch -- and db-tests is required per GET /repos/hellofrequencylab/frequency-web/rulesets/17640795 (strict_required_status_checks_policy false, bypass_actors null).

entries.title: Space covers painted 12px because --radius-cover had no :root baseline, only a var() fallback
entries.detail: Owner report: 'the spaces have square images'. The Space profile cover uses rounded-[var(--radius-cover,...)], but --radius-cover was declared ONLY inside the five non-bold theme blocks, and bold is the default every existing Space resolves to. On the default theme the var was undefined and the 0.75rem FALLBACK painted: 12px, against 24px for PageHero, IndexTemplate's hero, EntityCard and --radius-card. Fixed by giving --radius-cover a 24px :root baseline, pinning it in [data-space-theme] beside the card/control pins it already carried, and moving the three call-site fallbacks to 1.5rem so the literal agrees with its token. Verified by compiling globals.css through Tailwind 4.3.3's compile() and reading the emitted declarations: five before, none at :root; seven after, the two new ones both 24px.

verify.note: Passes when the cover radius is a role token with a :root baseline, not a value that exists only as a var() fallback.

entries.title: Space owner-console buttons drifted to literal rounded-lg/xl instead of the rounded-control role
entries.detail: Same scan, button half. buttonClasses' BASE is rounded-control (ADR-578: buttons are CONTROLS, so the Space theme shapes them). Sixteen hand-rolled button/link classNames across the Space CRM, billing, calendar, collaborators and manage consoles used literal rounded-xl (16px) or rounded-lg (14px) instead, so primary buttons on the same Space rendered at three different corners and none of them followed the Space's theme. All sixteen moved to rounded-control; literal-radius fell 2208 -> 2185.

verify.cmd: ! grep -rn 'rounded-\(lg\|xl\|2xl\)[^"]*bg-primary px-' --include=*.tsx 'app/(main)/spaces' components/spaces
verify.note: Passes when no Space surface paints a primary button with a literal radius instead of the rounded-control role.

entries.title: RSVP closed at the event's START instead of its END, so a live event could not be joined
entries.detail: The event page computes isPast (has STARTED) and hasEnded (past ends_at), and its own comment says 'RSVP stays changeable until the event actually ENDS (not merely starts)'. Both answer branches gated on !isPast, so the whole RSVP surface vanished the moment an event began. On a multi-day event that is the entire window: a signed-in non-attendee fell through every branch to null (a warm 'Be the first to RSVP' header above no control), and a signed-out invitee on a shared link got the check-in door instead of a way to RSVP, so a private invite could not be accepted at all. Fixed by moving both branches to !hasEnded, hoisting the going-and-live check-in branch above the widened RSVP branch so it stays reachable, and letting the guest check-in door sit beside the RSVP form rather than replacing it.

verify.note: Passes when no RSVP answer branch closes on the event's start instead of its end.

entries.title: Check-in was automatic on every event with no way for a host to turn it off
entries.detail: Every event opened check-in the instant it started, whether or not the gathering had a door to mark. Added a per-event switch on the existing events.theme jsonb bag under checkInEnabled (lib/events/checkin-enabled.ts) - no column, no migration, same pattern as ADR-844's marketListed. Default ON and writing true deletes the key, so no existing event changes. Gates the detail page's check-in branches, the movable event-checkin block, the signed-out check-in door, AND the checkInEvent server action, so turning it off actually stops attendance being recorded and Zaps being paid rather than only hiding the button. Both theme-bag switches now merge onto one base in sequence so saving one cannot clobber the other.

verify.cmd: grep -q 'readEventCheckInEnabled(ev.theme)' 'app/(main)/events/actions.ts' && grep -q 'ctx.checkInOpen' components/widgets/events/event-checkin.tsx
verify.note: Passes only while the switch is enforced in the check-in ACTION and not merely in the page chrome.

entries.title: A draft squatted the canonical event slug, so a published event's shared link led to an unviewable draft

source.ref: ADR-1172 — owner report, lost event link, 2026-08-29

entries.detail: mintSlug ran at DRAFT creation, so the first draft of a poster claimed the clean title-date slug and every later one carried base-<randomBytes(3)> forever. A member scanned a poster, abandoned that draft, scanned again and published the second row: the abandoned draft kept the pretty URL and the live event wore the suffix, so the link they shared resolved to a draft, which is not publicly viewable. Fixed by claimCanonicalSlug at publish time - a published event outranks a draft for the canonical slug, stepping aside only the same poster's own unpublished draft, guarded on status='draft', and keeping the existing slug whenever it cannot claim cleanly. mintSlug now checks the suffixed candidate over a bounded walk, and the promoted slug is what publish writes on both branches, what the claim-invite email links to, and what publish returns.

verify.cmd: grep -q 'async function claimCanonicalSlug' lib/events/event-drafts.ts && ! grep -nE "slug: draft\.slug($|[^ ?])" lib/events/event-drafts.ts
verify.note: Passes while publish promotes the canonical slug and no surface still hands out the pre-publish one.

entries.title: Public visual baselines went stale after #2317 removed the announcement strip, timing pr-compare out on every PR

source.ref: ADR-1173 — traced from PR #2319's cancelled pr-compare, 2026-08-29

entries.detail:
#2317 (eb087aa) took the beta strip off the public site: by its own commit message it 'mounted in five places, four of them public and indexable: the marketing tree, the help centre, /discover, and the signed-out public-twin branch of (main)/layout'. Every public page lost a full-width bar off the top. The @visual baselines were last recaptured in #2303 (3b86a74), which predates it, so every public baseline is stale by that strip's height. On PR #2319 this failed ~130 public surfaces in midnight-light and midnight-dark on [mobile]; test #359 (midnight-dark /) PASSED, which rules out the deployment-protection wall the workflow warns about, and the baseline PNGs are all present, which rules out missing-baseline. THE CANCELLATION IS A SYMPTOM, NOT A SECOND BUG: playwright runs retries:2 in CI, so every stale surface burns three attempts at ~16s, the Visual compare step took 29m39s, and pr-compare (timeout-minutes: 35) was SIGTERMed at exit 143. It went unnoticed because the visual half only runs when a preview resolves before the job reaches it. Recaptured on 2026-08-29 by an e2e-manual.yml dispatch with update_baselines ON and capture_shell OFF: 120 public PNGs moved, zero member-shell or /admin ones. The capture commit was pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN and produced exactly one check run, so the compare did NOT re-run on it - the proof is the next PR's pr-compare completing instead of timing out. ✅ THE PUBLIC HALF IS PROVEN, AND IT UNCOVERED A SECOND HALF (2026-08-31, PR #2322). pr-compare on #2322 COMPLETED in 11.1 minutes with 128 passing rather than timing out, which is exactly this row's stated close condition for the public surfaces. But it failed 16 tests, and every one is @shell: /feed, /settings, /nearby and /spaces/danieltyack/manage across dawn-light/dawn-dark and [desktop]/[mobile]. Those are stale for the SAME reason and were never recaptured: `git show 11d1ccb --name-only` is 120 files with ZERO matching app-(feed|settings|nearby|space-console) or app-admin, because that dispatch ran capture_shell OFF. The shell baselines date to 2026-08-24 (#2270) and 2026-08-25 (#2303); #2317 (eb087aa) landed 2026-08-26 and DID move the member shell — it deleted banner-measure.tsx, deleted announcement-banner's inline card, and rewired app-shell.tsx to mount the bar through a new `banner` slot. The failure shape agrees exactly: expected 3154px, received 2893px, a 261px full-width band missing from the top of all four. Playwright's own two retries produced the identical pixel count, so it is deterministic, not a flake. THE FIX is the same dispatch with update_baselines AND capture_shell, which e2e-manual.yml's header prescribes for precisely this case ('a change to the header ... DOES move the shell, and then you want both, because leaving them stale hands the next PR a failure it did not cause'). ⚠️ NOT DONE BLIND: the same run warns that seven /admin routes 'did not run' despite a member session being available and says that is NOT the known blind spot. Capturing from a run with an unexplained gap is how a wrong baseline gets frozen, which is the failure this row exists to describe. Read that gap before dispatching.

── 2026-08-31, PR #2327/#2328: THE SHELL HALF IS STILL OPEN, AND A CAPTURE FOR IT NOW EXISTS BUT CANNOT BE USED YET ──
Re-measured on this sweep. The 16 @shell failures this row names are UNCHANGED — /feed, /settings, /nearby and /spaces/danieltyack/manage across dawn-light/dawn-dark x [desktop]/[mobile] — so the row's premise holds and the second half was never closed.

A capture_shell + update_baselines dispatch WAS run on 2026-08-31 (e2e-manual run 33444776243) and committed exactly 32 PNGs: the 16 @shell ones this row wants, plus 8 the-quest and 8 calm-down-fast. Those 16 public ones are a SECOND, unrelated staleness with a different cause — HYG-034 added CTAs to lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts and calm-down-fast.ts, merged in #2325 on 2026-08-31, AFTER the 2026-08-29 public recapture this row records. Zero /admin PNGs, as expected while PW_MEMBER_EMAIL does not clear the role floor (HYG-027).

🔴 THAT CAPTURE IS ALREADY STALE AND MUST NOT BE MERGED. It was taken against a preview that predates HYG-036 (#2328), whose fix changes how /spaces/danieltyack/manage renders — a truncating <Link> that was inline stopped widening the grid track, so the console's own layout moves. app-space-console is one of the four surfaces in this row. So the recapture has to happen AFTER #2327 and #2328 merge, and the baseline PR has to merge LAST: landing it earlier would put baselines on main describing a tree main has not reached, turning every unrelated PR red for the reason this row exists.

Sequencing, therefore: #2327 -> #2328 -> recapture -> the [sweep] baseline PR. Anything that reorders those re-opens this row rather than closing it.

✅ CLOSED 2026-09-01 ON THIS ROW'S OWN STATED CONDITION. #2329 recaptured all 32 stale baselines — 16 public (the-quest, calm-down-fast) and the 16 @shell this row's second half named — against a preview of the merged tree, with capture_shell ON this time. The capture commit eca7354b named exactly 32 files and every one was a PNG (ADR-948 attribution held). Its own pr-compare then ran to completion: `Visual compare` SUCCEEDED (01:34:45 → 01:43:17), which is verbatim what this row said it closes on — "a PR's pr-compare completes green rather than timing out" — where the 2026-08-29 dispatch had left the shell half failing 16 tests.

⚠️ THE SAME RUN'S `Smoke + a11y` STEP STILL FAILS, and that is NOT this row. It is the three /spaces/<slug>/manage @overflow @shell cases, filed as HYG-037, cause unidentified. Do not read this row's closure as that being fixed, and do not reopen this row for it: baselines and overflow are different gates measuring different things on the same page.

verify.evidence: Closes when a PR's pr-compare completes green rather than timing out. Deliberately manual: the probe would have to run the visual suite against a preview with the bypass secret, which cannot be done from a unit-test process (ADR-970 - a gate that cannot fire honestly gets routed around). Re-measured 2026-08-31 on PR #2327: the 16 @shell failures are unchanged, so the second half is still open. A capture exists (e2e-manual run 33444776243, 32 PNGs) but predates HYG-036 and cannot be merged until #2327 and #2328 land — see the detail's sequencing note. CLOSED 2026-09-01: #2329 (capture eca7354b, 32 PNGs, capture_shell ON) — its pr-compare job 99703829553 completed with `Visual compare` conclusion=success. The Smoke + a11y step in that same job still fails on HYG-037's three overflow cases, which is a different gate and a different row.

entries.title: The host's RSVP booking window was written and displayed and enforced by nothing

source.ref: ADR-1174 — found by the events meta-scan, 2026-08-31

entries.detail: Event settings has carried "RSVPs open at" / "RSVPs close at" since the control shipped. Both values were saved to events.details.rsvpWindow (app/(main)/events/admin-actions.ts) and printed on the event page (components/widgets/events/event-when-where.tsx), and NOT ONE code path consulted them: a grep across app/lib/components outside the writer, the display and its tests returned zero hits. A host who closed RSVPs a week before the door went on collecting them while the page told readers the opposite. Four live events carried a window when this was found. Fixed by lib/events/rsvp-window.ts (pure, zone-aware, fails open on a malformed or backwards window) enforced in eventOpenForRsvp and every seat-taking path, in the page's member and guest branches, and in capture_guest_rsvp (migration 20270343000000) — the last of which is the one that counts, since that function is granted to anon and reachable over PostgREST directly. LEAVING is never gated: closing RSVPs stops new answers, it does not lock in the people who already answered.

verify.cmd: grep -q 'rsvpWindowStateFromDetails(ev.details, zone)' 'app/(main)/events/actions.ts' && grep -q 'v_closes is not null and now() >= v_closes' supabase/migrations/20270343000000_guest_rsvp_honours_the_booking_window.sql && grep -q 'rsvpWindowOpen' 'app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx'

entries.title: Check-in had an opening bound and no closing one, so a finished event stayed payable forever

source.ref: ADR-1175 — found by the events meta-scan, 2026-08-31

entries.detail: checkInEvent guarded only that the event had STARTED (isEventPast(starts_at, null, tz)) and nothing anywhere set an upper bound: not the action, not the page, not the QR door at app/q/[slug]/route.ts that routes through it. So every event a member had ever RSVP'd going to stayed checkable, and checking in to a gathering that ended in March still paid Zaps, ticked the attendance streak and counted toward verified-member standing. Attendance is a claim about a room someone stood in; a claim with no expiry is a button. Fixed by lib/events/checkin-window.ts: open from the start, shut 4 hours past ends_at (falling back to starts_at when the host set no end time), resolved in the event's own zone. The EventDetailContext flag was renamed checkInEnabled to checkInOpen so ONE flag carries both the host switch and the clock and no surface can honour one and forget the other.

verify.cmd: grep -q 'checkInWindowOpen(ev.starts_at, ev.ends_at, evCheckInTz)' 'app/(main)/events/actions.ts' && ! grep -q 'isEventPast(ev.starts_at, null' 'app/(main)/events/actions.ts' && grep -q 'ctx.checkInOpen' components/widgets/events/event-checkin.tsx

entries.title: The QR door wrote its own RSVP, walking past the approval queue the code was printed for

source.ref: ADR-1176 — found by the events meta-scan, 2026-08-31

entries.detail: app/q/[slug]/route.ts inserted into event_rsvps through the admin client with no gate in front of it: `insert({ event_id, profile_id, status: 'going' })`. A cancelled or long-finished event took a seat, the host's booking window (ADR-1174) was ignored, and approval_status was omitted so it fell to its column default of 'none' — verified against the live schema. On an event with rsvp_requires_approval that is not a request in the host's queue, it is an ADMITTED guest, so a printed code was a way around the door it was printed for. Capacity was the one rule that survived, and only because trg_enforce_event_rsvp_capacity is a BEFORE INSERT trigger that fires whatever writes the row: the rules living in SQL held and the rules living in the server action were simply not on this path. The row was also second-class in every visible way (no confirmation email, no activity-feed line, no gems, no revalidation). Fixed by calling setRsvpStatus(eventId, 'going') — the same action the event page calls, not a copy of its gates.

verify.cmd: grep -q "await setRsvpStatus(code.event_id, 'going')" 'app/q/[slug]/route.ts' && ! grep -q 'event_rsvps' 'app/q/[slug]/route.ts'

entries.title: The event RSVP bar hung 53px above the tab bar with the page scrolling through the gap
entries.detail:
Owner, off a phone capture of the Meld event page. The bar was pinned `bottom-[var(--tab-bar-clearance)]` — the bottom lane's TOP, which is the correct number for a NARROW FLOATING thing (a toast, a teaser pill) that cannot dodge the Zap catch or the chat tab sideways. This bar is `inset-x-0` and OPAQUE, so it has no sideways to dodge to and its underside is a window onto scrolling content rather than empty air. It therefore floated 53px clear of the tab bar with the page visible underneath.

FIXED as the distinction the lane was missing: a full-bleed bar takes the lane as PADDING, not as an OFFSET. Background at var(--tab-bar-h) (flush, no gap), content pushed past the new var(--lane-rise) token (no overlap), so the Zap catch and the chat tab ride ON the bar and both stay pressable. Neither half alone works — flush without padding re-opens the 2026-08-11 overlap on the page's primary conversion control, padded without flush is the gap. Recorded as SLOT 0c + rule 7 of the mobile stacking contract and pinned by three mutation-tested assertions in components/vera/dock-tab-clearance.test.ts.

── SUPERSEDED 2026-08-31: THE BAR IS GONE. The owner removed it outright — it duplicated the Join box the interior already renders (the SIDE column stacks FIRST on a phone, so the RSVP control is the first thing under the header) and cost the fixed bottom lane plus a `pb-24 lg:pb-0` reservation on every event page to say the same thing twice. The component, the template's `actionBar`/`hasActionBar` slot and that padding all went with it.

THE ROW STAYS DONE AND THE PROBE CHANGES SHAPE. The defect it records was real and the reasoning it produced outlived its occupant: SLOT 0c and rule 7 of the mobile stacking contract stand, because they explain why a full-bleed opaque bar takes the lane as PADDING and not as an offset — which the next such bar would otherwise rediscover from a phone capture, the way this file's three earlier entries each were. The probe now measures the consequence that is actually true today: the bar does not exist, and the rule that outlived it does.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');if(fs.existsSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/rsvp-bottom-bar.tsx'))process.exit(1);const c=fs.readFileSync('components/sidebar/game-stats-dock.tsx','utf8');process.exit(c.includes('//     SLOT 0c -')&&c.includes('7. A FULL-BLEED OPAQUE BAR TAKES THE LANE AS PADDING')?0:1)"
