verify.note: The bar was removed rather than kept fixed, so the probe asserts BOTH halves of what is true now: the component is gone, and SLOT 0c + rule 7 survive it in the stacking contract. Deleting the rule with its only occupant is what would make this row stale.

entries.title: The event cover cropped 47% off the width of a poster, and its own title with it
entries.detail:
Owner: 'the text and graphics work on web but not on mobile.' The cover band was a fixed-height box with `object-cover`. The Meld poster is 1400x600 (2.33:1); the phone band was 380x306 (1.24:1) at a 412px viewport and this app's 17px root, so `object-cover` scaled by HEIGHT and cropped by WIDTH — 380 of 714 rendered pixels, i.e. 53% shown. The missing half contained both ends of the event's name; the capture reads 'Creating What's N', 'eld @ Roy', 'nity Coworking'.

MEASURED ACROSS ALL 24 DISTINCT PRODUCTION COVERS as the fraction of artwork AREA surviving: mobile median 81% / worst 53% (8 of 24 lose >25%); desktop median 36% / worst 24% (23 of 24 lose >25%). 13 of the 24 are 1:1 and 6 more are portrait, because Luma and Partiful both tell hosts to upload a square cover — so the app renders square-by-convention artwork inside a letterbox band and asks the crop to be kind.

FIXED for phones (components/media/poster-band.tsx): `object-contain` below sm over a blurred, scaled copy of the poster filling the letterbox, in a band one rung shorter (306 -> 221px at the standard tier). No stored dimensions needed, which is the point — sharp is budget-gated here (69/100 og-trace) and a render-time header fetch would add a blocking subrequest on a marquee page. The desktop half is LIVE-131.

⚪ AMENDED 2026-09-04 (LIVE-146). The phone band CROPS again, and this row's fix still holds, because the band it crops in is a different shape: 412x221 full bleed (1.86:1) rather than the 380x306 (1.24:1) box photographed here. `object-cover` scales to cover the shorter axis, so at 1.86:1 it scales by WIDTH for any source narrower than that - 19 of the 24 covers are square or portrait, and they now reach both edges whole and lose height instead, which is the axis the focal picker aims. The 1400x600 flyer above keeps 80% of its width where it kept 53%. 🔴 The probe was rewritten in the same change because it had been matching a COMMENT, not code - see the verify note.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('components/media/poster-band.tsx','utf8');const code=s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'').replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm,'');const p=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx','utf8').replace(/\{\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/\}/g,'');const h=fs.readFileSync('lib/layout/cover-height.ts','utf8');const phone=h.match(/POSTER_HEIGHT_CLASS[\s\S]*?standard: '([^']+)'/)[1].split(' ')[0];const px=phone.startsWith('h-[')?parseFloat(phone.slice(3))*17:parseInt(phone.slice(2),10)/4*17;process.exit(412/px>=1&&/object-contain/.test(code)&&p.includes('<PosterBand')&&!/className=.object-cover./.test(p)?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence a poster's title survives on a phone, not the fit keyword that happened to deliver it. Three things together: the phone band is at least as WIDE as it is tall (412px full bleed against the standard rung parsed out of the ladder itself, at this app's 17px root), so `object-cover` there scales by width and a square or portrait cover keeps every pixel of its width; the band still contains somewhere (the desktop half); and the event page renders PosterBand rather than a hand-rolled cropping box. 🔴 THE OLD PROBE MATCHED A COMMENT. It was `b.includes('object-contain sm:object-cover')` against the UNSTRIPPED file, and that string had not been code since LIVE-131 - it survived only in the header paragraph explaining what was wrong. It would have passed a file whose fit was anything at all.

entries.title: The desktop cover band shows a median 36% of the artwork, and 23 of 24 covers lose more than a quarter
entries.detail:
Found while fixing the phone half (LIVE-130) and DELIBERATELY not taken in the same change. Measured on the 1044x374 desktop band against all 24 distinct production covers: median 36% of the artwork's area survives, worst 24%. That is a worse number than the phone case the owner reported, and the reason it does not read as broken is that desktop crops VERTICALLY — it trims a photo's sky rather than slicing a headline's letters.

THREE THINGS MAKE THIS A SEPARATE CHANGE, not a one-class extension. (1) The report was about phones and desktop was explicitly working for the owner. (2) All 24 covers carry an operator-set focal point aimed at the crop they currently get, so flipping to contain would silently retire 24 deliberate framing decisions. (3) A 1:1 poster contained in a 1044px-wide band is either enormous or heavily letterboxed, so the honest desktop fix is probably a narrower, poster-shaped column (what Luma does) rather than the same band with a different fit — which is a layout change to a marquee page with visual baselines.

The seam is already built: the fix is `sm:object-cover` coming off components/media/poster-band.tsx, plus whatever band geometry that decision lands on.

── FIXED 2026-08-31. PosterBand now contains at EVERY width, with the blurred backdrop everywhere rather than `sm:hidden`, so no cover is cropped on any surface. The band's `sm:` height is untouched, so nothing on the page moves.

TWO OF THE THREE REASONS THIS ROW GAVE FOR WAITING DID NOT SURVIVE RE-READING. 'The report was about phones' is true and irrelevant to whether desktop is broken — it is, and worse: median 36% of the artwork against the phone's 81%. 'Desktop crops VERTICALLY, which trims a photo's sky rather than a headline's letters' is true of a PHOTO, and 19 of the 24 covers are square or portrait posters whose top and bottom carry the date and the venue. The third — 'all 24 carry an operator focal point aimed at the crop they get' — was the one real cost, and it is smaller than it sounds: with `contain` nothing is cropped, so there is no framing decision left to honour. The value is not deleted and the picker still writes it.

WHAT IT COSTS, stated plainly: a landscape PHOTO cover (5 of the 24) now letterboxes instead of filling the band — 560x374 of a 1044px band for a 3:2 photo, inside its own blurred wash. That is the deliberate trade; the majority case is a poster that was losing its text, and a photo shown whole is a weaker look, not a broken one.

No visual baseline covers an event page (checked test/e2e/__screenshots__), so this does not move pr-compare. Pinned by components/media/poster-band.test.tsx, watched go red both ways: sm:object-cover restored, and the backdrop returned to sm:hidden.

🔴 THE PROBE HAD TO CHANGE SHAPE. It was `grep-absent 'sm:object-cover'` over the file — and the file still contains that string, in the header comment that explains what was wrong and why. That is the third probe on this sweep to match a comment instead of code. It is now a cmd probe that strips comments first, the same way components/vera/dock-tab-clearance.test.ts and the poster-band guards already do.

⚪ AMENDED 2026-09-04 (LIVE-146). The desktop half of this row is UNCHANGED and stays contain - the median-36% arithmetic that settled it is untouched, and the 2026-09-04 owner report was explicitly about phones. Two consequences of that report land inside this row's fix, though. (1) The phone half went back to `object-cover`, so the file now reads `object-cover sm:object-contain`; this row's probe checks for the absence of `sm:object-cover`, which is still exactly the right assertion. (2) The blurred backdrop is no longer painted at every width - it is `hidden sm:block`, i.e. present exactly where the band contains and therefore has bars to fill. This row's `!/sm:hidden/` clause still passes, and still means what it meant (the backdrop is not withheld from the containing surface), but read it as 'present wherever there is a letterbox' rather than 'present everywhere'.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('components/media/poster-band.tsx','utf8');const code=s.replace(/\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\//g,'').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'');process.exit(!/sm:object-cover/.test(code)&&/object-contain/.test(code)&&!/sm:hidden/.test(code)?0:1)"
verify.note: Read against the CODE, not the file: the header deliberately quotes `sm:object-cover` to record what was wrong, so a raw grep-absent fails on the comment explaining the fix. Checks all three: the desktop crop class is gone, contain is present, and the backdrop is not withheld from the width that letterboxes. ⚠️ Since LIVE-146 the phone half covers, so `object-contain` here matches `sm:object-contain` - that is the desktop fit this row is about, which is what it was always asserting.

entries.title: The breadcrumb titleizes the URL slug, so a renamed entity is announced under its old name
entries.detail:
Visible in the same phone capture. The page's H1 reads 'Co Creating What's Next'; the breadcrumb directly above it reads 'Meld Community Cowork Launch At Ro...'. Those are the same event: the slug is meld-community-cowork-launch-at-royal-temple-2026-09-02 and it froze at creation, while the title was edited afterwards.

The cause is structural rather than event-specific. <Breadcrumbs /> is rendered by the SHELL (components/layout/app-shell.tsx), derives its trail from usePathname, and titleizes any segment it does not recognise. Its own header says a page with a dynamic leaf 'can render its own <Breadcrumbs trail=.../>' — but the shell renders it, so no page on a slug route actually can. That makes the last crumb wrong-by-construction on every renamed entity across events, circles, channels, people and the commerce surfaces, and it is also the only crumb that is non-interactive and duplicated by the H1 20px below it.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and the choice is a design call: give pages a channel to name their own leaf (the shell already runs comparable contexts in page-admin-context.tsx and viewer-chrome.tsx), or drop the leaf on unknown slugs and let the trail end at the climbable parent. Not taken here because it changes site-wide wayfinding.

── FIXED 2026-08-31, in two halves, because either alone is broken. The shell renders <Breadcrumbs /> ABOVE {children}, so the page is a DESCENDANT of the crumb it would need to fill in: a context cannot reach upward, and a client store would flash the wrong name on first paint because the server pass renders the crumb before the page that would correct it. So the page renders its OWN trail with the real title, and the shell stands down for that route — which is exactly what components/spaces/space-breadcrumbs.tsx has always done, via a hardcoded `/^\/spaces\/[^/]+/` regex living in app-shell.tsx.

That regex is now `ownsBreadcrumb()` in lib/layout/page-chrome.ts — the registry whose stated job is to be the single source of truth for shell chrome, which the shell reads and pages never reach into. DetailTemplate gained a `breadcrumb` prop; the event page passes [Events, event.title]. Scoped precisely: /events/<slug> only, never /events itself (no slug there, so the derived trail is CORRECT and suppressing it would delete a good crumb to fix a different page's bad one), never the /manage /edit /settings sub-routes, never /events/new.

⚠️ Only EVENTS adopt it so far. Circles, channels, people and the commerce surfaces still render the derived trail and are still wrong on a renamed entity — the mechanism is now one registry line plus one prop per page. Pinned by lib/layout/breadcrumb-ownership.test.ts, watched go red three ways: the shell left on its old Spaces-only regex, ownsBreadcrumb widened to swallow the index, and the page building its trail from the slug.

🔴 AND THE PROBE ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG, which is worth recording. Its first version matched /crumb/i and passed on the JSON-LD helper `breadcrumbSchema`; check:backlog caught that. Its SECOND version enumerated the mechanisms I imagined (<Breadcrumbs, PageCrumb, setPageCrumb, crumbLabel) and was described as 'deliberately mechanism-agnostic' — it was not. It failed against the real fix, which uses a `breadcrumb={[...]}` prop. A probe that lists the implementations you can think of is not agnostic; it is a guess with more branches. The version below measures the CONSEQUENCE: the page supplies a real-name trail AND the shell defers for that route.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const p=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx','utf8');const c=fs.readFileSync('lib/layout/page-chrome.ts','utf8');const s=fs.readFileSync('components/layout/app-shell.tsx','utf8');process.exit(p.includes('label: event.title')&&c.includes('export function ownsBreadcrumb')&&s.includes('!ownsBreadcrumb(pathname) && <Breadcrumbs />')?0:1)"
verify.note: Both halves: the page supplies a trail carrying the real title, the registry names the routes that own one, and the shell defers to it. The page alone renders two trails; the shell alone renders none.

entries.title: The public /discover event page renders no cover at all, while the in-app one leads with it
entries.detail:
Found during the display-surface sweep. app/discover/events/[slug]/page.tsx composes EventDetailTemplate but passes no `cover` slot, so the public, crawlable event page opens on a back link and an H1 with no artwork — while app/(main)/events/[slug] leads with a full-width cover band. Same template, same event, two different first impressions, and the public one is the half a first-time visitor and a crawler see.

Mitigating context, which is why this is S and not M: that route's own comment names /events/<slug> as the canonical public URL and it sets a canonical link accordingly, so this is the secondary surface. It is still linked from /discover/events and still indexed.

The fix is now cheap — components/media/poster-band.tsx exists and takes a public URL, and the cover resolution is the same event-media getPublicUrl the in-app page already does.

── FIXED 2026-08-31, AND THE ROW'S OWN STATED FIX WAS WRONG. This said the fix was cheap because 'the cover resolution is the same event-media getPublicUrl the in-app page already does'. It is not: the in-app page uses the ADMIN client, and `public_event_by_slug` — the anon SECURITY DEFINER RPC behind getPublicEventBySlug — returns no cover column at all (verified against pg_proc). Adding one there is a DROP + CREATE on a function granted to `anon`, and it is the same function that before ADR-903 served private events to anonymous callers. That is a security-surface migration, not a cover change.

What made it cheap by another route: app/discover/events/_data.ts ALREADY reads `events` directly with the anon client on this very page, so RLS is the gate. `cover_image_path` + `theme` ride along on a select the page was making anyway, `getPublicUrl` is pure string construction needing no privileges, and a row the read cannot see returns nothing here either — no migration, no widening of the anon surface. The page now renders the same PosterBand as the in-app one, so a poster shows whole on a phone here too.

entries.title: Two of the seven mobile tab-bar labels truncate at every supported width, and three do at 320px
entries.detail:
Visible in the phone capture as 'Communi...' and 'Marketpl...'. The bar carries seven flex-1 slots (Menu, Feed, Community, Zap, Events, The Quest, Marketplace). At a 412px viewport each slot is 58.9px; the label renders at text-3xs = 0.625rem = 10.625px at this app's 17px root, so 'Marketplace' needs roughly 64px and 'Community' roughly 57px. At 320px — the narrowest width the contract commits to — each slot is 45.7px and 'The Quest' truncates too.

WHAT THE EXISTING CONTRACT DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. components/sidebar/game-stats-dock.tsx already calls seven 'a HARD CAP, not a preference' — but it caps on TOUCH TARGET (45.7px at 320px, above the 44px WCAG 2.5.5 floor), and nothing anywhere checks that the LABEL fits the slot it was given. app-shell.tsx adds `truncate` plus a full aria-label, which is a correct mitigation for a screen reader and does nothing for a sighted thumb: the caption is how a member tells Marketplace from The Quest.

Current published guidance is 3-5 primary destinations with short, untruncated labels, and explicitly names 'Notifi.../Transac...' as the failure mode. Cutting to five is an IA decision about which destinations leave the bar (the drawer already carries the long tail), and renaming is governed by docs/NAMING.md — so this is an owner row, not a mechanical one.

verify.evidence: Owner phone capture 2026-08-31 (Android, 412 CSS px): the bar renders 'Menu / Feed / Communi... / Zap / Events / The Quest / Marketpl...'. Arithmetic: 412/7 = 58.9px per slot and 320/7 = 45.7px; label type is --text-3xs 0.625rem = 10.625px at the --density-root 106.25% root (app/globals.css). Seven-slot cap and the 44px floor are stated in components/sidebar/game-stats-dock.tsx.

entries.title: The breathwork funnel's button says "Get a Free Timer" and the flow ends on the community feed
entries.detail:
Reported by a real user via the owner: they tried to download the Breathwork timer and "it took them to something else".

PROVEN, and it is not a redirect bug — it is the destination. app/join/(induction)/feature-funnel.tsx:325 renders a button labelled "Get a Free Timer" whose only handler is setShowFields(true) (it reveals name + email); :355 "Keep my timer" advances a beat; :307 heads the beat "Free breathwork timer". The funnel's terminal destination is lib/funnels/definitions.ts:277 — `destination: { mode: 'direct', url: '/feed?welcome=vera' }`. The signed-in branch's "Start breathing" button (:591) goes to that same feed URL. The actual timer is a different route: app/(main)/on-air/page.tsx, metadata title 'Mindless'.

So on the PERFECT happy path, someone who asks for a free timer is emailed a magic link and lands on the social feed with a Vera lightbox. No timer, no download. There is also no downloadable artifact anywhere in the repo — nothing in public/, and every `download=` hit is a QR/vCard/CSV export — so "download" is the wrong verb regardless of destination.

The repo already knew: ADR for the feature funnel lists as an open follow-up "a deep-link that opens the breath timer directly on landing (today lands at /feed?welcome=vera)". The ADR also records why /feed was chosen (landing in the app reuses the tested rewards path), so the fix is a product call — deep-link to the timer, or stop promising an artifact in the copy — not a mechanical repoint.

── FIXED 2026-08-31. The destination is `/on-air` (the Mindless timer), and the funnel grant now ADOPTS a practice for the finisher — both halves, because app/(main)/on-air/page.tsx renders 'Nothing on your list yet' for a member holding none, so repointing the destination alone would have swapped the wrong landing for an emptier one.

THE PRACTICE WAS RECOVERED, NOT INVENTED. The owner authored a 10-minute 4/4/4/4 box-breath practice through the Vera Spark and reported that it 'saved and disappeared'. It had: the Spark holds DEFERRED CREATION (app/(main)/practices/create-actions.ts header) — a practices row is written only once the author commits a reviewed title — so the wizard's autosave landed in `studio_draft` (scope 'practices-new.new-practice') and no practice ever existed. The draft's own answers were used verbatim to create `box-breath` ('Box Breath', 46cde204-3afd-454f-861a-402d54e46d5d) in the **Daniel Tyack** space at the owner's direction — every other practice in the library sits in the root Frequency space, because createPractice defaults spaceId to the root.

The grant names the practice by SLUG: lib/funnels/definitions.ts is pure data with no database access, so a uuid there would be an unresolvable magic string, and a slug that matches nothing is a silent no-op rather than a failed signup. Pinned by four assertions in lib/funnels/feature-funnel.test.ts, each watched go red (destination back to the feed / grant dropped / slug replaced by a uuid).

⚠️ STILL TRUE and deliberately not changed: the CTA copy still says 'Get a Free Timer' and 'download', and there is no downloadable artifact — the timer is an in-app surface. That is a copy decision, tracked separately.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const d=fs.readFileSync('lib/funnels/definitions.ts','utf8');const a=fs.readFileSync('app/join/(induction)/actions.ts','utf8');process.exit(d.includes(\"url: '/on-air'\")&&d.includes('practiceSlug')&&d.includes(\"practiceSlug: 'box-breath'\")&&a.includes('adoptPractice(profileId, practiceId)')?0:1)"
verify.note: Both halves or neither: the funnel ends on the timer AND grants a practice by slug, and the completion path actually adopts it. Destination alone lands the finisher on an empty timer.

entries.title: Two help articles link the words "open Mindless" to the help page about Mindless, not to Mindless
entries.detail:
PROVEN. content/help/find-your-people/how-to-calm-down-fast.md:55 and content/help/find-your-people/how-to-stop-doomscrolling.md:55 both read `[open Mindless](/help/the-quest/on-air)`. The label is an imperative to launch the tool; the href is a help article. The timer is at /on-air.

It fails silently because both routes resolve — a reader in the middle of a panic-attack article clicks "open Mindless" and gets prose. Note content/help/the-quest/movement.md:13 uses the SAME href correctly, because there the label is a noun reference rather than a command, so this is not a blanket find-and-replace.

Found in the same sweep as LIVE-134, and it is the same defect class: a control that names the timer and does not reach it.

── FIXED 2026-08-31. Both imperative links now point at /on-air. content/help/the-quest/movement.md was deliberately left alone: its label is a NOUN reference to the tool, so the help article is the right target there — the assertion in the fix script checks that it did not move, because a blanket find-and-replace was the obvious wrong fix. /on-air became a PROTECTED_PATH in LIVE-136, so a signed-out reader clicking through now signs in and lands on the timer rather than losing it.

entries.title: /on-air is not a protected path, so signing in to reach the timer drops the timer
entries.detail:
PROVEN. proxy.ts's PROTECTED_PATHS lists 17 prefixes and /on-air is not one of them. The proxy is what builds `/sign-in?next=<destination>` (the ADR-1082 re-measurement confirmed #2132 taught it to), so a route outside that list never gets a next=. /on-air therefore falls through to the page's own guard at app/(main)/on-air/page.tsx:26 — a bare `redirect('/sign-in')` with no next.

Consequence: a signed-out person who taps the PWA shortcut labelled "Mindless — Tune out: time your practice" (public/manifest.json) or a "Time to practice" push (lib/practices/lifecycle.ts:311, lib/vera-dispatch.ts:156,171) signs in and lands on /feed, never reaching the timer they tapped. Same user-visible symptom as LIVE-134 by a second, independent route.

── FIXED 2026-08-31. '/on-air' added to PROTECTED_PATHS in proxy.ts, so the proxy builds `/sign-in?next=/on-air` and the timer survives the sign-in it triggered. Pinned by app/auth/funnel-recovery.test.ts, watched go red with the entry removed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('proxy.ts','utf8');const m=s.match(/PROTECTED_PATHS[^=]*=\\s*\\[([^\\]]*)\\]/);process.exit(m&&m[1].includes('/on-air')?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence: the timer's own path is in the list the proxy uses to build next=, so the deep link survives a sign-in.

entries.title: The two marketing pages that explain the Mindless timer offer no way to open it
entries.detail:
PROVEN. lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts:229-238 ships a MediaText block headed "Mindless" whose body reads "Mindless is the timer you run a Practice on" — with `ctaLabel: ''` and `ctaHref: ''`, so the page that introduces the timer has no door to it. lib/page-editor/templates/calm-down-fast.ts:102-103 is step 3 of a timeline, "Let the timer hold the space… set a couple of minutes and let it count you down", and the BuildTimeline step shape carries no href at all; every CTA on that page points at /discover/practices/pillar/body, /discover, /loneliness or /the-community.

Low severity on its own — nothing is broken, a reader simply cannot act — but it is the third instance of the LIVE-134 pattern, and it is why a visitor told about a breathing timer ends up somewhere else no matter which door they use. ⚠️ Both pages render getPublishedData(SLUG) BEFORE the code template, so a published Puck document can override this copy; the probe reads the code template, which is what ships when no document exists.

── FIXED 2026-08-31. the-quest.ts's `tq-mindless` block gets ctaLabel 'Open Mindless' + ctaHref '/on-air'. calm-down-fast.ts needed a different shape: a BuildTimeline step carries no href, so the timer step now uses the entry-level `links` array the very next entry on that page already uses — a data row, not a new control. ⚠️ Unchanged and still true: both pages render getPublishedData(SLUG) BEFORE the code template, so a published Puck document can still override this copy.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('lib/page-editor/templates/the-quest.ts','utf8');const i=s.indexOf(\"id: 'tq-mindless'\");if(i<0)process.exit(0);const end=s.indexOf('\\n    },', i);const seg=s.slice(i, end<0?s.length:end);process.exit(/ctaHref:\\s*'\\/[^']+'/.test(seg)?0:1)"
verify.note: Scoped to the `tq-mindless` block by its own id, not a character window. 🔴 The first version of this probe read +/-900 chars around the body copy and passed on a NEIGHBOURING block's ctaHref — check:backlog rejected it as a row claiming OPEN whose probe said DONE, which is the second time this gate has caught a probe of mine measuring the wrong thing.

entries.title: A beta signup started in Instagram's in-app browser landed in the generic Circles induction
entries.detail:
Owner capture of the LIVE funnel showed the giveaway: the page is served inside INSTAGRAM'S IN-APP BROWSER. That webview keeps its own cookie jar, and the emailed magic link opens in Mail/Safari — a different one.

The chain, all proven: email submitted in the Instagram webview sets `fq_post_login` in ITS jar -> the emailed link opens elsewhere with the cookie absent -> app/auth/callback has no cookie and no ?next, so it defaults to /feed -> (main)/layout sees an un-onboarded member and sends them to /onboarding -> /onboarding forwards to /join with no ?seq -> /join resolves the DEFAULT funnel. Someone who asked for a breathwork timer got the generic Vera induction about starting a local Circle. For Instagram traffic this is the normal path, not an edge case, and nothing in the repo detects in-app browsers.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS NOT TAKEN. Putting ?next= on the callback URL is two lines and app/auth/callback/route.ts:22 already reads and validates it — but app/sign-in/actions.ts:12-15 documents a deliberate decision to keep `emailRedirectTo` bare so the provider's redirect-allowlist match is never affected, and on an allowlist miss some Supabase versions silently fall back to the Site URL, which would land people on the homepage and be WORSE than the bug. That config is owner-held and unreadable from the repo.

FIXED with a second carrier instead: the funnel slug is stamped on the AUTH USER at sign-in (Supabase `options.data`), which no change of browser, device or day can lose, and is read back in the callback through the SAME FUNNELS map that wrote it — never interpolated into a path unvalidated. It joins `seatLanding` as a sibling recovery for the identical cookie-less arrival the `destination` comment there already described, and sits behind `hasExplicitNext` so it can never overrule a destination actually asked for. Seat wins over funnel: a claimed seat can be an event happening right now.

⚠️ This lands them back in the BREATHWORK funnel, with its timer and its copy. Where that funnel then finishes is LIVE-134, still open.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('app/sign-in/actions.ts','utf8');const c=fs.readFileSync('app/auth/callback/route.ts','utf8');process.exit(s.includes('data: { funnel_seq: seq }')&&s.includes('hasOwnProperty.call(FUNNELS, v)')&&c.includes('hasOwnProperty.call(FUNNELS, seq)')&&c.includes('seatLanding ?? funnelLanding')?0:1)"
verify.note: All four halves or none: the slug is stamped on the auth user, narrowed through FUNNELS on the way in, re-validated through FUNNELS on the way out, and ordered behind the seat claim. Any one missing and the recovery is either dead or an open redirect.

entries.title: Every event with an UPLOADED cover shared as a plain text card, because the OG route never selected cover_image_path
entries.detail:
Reported from an iMessage thread, 2026-09-01: an event shared to a phone rendered as a plain dark text card. Owner: 'Something is broken on the social share preview. We used to have a well designed version for Events.'

An event's artwork arrives from three places, in two buckets, by two kinds of URL: the host's uploaded cover (events.cover_image_path, PUBLIC event-media, getPublicUrl), the full scanned poster (events.poster_path, PRIVATE, signed), and the scanner's cropped cover (details.media.coverPath, PRIVATE, signed). The precedence across them - uploaded cover -> full flyer -> crop - was hand-rolled at THREE call sites. The event page and the claim card resolved all three. app/(main)/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx selected only the two poster columns and ordered them backwards, so for any event whose host uploaded a cover it resolved null and took its documented no-poster branch. Uploading a cover is the ordinary way an event gets artwork, so the rich poster card was reachable almost only by SCANNED events.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: correct-looking code that renders successfully. Every page rendered, every test passed, every gate stayed green; the only symptom was a plain card in someone else's message thread. lib/og/root-card.test.ts opens with the same lesson for the ROOT card one route over - a stale share card is invisible from inside the app.

FIXED by extracting the precedence to lib/events/hero-url.ts: eventHeroCandidates() is pure and returns the ordered {path,bucket} list (so the page keeps its batch-signed gallery URLs and walks the same order without a second round trip), resolveEventHeroUrl() walks it against injectable storage deps, and an unbuildable URL falls through to the next source rather than erasing the image. All three surfaces resolve through it.

CONFIRMED AGAINST PRODUCTION DATA, and it was not one event. The reported row - 'Co Creating What's Next', the exact title on the screenshot - has cover_image_path SET and both poster_path and details.media.coverPath NULL, so the old card resolved posterSignedUrl(null) and took the text branch. Measured across all 63 published, un-removed events:
  34  uploaded cover AND a scanned poster/crop  -> the card showed the SCAN, not the host's chosen cover, disagreeing with the page hero
  16  uploaded cover only                       -> plain TEXT card despite having artwork (the reported bug)
   1  scanned flyer + crop                      -> the crop, where the page shows the full flyer
   9  scanned, single source                    -> correct before and after
   3  no artwork at all                         -> text card, correctly
So 51 of 63 (81%) shared the wrong image or none. Only 12 were right.

CONFIRMED ON THE RENDERED CARD TOO. This row twice said the pixels could not be checked because every deployment sits behind Vercel deployment protection. True of the *.vercel.app deployment URLs, FALSE of the apex, which serves the same build and is reachable. The card was fetched on the same URL before and after, both freshly rendered (x-vercel-cache: MISS), across this change's production deploy:
  02:55:50Z  old code  image/jpeg   25,737
  03:00:31Z  new code  image/jpeg  146,739   (5.7x)
  03:01:06Z  control   image/jpeg   96,066   a scanned-only event, already showing a photo
The control is what makes it readable rather than suggestive: ~25K is the flat text card and ~96-147K is a photograph, matching the ~151KB-as-JPEG figure this route's own header quotes for the photographic variant. The reported event crossed that boundary at the deploy.

NOT proven this way: that the card is well COMPOSED - scrim, focal crop, lockup. Byte count says a photograph is present, not that it looks right. The bytes could not be recovered intact (the fetch path lossily transcodes them), so no image was ever displayed.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const og=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx','utf8');const h=fs.readFileSync('lib/events/hero-url.ts','utf8');const sel=(og.match(/\\.select\\(\\s*'([^']*)'/)||['',''])[1];const b=h.slice(h.indexOf('export function eventHeroCandidates'));const i=['ev.cover_image_path','ev.poster_path','ev.details?.media?.coverPath'].map(k=>b.indexOf(k));process.exit(sel.includes('cover_image_path')&&og.includes('resolveEventHeroUrl(ev)')&&i[0]>=0&&i[0]<i[1]&&i[1]<i[2]?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence, not the title: the OG route's own .select() string must name cover_image_path (the omitted column IS the bug), the route must resolve through resolveEventHeroUrl, and eventHeroCandidates must still push cover before poster before crop. A CLI rather than a vitest run because LIVE-034 forbids a backlog probe from spawning a test runner. scripts/check-event-hero-parity.test.ts is the enforcing arm - it adds the claim card, the page, and a repo-wide net for a fourth surface, and every arm was watched go red against a real mutation.

source.ref: no cover, while getEventEnrichment already returns one

entries.title: The PUBLIC event share card is still text-only, and the cover it needs is already on the row it reads
entries.detail:
Found while fixing LIVE-138 (the member card, ADR-1179). The /discover/events/<slug> OG card renders the brand text layout for every event. It is the crawlable, SEO half - the card a search engine and a first-time visitor see - and it has no artwork at all.

The ingredient is already there and already privacy-cleared: LIVE-133 taught app/discover/events/_data.ts to return `cover_url` (public event-media getPublicUrl, built on the ANON client so RLS is the gate) plus `cover_focus`, and this route ALREADY awaits getEventEnrichment for its chip. It reads neither. Only tier 1 applies here on purpose: the private poster bucket is not anon-readable, and a scanned flyer can carry the venue address this surface deliberately redacts to city level (ADR-186).

DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN IN THE SAME CHANGE AS LIVE-138, and the reason is build cost, not scope tidiness. This route is PRERENDERED for the same ~200 slugs as the page, and it currently fetches nothing and loads no font - its own header says so ('no remote font fetch so this can never slow or fail a crawl'). Leading with the cover adds, per slug at export time, one remote image fetch (3.5s timeout, 6MB cap) and one photographic 1200x630 rasterisation. LIVE-123 is an OPEN row about builds stalling and OOM-ing in Collecting page data; adding ~200 fetches plus ~200 heavy rasterisations to the export is exactly the kind of change that decides a marginal build, and it must be measured on a real preview build rather than reasoned about (DEPLOY-SAFETY.md).

So: do it behind a real build reading. If the export cost is unacceptable, the alternative is to drop the prerender for this one route and serve the card dynamically with the CDN headers cardResponse already sets.

⚪ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN REASONING, neither of which changes its conclusion.
(1) 'it currently fetches nothing' is FALSE: the route makes two DB reads per slug (getPublicEventBySlug + getEventEnrichment). Its header only claims no remote FONT fetch. The cost argument survives intact - what leading with the cover would add is a remote IMAGE fetch plus a photographic 1200x630 raster per slug at export time - but the premise as written was wrong.
(2) 🔴 WITHDRAWN, AND IT WAS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT DOES DAMAGE. This row used to say "'redacts to city level (ADR-186)' is a MIS-CITATION … the authorities are ADR-825 and SCAN-209". That is FALSE, and ADR-825's own body is the disproof, in one sentence: "The public /discover surface was already city-level only (ADR-186) and the event JSON-LD never carried the venue, so the event page was the single leak surface." ADR-825 CREDITS ADR-186 for the city-level rule by name and scopes ITSELF to the event page. So the three authorities divide cleanly: ADR-186 owns city-level public surfaces and the venue-free JSON-LD; ADR-825 owns hiding the exact address until a viewer registers; SCAN-209 owns the bug that hide_address was render-layer only and leaked through grants, two feeds and the .ics. '(ADR-186)' beside 'redacts to city level' is CORRECT and stays.
⚠️ THE DAMAGE WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Acting on this claim in the same commit that wrote it (#2334) changed lib/events/visible-location.ts from 'JSON-LD is city-level by ADR-186' to 'by ADR-825 + SCAN-209' — replacing a correct pointer with a wrong one in the privacy layer, which is the worst place to send the next reader to the wrong decision. Reverted, with the ADR-825 quote pinned beside it so the same 'correction' cannot be made a third time. And the row's follow-on instruction was worse than the claim: roughly FOURTEEN more ADR-186 citations sit in event-venue code (lib/jsonld.ts x4, lib/jsonld.test.ts, listings-shared/listing-seo.ts, events-map.tsx, events/index-data.ts, the discover routes), and 'its own small cleanup' would have swept every one of them into the same error.
⚪ It was also STALE on its own terms by the time anyone could act on it: it said lib/events/visible-location.ts 'carries the same wrong citation', but #2334 had already changed that line — so the row described a file state that no longer existed, in service of a claim that was never true. See ADR-1189.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('app/discover/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx','utf8');process.exit(s.includes('cover_url')&&s.includes('fetchRemoteImage')?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence: the public OG route reads the enrichment's cover_url and inlines it for Satori. Fails today, which is what an open row should do.

entries.title: The event share card had no visibility gate and published a street 19 hosts had switched off
entries.detail:
Found by an audit sweep hours after ADR-1179 fixed WHICH image that card renders. The image was the smaller problem.

app/(main)/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx read `events` on the SERVICE-ROLE client, so RLS was bypassed and .eq('slug', slug) was the only predicate. It needs no credential (proxy.ts's isPublicEventView lets all of /events/* through except /new and /manage), Next emits its <meta og:image> on every event page including noindexed ones, the URL follows from the slug, and lib/og/deliver.ts caches the render for 24h with a week of stale-while-revalidate - so a leak outlives its fix by a day.

TWO LEAKS, measured against production:
1. hide_address (ADR-825) was never consulted; the card rendered the host's free-text venue line straight onto the image. 19 published PUBLIC events have hide_address = true right now, and every one published the address its host switched off to anyone who pasted the link into a chat.
2. No visibility gate at all: private / circle_only / unlisted / draft / removed events rendered title, date, venue and host name. 4 non-public + 1 removed; for 1 of those the card also signed a PRIVATE-bucket poster and baked the bytes into the publicly cached JPEG.

lib/events/visible-location.ts exists for exactly this and its header names the same street that leaked before - '3598 Royal Rd, Vista, California', the same event, one surface over - under the sentence 'A rule that lives in one consumer is a rule the next consumer does not know about'. SCAN-209 enumerated the .ics, the guest email and the two SQL feeds. The share card was not on the list.

FIXED: gate on visibility='public' AND status='published' AND removed_at is null, else an identity-free neutral card (the pattern the Space card already used); venue line through publicVisibleLocation; gate + rule inputs added to the select, because a rule whose inputs were never fetched reads undefined and silently never redacts. is_cancelled is deliberately NOT in the gate - a cancelled public event is still public and the card's Cancelled chip exists to say so.

NOT CAUSED BY ADR-1179, and worth stating because the shape invites the opposite conclusion: that commit added cover_image_path so more events render a photograph, but the old code already signed the private bucket via posterSignedUrl(coverPath ?? poster_path) and the old text card already rendered the venue line. It changed which image appears, not who may see the card.

STRUCTURAL: opengraph-image.tsx is neither a route handler nor a 'use server' file, so check:authz counts none of the 18 of them (15 opengraph-image.tsx + 3 twitter-image.tsx) - a whole route class outside every authz gate, on the most reliably-fetched anonymous surface there is. Enforcement went where the rule lives: the share card is now the fourth entry in visible-location.test.ts's reader enumeration, asserting redaction AND gate. Only two OG routes use the service-role client; the other (the event claim card) already gated, which is why this stayed a single-route defect.

🔴 THE FIRST VERSION OF THE GATE WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE CARD IT PROTECTS. It read visibility === 'public', copied from generateMetadata - which neutralises `unlisted`. Wrong rule: generateMetadata decides INDEXABILITY (noindexing an unlisted event is right), while this card decides whether the person SENT THE LINK may see it, i.e. READABILITY. 20260612000000_events_visibility_rls.sql says it in words - 'unlisted -> readable by anyone WITH THE LINK' - and page.tsx:587 notFound()s only `private`, with circle_only requiring membership.

Caught by querying production before merge rather than by re-reading the diff: the event this whole thread began with is UNLISTED, so the gate would have replaced its poster card with a blank brand card - undoing ADR-1179 two hours after it shipped, on the one event the owner was watching. The gate is now link-readability: (public OR unlisted) AND published AND not removed. Both directions pinned by mutation - dropping unlisted fails, widening to any visibility fails.

✅ VERIFIED ON THE RENDERED ARTIFACT, by identity rather than by byte count. Fetching the card for two DIFFERENT gated events off the production apex after deploy returns the SAME image:
  flow-frequency-2026-08-02      public + published but REMOVED, private-bucket poster
  breathe-connect-expand-2026-07-23  circle_only, no artwork at all
Different titles, different dates, different hosts, one with a poster and one without - byte-identical output is only possible if NEITHER renders any of its own identity. That is the neutral card, proven on the artifact rather than in the diff, and it is a stronger test than the size comparison it replaced.

The negative half was checked programmatically: none of the distinctive compressed-scan segments from the post-deploy images appear in the pre-deploy bytes, so the image genuinely changed and was not served from cache (both fetches x-vercel-cache: MISS). The public control is unchanged at 96,066 chars before and after, which is what proves the gate did not over-fire. Before the deploy the REMOVED event served 106,733 chars - a photograph, built from the private poster bucket, to an anonymous caller.

⚪ METHOD LIMIT, stated so nobody over-reads this: the two gated cards were compared by inspecting long high-entropy segments of their compressed scan data, not by a byte-for-byte hash - the fetch path returns them lossily transcoded. And the hide_address half is proven at the data and code layer only: a JPEG can be shown to carry a photograph or not, but the address cannot be read off it.

🔴 THE GUARD WAS WEAKER THAN THIS ROW CLAIMED, AND A RE-AUDIT IS WHAT FOUND IT. ADR-1180 says five mutations were watched go red; that was true, and it was not enough. Mutating the FIXED tree on 2026-09-01 showed that TWO of the three leaks this row exists for could be re-introduced with the backlog probe AND lib/events/visible-location.test.ts both GREEN:
  · deleting `&& !ev?.removed_at` from the gate - the removed-event leak, back, silently. The old assertion was toContain('removed_at'), and that string also appears in the .select() and in the Row type, so it passed BY EXISTING. That is the shape-not-truth failure this repo names in four ADRs, occurring inside the guard written to stop a leak.
  · widening the readable set with `|| 'private' || 'circle_only'` - the four-non-public-events leak, back. Nothing pinned the SET; the arms only checked that 'public' and 'unlisted' were mentioned somewhere in the file.
Both arms now extract the two-line gate expression and assert the readable set is EXACTLY {public, unlisted}, with the published and removed_at clauses inside that expression rather than anywhere in the file. Both mutations were watched go red afterwards.

THE LESSON, which is the one this repo keeps relearning from a new angle: a mutation sweep proves only what it mutates. Five green-to-red results read as coverage and were not, because the sweep never tried the two edits closest to the original bug.

⚪ TWO NUMBERS IN THIS ROW WERE WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED ABOVE. 'the 19 of them' was a carried number - 19 is the hide_address event count from two paragraphs up; the metadata image routes are 15 opengraph-image.tsx + 3 twitter-image.tsx = 18. And the share card is the SECOND of four `it` blocks in visible-location.test.ts, not the fourth entry; the code comment's 'FOURTH CONSUMER' is about readers of the rule, which is defensible, but the row's phrasing pointed at a position that does not exist. Neither error touches the structural claim, which holds: check-authz-guards.mjs scans 'use server' files and route.ts|tsx only, so it counts none of them.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx','utf8');const g=s.match(/const linkReadable = ([^\\n]*)\\n\\s*const isPublic = ([^\\n]*)/);if(!g)process.exit(1);const vis=[...g[1].matchAll(/'([a-z_]+)'/g)].map(m=>m[1]).sort().join(',');process.exit(vis==='public,unlisted'&&/=== 'published'/.test(g[2])&&/!ev\\?\\.removed_at/.test(g[2])&&s.includes(\"from '@/lib/events/visible-location'\")&&s.includes('publicVisibleLocation(')&&!/const where = ev\\??\\.location/.test(s)&&/\\.select\\(\\s*\\n?\\s*'[^']*hide_address[^']*'/.test(s)&&/return neutralCard\\(\\)/.test(s)?0:1)"
verify.note:
Measures the GATE EXPRESSION, not the presence of words in the file. It extracts the two-line linkReadable/isPublic gate and asserts: the link-readable set is EXACTLY {public, unlisted}; the published clause and the !ev?.removed_at clause both live in that expression; the venue goes through the SCAN-209 rule and never reads ev.location raw; hide_address is actually selected; and the neutral card is returned.

🔴 THE PREVIOUS PROBE, AND THE VITEST ARM, BOTH MISSED TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN THREE LEAKS. Re-audited 2026-09-01 by mutating the FIXED tree: deleting `&& !ev?.removed_at` passed BOTH arms, because `removed_at` also appears in the .select() string and the Row type, so toContain passed by EXISTING - shape-not-truth verbatim, in the guard written to prevent a leak. Widening the set with `|| 'private' || 'circle_only'` also passed both, because nothing pinned the SET, only that two members were mentioned somewhere. Both mutations now fail both arms.

entries.title: Two surfaces declare `images: undefined`, which OWNS the key and suppresses the share card built for them
entries.detail:
Found in the same audit sweep as LIVE-140; NOT yet verified against the Next internals myself, so confirm the mechanism before acting.

REPORTED MECHANISM: Next applies a file-convention opengraph-image only when that segment's metadata does not OWN the `images` key (resolve-metadata.js checks hasOwnProperty). `images: x ? [...] : undefined` owns it either way, so the branded card is suppressed and, when the ternary falls to undefined, the inherited root card is replaced by nothing.

TWO SITES:
1. app/spotlight/[handle]/page.tsx - sets images from profiles.avatar_url. The segment HAS an opengraph-image.tsx built to stop this exact thing (its header: 'an indexable person page that was sharing only the raw avatar'), and it never ships. A member WITH an avatar shares a 112px square stretched into a summary_large_image slot; a member WITHOUT one shares no og:image and no twitter:image at all. Third miss: the page's real hero is header_image_url, read by neither.
2. app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/podcasts/[showSlug]/page.tsx - coverAssetId is optional at creation, so a Show with no cover art emits no image AND discards the Space card it would have inherited from the parent segment.

The repo already uses the correct form elsewhere - `...(url ? { images: [...] } : {})` in journeys/[slug]/page.tsx and store/[id]/page.tsx - so this is a one-line shape fix per site, not a design question. A guard belongs with it: `images:` may never be assigned a possibly-undefined ternary in a generateMetadata, because the failure is invisible from inside the app.

🔴 THE PROBE THIS ROW SHIPPED WITH WAS BLIND TO HALF THE DEFECT, corrected 2026-09-01. It matched /images:[^,}]*\?[^,}]*:\s*undefined/ over two hand-named files; `[^,}]` excludes `}`, so the OBJECT form at podcasts/[showSlug]/page.tsx:73 - `images: coverUrl ? [{ url: coverUrl }] : undefined`, the openGraph key doing the actual suppression - never matched. Only the array form on :82 was keeping the probe honest, so a half-fix would have closed the row with the primary site untouched. The probe now walks every generateMetadata under app/ and also catches `: null`.

CORRECTION TO THE PATHS NAMED ABOVE: the working spread idiom is at app/(main)/journeys/[slug]/page.tsx:84 and app/(main)/store/[id]/page.tsx:43 (also circles/[slug]/(circle)/page.tsx:95 and practices/[id]/page.tsx:57,63). app/discover/journeys/[slug]/page.tsx has no `images` key at all, so a reader following the earlier phrasing found nothing.

✅ THE NEXT-INTERNALS CAVEAT IS CLOSED. This row said the mechanism was 'NOT yet verified against the Next internals'. It is now: node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/resolve-metadata.js:138,149 - mergeStaticMetadata applies the file-convention image only when source.openGraph/source.twitter does NOT hasOwnProperty('images'). One nuance to keep rather than drop: at :627 postProcessMetadata uses hasOwnProperty('images') && twitter.images, so an explicitly-undefined twitter.images still inherits from openGraph.images - only the twitter-image FILE convention is suppressed there.

✅ FIXED 2026-09-01, and the blast radius was WIDER THAN THIS ROW DESCRIBED. Both sites were verified against the tree before touching them:
  · app/spotlight/[handle]/page.tsx suppressed its OWN opengraph-image.tsx, which sits in the same folder.
  · app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/podcasts/[showSlug]/page.tsx has NO card of its own - it INHERITS app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx AND twitter-image.tsx from an ancestor segment. That is the easier one to miss, because the file convention is not in the route's own directory.

THE IRONY IS WORTH RECORDING: each `: undefined` sits directly above a comment explaining that the block exists to stop shares reading 'Frequency, the Community Collective' with the generic card. The `: undefined` reintroduced exactly that failure, for exactly the rows with no image of their own - a Spotlight without an avatar, a Show without a cover.

FIXED with the spread idiom already in use at journeys/[slug], store/[id], circles/[slug] and practices/[id]: ...(x ? { images: [x] } : {}). All four sites (openGraph + twitter on both routes) moved. scripts/check-metadata-images.test.ts is the enforcing arm - it walks every generateMetadata under app/, carries a positive control that pins BOTH the array and object forms plus `: null`, and floors the corpus so an empty walk cannot pass as compliance. Three mutations watched go red, including the object form the row's original probe was blind to.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');const bad=[];(function walk(d){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d)){if(e==='node_modules'||e.startsWith('.'))continue;const f=path.join(d,e);const st=fs.statSync(f);if(st.isDirectory()){walk(f);continue}if(!(e.endsWith('.tsx')||e.endsWith('.ts')))continue;const s=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8');if(!s.includes('generateMetadata'))continue;const re=/images:\\s*[^\\n]*\\?[^\\n]*:\\s*(undefined|null)/g;while(re.exec(s))bad.push(f)}})('app');process.exit(bad.length?1:0)"
verify.note:
Walks EVERY generateMetadata under app/ and fails while any `images:` ternary falls back to undefined or null - which OWNS the key and suppresses the file-convention card.

🔴 THE PREVIOUS PROBE COULD NOT SEE ONE OF ITS OWN TWO SITES. It read /images:[^,}]*\?[^,}]*:\s*undefined/ against two hand-named files. `[^,}]` excludes `}`, so the OBJECT form - `images: coverUrl ? [{ url: coverUrl }] : undefined` at podcasts/[showSlug]/page.tsx :73, the openGraph key that actually suppresses the card - was invisible. Fixing only the array form on :82 would have flipped the probe to exit 0 with the primary defect intact. It also missed `: null`, missed the hoisted-variable form, and pinned two files by hand when the row's own detail asks for a repo-wide rule. Now it is the repo-wide rule.

entries.title: A live Server->Client serialization error on /events/[slug]: 46 occurrences, 14 users, still firing today
entries.detail:
Surfaced by reading Vercel runtime errors during the audit sweep, not by any repo signal. NO backlog row and no ADR mentions it.

  Error: Only plain objects, and a few built-ins, can be passed to Client Components from Server Components. Classes or null prototypes are not supported.
  route /events/[slug] - count 46, users 14 - first 2026-06-27, last 2026-09-01T02:30:10Z
  digests 4155556756, 1047665748

Still firing on the day it was found, on the most-shared member route in the product, and it has been running for two months. Something the server page passes into a client component is not a plain object - a Date, a class instance, a Map/Set, or a Postgres value that arrives with a prototype. The page is ~2000 lines and hands a lot across the boundary.

NOT DIAGNOSED YET. Next step is to pull the full stack for either digest from Vercel runtime logs, which names the prop, rather than guessing from the file. Two sibling errors found in the same read and worth their own look if they recur: a members' createEvent hitting RLS (42501, events_space_writable_ins, count 2, /(.)events/new) and 'TypeError: u2 is not iterable' on /spaces/[slug]/opengraph-image (count 1).

⚠️ Do NOT infer the cause from the route's recent changes: this error predates every 2026-08/09 change to that page by two months.

verify.evidence: Vercel get_runtime_errors, 7-day window read 2026-09-01: group present, count 46, users 14, last 2026-09-01T02:30:10Z. Closes when a 7-day read returns the group with a zero standing rate after a fix ships.

entries.title: A guide or mentor renaming a Circle silently wiped its cover image, city, neighborhood and resonance flag
entries.detail:
/admin/circles builds its list from four role-scoped queries and casts all four to one hand-written CircleRow. Janitor and host selected image_url, city, neighborhood, resonance_public, featured_at. The GUIDE branch omitted the first four; the MENTOR branch omitted all five. TypeScript could not see it - the repo casts the payload rather than regenerating database.types (ADR-246), so an unselected column is undefined at runtime, the same property that made ADR-1179 invisible one surface over.

IT DESTROYED DATA. circles-client.tsx prefills with `initial?.image_url ?? ''`, handleSubmit fd.sets all four UNCONDITIONALLY, and updateCircle guards with fd.has(...) - always true once the form set them. A guide or mentor who opened a circle, changed only its name and saved wrote image_url: null, city: null, neighborhood: null, resonance_public: false over live values. The action's own comment is the invariant that broke: 'Optional fields are only written when present in the form, so a partial form never clears image/location/resonance it didn't show.' True of the form, false of the query feeding it.

The featured_at miss is quieter and still wrong: for a mentor every `featured_at != null` was false, so a featured circle rendered unstarred and FeatureStar's optimistic seed made every click send act(true) - a mentor could feature a circle and never unfeature one. /admin/events had the identical shape: load-events.ts's directly-hosted branch omitted featured_at while the circle-scoped branch selected it and both merge into one AdminEvent[], so it appeared only for events NOT scoped to the operator's circles, which is what kept it hidden.

FIXED: every branch now selects every column its row type declares. scripts/check-row-type-select-parity.test.ts pins both pairs; three mutations were watched go red, including a re-introduction of the exact original bug.

NOT MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION: whether any circle has ALREADY been flattened this way is not knowable from the tree - a nulled image_url is indistinguishable from one never set. Worth an operator eye on circles whose cover vanished.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const p=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/admin/circles/page.tsx','utf8');const e=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/admin/events/load-events.ts','utf8');const B=String.fromCharCode(96);const RX=new RegExp('\\\\.select\\\\(\\\\s*'+B+'([^'+B+']*)'+B,'g');const sels=[...p.matchAll(RX)].map(m=>m[1]).filter(s=>s.includes('member_cap'));const need=['image_url','city','neighborhood','resonance_public','featured_at'];const ok=sels.length===4&&sels.every(s=>need.every(c=>s.includes(c)));const ev=[...e.matchAll(RX)].map(m=>m[1]).filter(s=>s.includes('is_cancelled'));process.exit(ok&&ev.length===2&&ev.every(s=>s.includes('featured_at'))?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence in both files: all four role-scoped circle selects name every optional column CircleRow declares, and both event selects name featured_at. scripts/check-row-type-select-parity.test.ts is the enforcing arm and derives the column list from the type rather than hardcoding it.

entries.title: Circles may already carry nulls written by the /admin/circles select bug, and nothing has looked
entries.detail:
FILED 2026-09-01. LIVE-143 fixed the cause (ADR-1181: a role-scoped select omitted columns the row type declared, and the edit form wrote the gap back as null). It closed carrying an unfiled action: 'whether any circle has ALREADY been flattened this way is not knowable from the tree - a nulled image_url is indistinguishable from one never set. Worth an operator eye on circles whose cover vanished.'

That is a remediation task for a person, and it was sitting in the tail of a DONE row, which is where work goes to be forgotten. The data-loss window is unbounded backwards: the guide and mentor branches have had the wrong select for as long as they have existed.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: circles whose image_url / city / neighborhood are null AND whose updated_at moved while a guide or mentor held the console. The columns cannot distinguish 'nulled' from 'never set' on their own, so this needs either an operator who remembers the circle, or an audit-trail read if one covers circle updates.

⚪ SCOPE NOTE: this is remediation, not a fix. The bug is closed. Leaving this open is the honest state - nobody has looked yet.

verify.evidence: ADR-1181 and LIVE-143 record the cause and the fix. Closed when someone has actually inspected production circles for flattened covers/locations and recorded what they found, including 'none'.

entries.title: The phone cover band bled off the left edge and stopped 34px short on the right, because two width classes fought
entries.detail:
Owner report off a phone, 2026-09-01, second one on the same page. components/media/poster-band.tsx baked `w-full` into its base class string; the event page asked for a full bleed with className="-mx-4 w-auto sm:mx-0 sm:w-full". The element rendered carrying BOTH w-full and w-auto, and this repo's `cn` is a plain join with no tailwind-merge, so the winner is Tailwind's emission order rather than source order. w-full won.

THE GEOMETRY IS EXACT: margin-left:-1rem on a width:100% child of a px-4 content box puts the left edge at 0 and the right edge at viewport-2rem. One gutter of bleed on the left, a 34px stripe of page colour on the right. Confirmed against the live rendered markup fetched from production, and the capture's geometry matches - which is how this was diagnosed rather than guessed.

⚠️ THE COMPONENT HAD ALREADY LEARNED THIS AND DID NOT TRANSFER IT. radiusClass is a prop with a comment naming this exact trap ('settled by Tailwind's alphabetical EMISSION order, not by the order you wrote them'). The author protected the radius and left the width in the base string, where the very next caller hit it.

FIXED: width is a prop (widthClass, default w-full so framed callers are untouched); the full-bleed caller passes widthClass="w-auto sm:w-full" and keeps margins in className. The no-cover placeholder had the same defect with no w-auto at all and is fixed too. Four mutations watched go red.

⚪ NOT VISUALLY CONFIRMED: the fix is proven at the markup and geometry layer, not on a re-rendered phone. Worth an owner eye after the deploy.

⚪ THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME CAPTURE is HYG-033 (owner, still open): the tab bar truncates 'Marketpla...'. min-w-0 flex-1 truncate is a deliberate trade against a worse failure, and the obvious rename is foreclosed by NAMING.md - 'Marketplace' != 'Market' name different things.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const b=fs.readFileSync('components/media/poster-band.tsx','utf8');const p=fs.readFileSync('app/(main)/events/[slug]/page.tsx','utf8');const call=p.slice(p.indexOf('<PosterBand'),p.indexOf('radiusClass=\"rounded-none'));process.exit(b.includes('widthClass} overflow-hidden')&&!b.includes('w-full overflow-hidden')&&call.includes('widthClass=\"w-auto sm:w-full\"')&&!/className=\"[^\"]*w-/.test(call)?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence: the band's base class string carries NO w-full (so nothing collides), the component exposes widthClass, and the event page passes its width through that prop with no w-* left in className. Re-baking w-full, or moving the width back into className, fails. components/media/poster-band.test.tsx is the enforcing arm - it parses the rendered class list and asserts exactly one width utility per breakpoint.

source.ref: the phone band contained, so the focal picker had nothing to aim

entries.title: The phone event header letterboxed the poster into two blurred bars, and the focus picker was inert
entries.detail:
Owner report off a phone, 2026-09-04, third on this band: "something got messed up with the mobile header view for events. it should be full bleed and adjusted with the focus picker."

WHAT THE CAPTURE SHOWS. The band was full bleed - LIVE-145 fixed that - but `object-contain` (LIVE-130, then LIVE-131 at every width) fits the artwork INSIDE the box, so on a 412px phone the Meld cover, a 1:1 poster, painted 221x221 in the middle of a 412x221 band: 54% of the width, with a blurred wash either side. The poster was whole and small between two bars, and `object-position` is inert under contain, so the host's focal point - written by the picker in the header controls, whose own hint reads "Vertical matters most" - decided nothing.

FIXED: the band below `sm` covers again, full bleed, at the host's focal point (`object-cover sm:object-contain`). The blurred backdrop moved to `hidden sm:block`, i.e. exactly the width that still letterboxes, which also saves a decode of a second full-size image on the surface least able to afford one.

🔴 WHY THIS DOES NOT REOPEN LIVE-130, and the reason is the band's SHAPE rather than the fit keyword. `object-cover` scales to cover the shorter axis, so it shows the full WIDTH of any source narrower than the band. The band that sliced the Meld title in August was 380x306 (1.24:1). This one is 412x221 full bleed (1.86:1), because the poster ladder cut the phone rung one step. 13 of the 24 production covers are 1:1 and 6 are portrait - Luma and Partiful both tell hosts to upload a square cover - so 19 of 24 now reach both edges WHOLE and lose height instead, aimed by the picker.

⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, stated rather than buried: a source WIDER than 1.86:1 still crops horizontally. The 1400x600 flyer keeps 80% of its width (515 rendered px cropped to 412) against the 53% that produced the August report - better, but not whole. The lever for that case is the height picker, and it points the opposite way from the intuition: SHORT is the widest band (412x170, 2.42:1, wider than every cover in the survey and so horizontally lossless), TALL the narrowest (412x306, 1.35:1). Both are pinned by arithmetic in components/media/poster-band.test.tsx.

⚪ THE DESKTOP HALF IS UNTOUCHED and stays contain: the 1044x374 band is 2.79:1, where a crop showed a median 36% of the artwork across those same 24 covers (LIVE-131). One fit per surface, each chosen on the geometry that surface actually has.

⚪ NOT VISUALLY CONFIRMED on a re-rendered phone - proven at the markup, class and geometry layer, with three mutations watched go red (the fit reverted to contain, the backdrop returned to every width, the objectPosition dropped). Worth an owner eye after the deploy. The follow-up that removes the trade entirely is still to capture the cover's intrinsic aspect in the BROWSER at upload and store it on events.theme beside coverFocus, which makes the band the poster's own shape at both widths; the component is shaped so that is a prop and a class.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=fs.readFileSync('components/media/poster-band.tsx','utf8');const code=s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,'').replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm,'');const h=fs.readFileSync('lib/layout/cover-height.ts','utf8');const phone=h.match(/POSTER_HEIGHT_CLASS[\s\S]*?standard: '([^']+)'/)[1].split(' ')[0];const px=phone.startsWith('h-[')?parseFloat(phone.slice(3))*17:parseInt(phone.slice(2),10)/4*17;process.exit(/object-cover sm:object-contain/.test(code)&&/objectPosition: focus/.test(code)&&/sm:block/.test(code)&&412/px>=1?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the two halves of the owner's sentence against the CODE with comments stripped: the phone band covers while the desktop band contains, the host's focal point is actually rendered onto it (objectPosition from `focus`, which is what 'adjusted with the focus picker' means and what contain made inert), the backdrop is gated to the containing width, and the phone band is at least as wide as it is tall - parsed out of the ladder, so a re-tuned tier that made the band portrait would fail here rather than silently start cropping words off the sides.

entries.title: The row-type/select parity guard now DISCOVERS its pairs through the TypeScript AST, because three different things make the regex lie
entries.detail:
ADR-1181 fixed two instances of 'several selects feed one hand-written row type and a branch forgot a column' and pinned exactly those two. Every other instance in the repo is unguarded.

🔴 THE OBVIOUS GENERAL RULE WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED AND REJECTED - do not re-derive it. 'All selects on the same table in one file must request the same columns' fires on 346 FILES (measured 2026-09-01 across app/ and lib/), and almost every hit is legitimate: a count query and a detail query on one table are supposed to differ. Sample of the noise: admin/actions.ts [profiles] 'omits' auth_user_id/is_system/id/display_name; admin/page.tsx [circles] 'omits' seven columns. A gate with that false-positive rate earns an allowlist and then reads as coverage (ADR-970).

WHAT THE REAL RULE NEEDS: the relation 'this select's result is cast to THAT type'. Divergence is a defect only across branches feeding one type. The pinned guard already resolves it for a named pair by scanning ~400 chars after each select for `as unknown as <Type>`; generalising means walking the TypeScript AST to collect (select -> cast type) edges repo-wide, then grouping. That is a real piece of work, not a regex - hence M.

SECOND HALF, same file: PAIRS is hand-maintained, so a THIRD multi-branch row type added tomorrow is unguarded and nothing says so. The generalised version removes the hand list. Until then the guard asserts each pinned type is still fed by >1 select, so a pin that goes stale fails loudly rather than passing vacuously.

── ✅ CLOSED 2026-09-01. scripts/check-row-type-select-parity.test.ts now walks app/ + lib/ with the TypeScript compiler API and DISCOVERS the (select ⟶ cast) edges; the two hand-listed pairs are gone. Reading: 12 multi-select row types discovered, 0 findings — and both originally-bled pairs are among the 12, correctly attributed (CircleRow with 4 feeding selects, AdminEvent with 2). 3.2s for ~3,100 files, so it rides `pnpm test` rather than needing its own job.

🔴 THE ROW SAID 'that is a real piece of work, not a regex' AND IT WAS RIGHT — MEASURED, not assumed. Generalising the existing 400-character lookahead across app/ + lib/ was tried FIRST and produced 13 failures, at least three of them pure artefact, each a different way text lies about code:
  1. TWO BLOCK-SCOPED TYPES SHARING A NAME. hubs/admin-actions.ts declares `type Row` inside two different functions — {id,name,slug,status,member_count,member_cap,host} in one and {member_count,status} in the other. Name-matching merges them, then reports the second select as 'omitting id, name, slug, member_cap'. nexuses/admin-actions.ts is identical. Only lexical scope resolution separates them.
  2. A LOOKAHEAD CROSSES A Promise.all. event-stats.ts issues three selects on three tables in one array and casts after the last, so `select('status')` on event_rsvps read as TicketRow 'omitting amount_cents, qty'.
  3. select('*') READ AS OMITTING EVERYTHING — five types including ShareRow, VenueHoldRow, CollaborationRow and WalkthroughRow.
The AST version admits an edge only when it can PROVE the flow (the select is syntactically inside the asserted expression, or the asserted expression names a local binding whose initializer contains it), and exempts OPTIONAL (`?`) members: TopicalChannel.pillar_id is declared optional and only the branch that filters on it selects it, so a `?` is the type saying 'may be absent' while a REQUIRED key missing from one branch is the bug.

⚪ WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM. A select whose result reaches its cast through more than one hop is not covered — the guard would rather miss an edge than invent one, which is the opposite of the 346-file rule this row rejected. The corpus floor (≥8 discovered pairs, 12 today) is what notices if discovery ever collapses.

SIX MUTATIONS WATCHED GO RED, each naming what it protects:
  1. reintroduce the real guide-branch omission in admin/circles → RED, naming image_url, city, neighborhood, resonance_public
  2. drop featured_at from load-events' directly-hosted branch (the second real site) → RED
  3. break select discovery → the corpus floor AND the positive control both RED
  4. stop exempting optional keys → RED, and the optional control fires
  5. replace scope resolution with file-wide name matching → RED, reproducing the documented artefact by name: 'hubs/admin-actions.ts :: Row omits id, name, slug, member_cap'
  6. stop special-casing select('*') → RED
⚠️ MUTATION 5 WAS WRONG THE FIRST TIME AND PASSED VACUOUSLY. Scoping resolution to the source file's top level made the detector BLIND rather than file-wide, so the control saw no edges at all and its `toEqual([])` succeeded. A mutation that makes a guard blind does not test the guard — it tests nothing, and it looks identical to a pass. Rewritten to actually perform the regression it names.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('scripts/check-row-type-select-parity.test.ts','utf8');const handrolled=(s.match(/\\{\\s*file:\\s*'[^']+',\\s*type:\\s*'[^']+'\\s*\\}/g)||[]).length;const discovers=/readdirSync|globby|walk\\(/.test(s);process.exit(handrolled===0&&discovers?0:1)"
verify.note:
Measures the CONSEQUENCE the row asks for: that the file/type pairs are DISCOVERED rather than hand-listed. Exits 0 only when zero literal {file,type} pairs remain AND the guard actually walks the tree. `npx vitest run scripts/check-row-type-select-parity.test.ts` is the enforcing arm — 8 tests: the corpus scan, a discovery floor of ≥8 pairs, and six controls.

🔴 THE PREVIOUS PROBE MEASURED A VARIABLE NAME: /const PAIRS = \[/ ? 1 : 0. Renaming PAIRS to PINS, adding a type annotation, or Prettier wrapping the line would each have flipped this OPEN row to done with nothing generalised. A probe that a rename can close is not measuring anything.

entries.title: The public changelog is member-facing copy and check:canon never scanned it, so eight canon violations shipped
entries.detail:
FOUND 2026-09-01 by asking what check:canon does NOT look at, rather than by reading its green output. Its content arm walked content/**/*.md. docs/CHANGELOG.md is not under content/, and docs/HELP-CENTER.md says it 'renders docs/CHANGELOG.md at /help/changelog' - a page every member can read, sitting outside the guard that governs what members read.

WHAT WAS IN THERE once the scope widened: 3 em dashes (a CONTENT-VOICE hard rule), 3 uses of 'broadcasts' as a noun where the canon noun is Dispatch, 4 lowercase 'zaps' and 1 lowercase 'gems'. Eight violations on a live public page - the file the product uses to tell people what changed.

FIXED: the content arm now scans content/**/*.md PLUS a named EXTRA_MEMBER_MD list whose only member is docs/CHANGELOG.md, and all eight violations are corrected in the same change, because a gate wired red is a gate someone disables.

THE SHAPE, and it is this session's third instance: the guard was scoped by DIRECTORY when the rule it enforces is defined by AUDIENCE. ADR-1180 found the same thing one layer down - opengraph-image.tsx is neither a route handler nor a 'use server' file, so check:authz counted none of the 19 of them. Both were invisible precisely because the guard reported success.

Four mutations watched go red, including the meta one: re-adding an em dash, a lowercase zaps, and broadcasts-as-noun each fail, and EMPTYING EXTRA_MEMBER_MD makes the guard go blind again, which is what proves the hole was real rather than theoretical.

verify.cmd: node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('scripts/check-canon.mjs','utf8');process.exit(s.includes('EXTRA_MEMBER_MD')&&/EXTRA_MEMBER_MD = \\[[^\\]]*'docs\\/CHANGELOG.md'/.test(s)&&s.includes('...mfiles') === false&&/for \\(const file of \\[\\.\\.\\.mdFiles\\(ROOT\\), \\.\\.\\.EXTRA_MEMBER_MD\\]\\)/.test(s)?0:1)"
verify.note: Measures the consequence: the canon guard's content arm actually iterates EXTRA_MEMBER_MD alongside content/, and that list still names docs/CHANGELOG.md. Emptying the list or reverting the loop fails. `node scripts/check-canon.mjs` is the enforcing arm and fails on any violation the widened scope now sees.

entries.title: Eight segmented controls and menus nested a 14px radius inside a 24px card, the same mismatch the RSVP picker had
entries.detail:
Found while fixing the RSVP picker's corners. The repo's radius ladder is authored BY ROLE (docs/DESIGN.md: control = 14px, card = 24px), which is right for siblings and wrong for NESTING — two corners share a centre only when the inner radius is the outer minus the gap. A `rounded-control` (14px) child inside a `rounded-card` (24px) box with `p-1` between them reads 5.75px too square, because `p-1` is 4.25px at this app's 17px root (--density-root 106.25%).

`--radius-control-nested` (app/globals.css, `calc(var(--radius-card) - 0.25rem)` so it tracks both the skin's radius and the generation's density) now carries it, and eight surfaces use it: components/events/rsvp-controls.tsx, components/quest/board-controls.tsx (scope + track), app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/airwaves/airwaves-console.tsx, app/(main)/connections/new/creator.tsx, app/(main)/events/events-sort.tsx, components/spaces/spaces-sort.tsx, components/ui/facet-dropdown.tsx and components/ui/underline-tabs.tsx.

⚠️ THE ROW'S FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and it is the useful part of this entry. It was `grep-absent 'rounded-control px-3 py-1.5'` over three files — a string that also matches three SIBLING controls (a dropdown's trigger button, the leaderboard's hide-me toggle) that are correct at 14px, so satisfying the probe would have meant breaking them, while the four menu surfaces it named none of stayed broken. Nesting is the claim, so nesting is what is now measured: scripts/check-nested-radius.mjs walks app/ and components/ for a container carrying both `rounded-card` and `p-1` with a bare `rounded-control` in its subtree.

🔴 That detector printed a clean ✓ on its first run and was more than half blind: a mutation sweep reintroducing the defect at each of the 15 fixed sites showed EIGHT walking past it (a multi-line JSX tag closes its own `>` at the opening tag's indent, so the subtree window ended before any child). Fixed, plus a second arm that follows a capitalised child into a same-file helper component. The sweep is now scripts/check-nested-radius.test.ts (18 tests), and the guard is registered in VITEST_ENFORCED so vitest auto-discovery keeps it running rather than an array in ci.yml.

verify.cmd: node scripts/check-nested-radius.mjs
verify.note: Fails when a bare `rounded-control` appears inside a `rounded-card` + `p-1` container. A helper imported from ANOTHER module is the declared blind spot (resolveLocalComponent says so in its own doc comment); scripts/check-nested-radius.test.ts drives every arm against fixtures that must fail, and asserts a floor on the denominator so an empty walk cannot read as compliance.

entries.title: `truncate` on an inline <Link> drops the ellipsis and keeps white-space:nowrap (found while chasing the Space console overflow, which it does NOT fix)
entries.detail:
🔴 AMENDED 2026-09-01, BEFORE MERGE: this row was written claiming the defect CAUSED the /spaces/<slug>/manage overflow. It does not. With the fix live on #2328's preview the offending box still measures `x 17→447, width 430` at 320/360/390px — identical to the pre-fix reading. The overflow is unfixed and is now HYG-037. What this row still closes is the defect itself, which is real: on a non-replaced inline box `overflow`/`text-overflow` do not apply, so an inline <a class="truncate"> gets no ellipsis and keeps nowrap. Six were fixed and a guard prevents more. Read the rest as the mechanism, not the diagnosis.

Caught by test/e2e/overflow.spec.ts, not by review: /spaces/<slug>/manage ran 57px past a 390px viewport in TWO <section>s at once, on a shell root carrying overflow-x-clip — so nothing scrolled and the dashboard was cut off.

Both sections reported the SAME width because they are the two items of one single-column grid, and a grid track is sized by the widest item's min-content. Tailwind's `truncate` is overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis + white-space:nowrap; the first two do NOT apply to a non-replaced inline box, and <Link> renders an inline <a>.
